row.title: Normal density states and spectral moments

items.title: Trace-class normal density states
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement:
Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, with inner product linear in its first argument. An operator $\rho\in\mathcal B(H)$ is a **density operator** when it is positive, trace class, and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. Here trace class means compact with summable singular values, and $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the basis-independent trace of a trace-class operator.

The **normal density state represented by $\rho$** is the functional on bounded operators
$
\omega_\rho(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A),\qquad A\in\mathcal B(H).
$
In this page, “normal density state” means this specified trace-pairing representation; no equivalence with other definitions of normal functionals is assumed. The trace pairing is used only for bounded $A$. Unbounded observables are treated through their spectral probability measures in [[lem-qsm-trace-state-calculus]].

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.3, author-hosted manuscript
Mehran Kardar, Statistical Mechanics I, MIT OpenCourseWare, Lecture 21, Quantum Microstates and Quantum Macrostates

items.title: Finite matrix spectral and state calculus
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement:
Use the following conventions on a complex inner-product space $H$ of dimension $D\geq1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. For an endomorphism $A$, define $\operatorname{Tr}A:=\sum_{j=1}^D\langle Ae_j,e_j\rangle$ in an orthonormal basis; step 3.1 proves basis independence. For any Hermitian $M$, its **positive spectral subspace** (called its positive support here) is $S_M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda>0}\ker(M-\lambda I)$; when $M\geq0$ this equals $(\ker M)^\perp$. Its support logarithm is $\log(M|_{S_M}):=\sum_{\lambda>0}(\log\lambda)P_\lambda|_{S_M}$, where $P_\lambda$ is the orthogonal projection onto that eigenspace. No value $\log0$ is assigned; for $M=0$ this is the unique endomorphism of the zero space. For the set $\mathcal D(H)$ of positive semidefinite Hermitian endomorphisms with trace one, a point $\rho$ is **extreme** if every equality $\rho=t\sigma+(1-t)\tau$ with $\sigma,\tau\in\mathcal D(H)$ and $0<t<1$ implies $\sigma=\tau=\rho$.

Let $H$ be a complex inner-product space of finite dimension $D\geq1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. Every Hermitian endomorphism $M$ has an orthonormal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues. For a real function $f$ on its finite spectrum, define $f(M)$ by its spectral projections; this definition is independent of the choice of eigenbasis. In particular positive square roots, exponentials, and logarithms on positive supports are well defined.

For a density matrix $\rho$ on $H$, meaning a Hermitian positive semidefinite operator with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)=\sum_jp_j\langle Au_j,u_j\rangle$ for bounded $A$, where $\rho=\sum_jp_j|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|$. The weighted form $(X,Y)_\rho=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho X^*Y)$ satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz, $|(X,Y)_\rho|^2\leq(X,X)_\rho(Y,Y)_\rho$. Finally, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^2)\leq1$, with equality exactly for rank-one densities, and those are exactly the extreme points of the finite density-matrix set.

items.title: Finite matrix C-star algebra and density-state duality

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.3
Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §§2.3–2.4

items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, $D=\dim H\ge1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. With composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity and the induced operator norm, $\mathcal B(H)$ is a nonzero unital complex C*-algebra in the sense of [[def-c-star-algebra]]. In particular it is complete, $\|AB\|\le\|A\|\|B\|$, $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$, $\|A^*\|=\|A\|$ and $\|I\|=1$. The matrix $\|A\|^2I-A^*A$ is positive semidefinite and has a positive square root in $\mathcal B(H)$.

Every complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal B(H)\to\mathbb C$ that is positive, meaning $\omega(B^*B)\ge0$ for all $B$, has a unique positive semidefinite matrix $\rho$ such that $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ for all $A$. It is bounded and satisfies

$$|\omega(A)|\le\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)\|A\|\quad(A\in\mathcal B(H)),\qquad \|\omega\|=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)=\omega(I).$$

Consequently the canonical states of [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]] are exactly the trace pairings of density operators of [[def-qc-density-operator]]; for a positive functional, normalization $\omega(I)=1$ is equivalent to norm one. The result includes zero positive functionals, nonfaithful densities and $D=1$; it makes no infinite-dimensional density representation assertion.

items.title: Finite Gibbs density and its canonical purification
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension $d\geq1$, $K=K^*$ an endomorphism, and $\beta>0$. Define $Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta K})$ and $\rho_\beta=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta K}$. Given an ordered orthonormal basis $(e_j)_{j=1}^d$ and its identified copy in a reference space $\mathcal H_R$, define
$
|\Phi_d\rangle=d^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^d e_j\otimes e_j,\qquad
|\Psi_\beta\rangle=\sqrt{d/Z_\beta}(e^{-\beta K/2}\otimes I_R)|\Phi_d\rangle.
$
Then $Z_\beta>0$, $\rho_\beta$ is a density operator, $|\Psi_\beta\rangle$ is a unit vector, and $\operatorname{Tr}_R(|\Psi_\beta\rangle\langle\Psi_\beta|)=\rho_\beta$. If $K$ is interpreted as energy, the product $\beta K$ is dimensionless.

items.title: Duhamel derivative and finite Kubo–Mori response
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement:
The path convention is $D\geq1$, an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, and a continuously differentiable map $M:I\to\operatorname{Herm}(D)$, where $\operatorname{Herm}(D)$ is the real vector space of Hermitian $D\times D$ matrices. For the control convention, $m\geq1$, $\theta\in\mathbb R^m$, and $M(\theta)=M_0+\sum_{a=1}^m\theta_aX_a$ with Hermitian matrices $M_0,X_1,\ldots,X_m$. At each control value let $Z=\operatorname{Tr}e^M$ and $\rho=e^M/Z$. For Hermitian $X$, define
$$\langle X\rangle_\rho:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho X),\qquad \operatorname{Var}_\rho(X):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho(X-\langle X\rangle_\rho I)^2).$$
For Hermitian $X,Y$, put $\delta X:=X-\langle X\rangle_\rho I$ and $\delta Y:=Y-\langle Y\rangle_\rho I$, and define the Kubo--Mori covariance by
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{KM,\rho}(X,Y):=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^{1-u}\delta X\rho^u\delta Y)\,du.$$
For the static-control clause, take $H_0,B\in\operatorname{Herm}(D)$, $h\in\mathbb R$, $\beta>0$, and $H(h):=H_0-hB$.

Let $M(s)$ be a continuously differentiable path of Hermitian $D\times D$ matrices, $D\geq1$. Then
$
\frac{d}{ds}e^{M(s)}=\int_0^1 e^{(1-u)M(s)}M'(s)e^{uM(s)}\,du,\qquad
\frac{d}{ds}\log\operatorname{Tr}e^{M(s)}=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_sM'(s)),
$
where $\rho_s=e^{M(s)}/\operatorname{Tr}e^{M(s)}$. For real controls $M(\theta)=M_0+\sum_a\theta_aX_a$ with Hermitian $X_a$,
$
\partial_a\log Z=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho X_a),\qquad
\partial_a\partial_b\log Z=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^{1-u}\delta X_a\rho^u\delta X_b)\,du,
$
where $Z=\operatorname{Tr}e^M$, $\delta X_a=X_a-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho X_a)I$. The diagonal quadratic form of this Hessian is nonnegative. It equals the ordinary variance when $X_a$ commutes with $\rho$, and in general is bounded above by that variance. For $H(h)=H_0-hB$, $\beta>0$, and Hermitian $B$, the static susceptibility satisfies $\partial_h\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_hB)=\beta\,\operatorname{Cov}_{KM,\rho_h}(B,B)\geq0$. No infinite-dimensional or dynamical response is asserted.

More precisely, for every positive definite $\rho=e^M/\operatorname{Tr}e^M$ and Hermitian $X$, equality between the diagonal Kubo--Mori quadratic form and $\operatorname{Var}_\rho(X)$ holds if and only if $X\rho=\rho X$.
$
\frac{d}{dh}\langle B\rangle_{\rho_h}=\beta\,\operatorname{Cov}_{KM,\rho_h}(B,B)\geq0,
\qquad \rho_h:=\frac{e^{-\beta H(h)}}{\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H(h)}}.
$
No infinite-dimensional or dynamical response is asserted.

items.title: Trace-state cyclicity and spectral probability calculus
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement:
For a nonnegative countably additive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R$ with $\mu(\mathbb R)=1$, define
$$m(\mu):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu(\lambda)$$
when $\int|\lambda|\,d\mu(\lambda)<\infty$. If $\int\lambda^2\,d\mu(\lambda)<\infty$, then $|\lambda|\le(1+\lambda^2)/2$ makes the first absolute moment finite, and define
$$V(\mu):=\int_{\mathbb R}(\lambda-m(\mu))^2\,d\mu(\lambda)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,d\mu(\lambda)-m(\mu)^2.$$
Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space and $\rho$ a trace-class normal density state. Its positive eigenvalues $p_j$ and orthonormal eigenvectors $u_j$ satisfy $\rho=\sum_jp_j|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|$ in trace norm and $\sum_jp_j=1$. For bounded $A$, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)=\sum_jp_j\langle Au_j,u_j\rangle$, with absolute value at most $\|A\|$, and $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)=\operatorname{Tr}(A\rho)$. For a self-adjoint observable $A$ with spectral PVM $E_A$, the scalar law
$
\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho E_A(B))=\sum_jp_j\|E_A(B)u_j\|^2
$
is a probability measure. Its first absolute moment defines a scalar mean, and its second moment defines a variance; these are not defined as arbitrary unbounded products $\rho A$. For a fixed positive Boltzmann scale $k_B>0$ (in SI units J/K), the von Neumann entropy is $S(\rho)=-k_B\sum_jp_j\log p_j\in[0,\infty]$, and need not be finite. Countable convex mixtures of normal density states converge in trace norm.

For this spectral law, the notations are $m_\rho(A):=m(\mu_\rho)$ and $\operatorname{Var}_\rho(A):=V(\mu_\rho)$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.3, author-hosted manuscript

items.title: Normal-state quantum measurement interpretation
items.design_state: draft-research
items.physical_scope: Adopted Hilbert-space Born interpretation for trace-class normal density states and their self-adjoint spectral measurements; nonnormal algebraic states and empirical apparatus claims are outside scope.
items.statement:
Adopt the following measurement interpretation for this nonrelativistic quantum-statistical model. A prepared normal state is a trace-class density operator $\rho$ on a specified separable complex Hilbert space $H$. A sharp measurement of a self-adjoint observable $A$, with spectral PVM $E_A$, assigns probability
$
\mathbb P_\rho\{A\in C\}=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho E_A(C))
$
to each Borel outcome set $C\subseteq\mathbb R$. Finite projective measurements use the same rule with their orthogonal projections. This adopts a physical probability interpretation for the mathematical state law proved in [[lem-qsm-trace-state-calculus]]; it does not derive the Born rule, assert that an apparatus realizes a specified PVM, or report experimental outcomes. Infinite algebraic states not represented by trace-class density operators are not included.

The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the unbounded spectral theorem and its spectral-calculus supplier closure. Its strength is retained in the mathematical dependencies. The scalar probability and bounded cyclicity clauses now use the exact canonical suppliers cited by [[lem-qsm-trace-state-calculus]]; this source adoption supplies no native readiness or empirical validation, and implies no weaker foundation.

items.title: Sparse-oracle finite Gibbs purification procedure
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement:
**Input:** a nonzero finite-dimensional Hilbert space of dimension $d$, a Hermitian Hamiltonian matrix $K$, an inverse-energy parameter $\beta>0$ such that $H=\beta K$ is dimensionless, the ordered reference preparation $|\Phi_d\rangle$ from [[def-qsm-finite-gibbs-purification]], an output vector-error tolerance $\varepsilon_{\rm out}>0$, and a rational amplification-failure target $0<\rho<1$. The input contract must also supply a rational shift-confidence target $0<\delta_{\rm sh}<1$, a finite call cap $Q_{\rm cap}$, and rational sampler precision $0<\nu\leq\delta_{\rm sh}^2/(10^{12}d(Q_{\rm cap}+1)^2)$ as required by [[lem-qa-30-spectral-minimum-shift]], as well as every sparse-oracle, block-encoding, controlled-evolution, inverse, norm-bound, energy-shift, coefficient-generation, implementation-error budget, synthesis-precision, reference-preparation, and cost object required by [[alg-qa-30-sdp-gibbs-purification]]. No matrix exponential, trace, exact spectral minimum, or gate is free input.

**Procedure:** invoke the normalized-output branch of [[alg-qa-30-sdp-gibbs-purification]] on $K$ with coefficient $\eta=\beta$, the stated vector-error and amplification-failure targets, the supplied shift-confidence target $\delta_{\rm sh}$, and complete access/cost certificates. Retain its frozen energy shift and all declared finite subroutines. Measure only its specified good/bad flag. On a good branch return the normalized system-reference vector; on a cap failure return the explicit output FAIL. If the certified shift event fails, do not assert the Gibbs approximation guarantee; any overall failure probability includes the supplied $\delta_{\rm sh}$ shift-confidence budget.

**Output:** either FAIL, or a normalized vector-register state in the successful branch, with the error and success guarantees supplied by [[thm-qa-30-sdp-gibbs-state-error-cost]]. An identity energy shift changes neither the normalized Gibbs density nor its canonical purification, since $e^{-(\beta K+cI)}=e^{-c}e^{-\beta K}$ and the trace is multiplied by the same scalar. This is a mathematical state-preparation procedure under the stated finite access model; it is not a physical bath or thermalization process.

references.title: Joran van Apeldoorn, András Gilyén, Sander Gribling, and Ronald de Wolf, Quantum SDP-Solvers, arXiv:1705.01843v4
András Gilyén, Yuan Su, Guang Hao Low, and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum singular value transformation and beyond, arXiv:1806.01838

items.title: Quantum spectral entropy and relative-entropy domains
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement:
For a trace-class density $\rho$ on a Hilbert space $H$, define its support subspace in either finite or infinite dimension by
$$\operatorname{supp}\rho:=(\ker\rho)^\perp,\qquad \ker\rho:=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}.$$
It is closed; write $P_\rho$ for its orthogonal projection, whose existence and uniqueness follow from [[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]].

Fix the positive Boltzmann scale $k_B>0$ (in SI units J/K, as in the approved QSM quantities design and [[lem-qsm-trace-state-calculus]]). For a trace-class density $\rho$ with positive eigenvalues $p_i$, define $S(\rho)=-k_B\sum_i p_i\log p_i\in[0,\infty]$, with $0\log0=0$. The logarithm is natural and acts on dimensionless density eigenvalues.

For finite-dimensional densities $\rho,\sigma$, define $\operatorname{supp}\rho=(\ker\rho)^\perp$. If $\operatorname{supp}\rho\not\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\sigma$, set $D(\rho\|\sigma)=+\infty$. Otherwise define
$
D(\rho\|\sigma)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\sigma),
$
where each logarithm is restricted to the positive support of its operator and zero eigenvalues contribute zero to $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)$.

For trace-class normal densities on a separable Hilbert space, write $\rho=\sum_i p_i|u_i\rangle\langle u_i|$ and $\sigma=\sum_j s_j|v_j\rangle\langle v_j|$ on their positive supports. Define the nonnegative cross-log moment
$
C(\rho,\sigma):=\sum_{i,j}p_i(-\log s_j)|\langle u_i,v_j\rangle|^2\in[0,\infty].
$
This is the spectral first moment of $-\log\sigma$ in the scalar state law of $\rho$; equivalently it is the nonnegative sum over the spectral projections, so it is independent of bases within eigenspaces. When support inclusion holds and $C(\rho,\sigma)$ and $S(\rho)$ are both finite, define $D(\rho\|\sigma)=C(\rho,\sigma)-S(\rho)/k_B$. If $C=+\infty$ and $S(\rho)<\infty$, set $D=+\infty$. No value is assigned by this definition to $+\infty-(+\infty)$; [[thm-qsm-trace-cross-log-inequality]] proves that finite $C$ forces finite $S(\rho)$.

The spectral-moment identification in the preceding cross-log clause is restricted to $\operatorname{supp}\rho\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\sigma$, so that the state is supported on the space where $-\log\sigma$ acts. Outside that domain, $C$ denotes only the displayed nonnegative double sum.

items.title: Finite unitary dynamics and Gibbs KMS identity
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $H=H^*$ be a Hamiltonian on $\mathcal H$ with energy unit J; let $\hbar>0$ have unit J s. For real $t$ measured in seconds, $U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ is unitary and $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$. For a trace-one density $\rho$ on $\mathcal H$, the Schrödinger state $U(t)\rho U(t)^*$ and the Heisenberg observable $\alpha_t(A)=U(t)^*AU(t)$ have the same trace expectation. Fix $k_B>0$ in J/K for the entropy convention; then the von Neumann entropy is unchanged. If $d=\dim\mathcal H\geq1$, $\beta>0$ has unit J$^{-1}$, and $\sigma_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z_\beta$ with $Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H}$, then it is stationary and satisfies the finite Gibbs KMS strip identity
$
F_{A,B}(t+i\beta\hbar)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta\alpha_t(B)A),\qquad
F_{A,B}(z)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta A\alpha_z(B)),
$
where $\alpha_z(B)=e^{izH/\hbar}Be^{-izH/\hbar}$, with complexified time $z$ measured in seconds. The function is entire and bounded on $0\leq\operatorname{Im}z\leq\beta\hbar$ seconds. No infinite-volume KMS existence or approach to equilibrium follows.

references.title: Alain Connes and Matilde Marcolli, Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, §2.2, “The KMS condition”
references.locator: Complete 705-page author-hosted book; Chapter 3, §2.2, printed pp. 407–408 (PDF pp. 406–408), Definition 3.6 and equation (3.11); also §2.1, pp. 404–406, for finite Gibbs states and time evolution.

items.title: Finite Gibbs free-energy and entropy optimization
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement:
Let $H=H^*$ act on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension $d\geq1$, $\beta>0$, $k_B>0$, $T=(k_B\beta)^{-1}$, and $Z=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})$. Put $\sigma=e^{-\beta H}/Z$, $F_\beta=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$, and $S(\rho)=-k_B\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)$, with $0\log0=0$. Then every density matrix $\rho$, including rank-deficient matrices, satisfies
$
\operatorname{Tr}(\rho H)-TS(\rho)\geq F_\beta,
$
with equality if and only if $\rho=\sigma$. Moreover $S(\sigma)=k_B(\log Z+\beta\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma H))$, so $F_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma H)-TS(\sigma)$. This is finite-dimensional mathematical optimization; actual preparation is a separate postulate.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 5, §§5.1–5.2, author-hosted manuscript
Mehran Kardar, Statistical Mechanics I, MIT OpenCourseWare, Lecture 21, Quantum Microstates and Quantum Macrostates

items.title: Finite Gibbs circuit marginal and trace-distance error
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement:
Assume the finite access and successful shift conditions of [[alg-qsm-finite-gibbs-state-preparation]]. Let $|\Psi_\beta\rangle$ be the normalized canonical purification of [[def-qsm-finite-gibbs-purification]], and suppose the successful normalized output $|\widetilde\Psi_\beta\rangle$ has vector distance at most $\varepsilon_{\rm out}$ from $|\Psi_\beta\rangle$, up to a global phase, as supplied by [[thm-qa-30-sdp-gibbs-state-error-cost]]. Then
$
D\!\left(\operatorname{Tr}_R|\widetilde\Psi_\beta\rangle\langle\widetilde\Psi_\beta|,\rho_\beta\right)\leq\varepsilon_{\rm out},
$
where $D(\rho,\sigma)=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$. The assertion is conditional on the algorithmic success events and says nothing about physical thermalization or finite measurement frequencies.

items.title: Trace-class cross-log entropy inequality
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement: Fix the positive Boltzmann scale $k_B>0$ of [[def-qsm-relative-entropy-domain]] (in SI units J/K). Let $\rho,\sigma$ be trace-class normal densities on a separable complex Hilbert space, with $\operatorname{supp}\rho\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\sigma$. Define $C(\rho,\sigma)$ and $D(\rho\|\sigma)$ as in [[def-qsm-relative-entropy-domain]]. If $C(\rho,\sigma)<\infty$, then $S(\rho)<\infty$, $D(\rho\|\sigma)=C(\rho,\sigma)-S(\rho)/k_B\geq0$, and equality holds exactly when $\rho=\sigma$. This restricted cross-log domain makes no assertion about an undefined $\infty-\infty$ difference.

items.title: Finite mixing, product entropy, and bipartite subadditivity
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement:
For $m\geq1$ density matrices $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_m$ on one finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and weights $t_a\geq0$ with $\sum_at_a=1$, define their mixture $\rho:=\sum_at_a\rho_a$. The exact content of entropy concavity under finite mixing is
$$S(\rho)\geq\sum_{a=1}^m t_aS(\rho_a).$$
For density matrices $\rho,\sigma$ on finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, the exact content of product additivity is $S(\rho\otimes\sigma)=S(\rho)+S(\sigma)$.

For the positive entropy scale $k_B>0$ fixed in [[def-qsm-relative-entropy-domain]] (in SI units J/K), entropy is concave under finite mixing and additive on product states for finite-dimensional density matrices. If $R$ is a density matrix on $H_A\otimes H_B$, with marginals $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B R$, $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A R$, then
$
S(R)\leq S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B),
$
with equality exactly when $R=\rho_A\otimes\rho_B$. These finite statements include rank-deficient densities and assert neither strong subadditivity nor general infinite-dimensional data processing.

items.title: Self-adjoint trace-Gibbs normalization and form-energy optimization
items.design_state: draft-research
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space and $A=A^*$ a densely defined Hamiltonian bounded below by $a\in\mathbb R$. Assume $e^{-\beta A}$ is trace class for every $\beta$ in an open interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$. For each $\beta\in I$, put $Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta A})$ and $\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta A}/Z_\beta$. Then $Z_\beta\in(0,\infty)$ and $\rho_\beta$ is a faithful normal density. For the entropy and optimization clause, fix $k_B>0$ (in SI units J/K), put $T=(k_B\beta)^{-1}$ and $F_\beta=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_\beta$, and let $\rho$ be any normal density with finite spectral form energy
$
\mathcal E_A(\rho)=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu_\rho(\lambda),\qquad
\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu_\rho(\lambda)<\infty.
$
Then $\rho$ has finite entropy and satisfies
$
\mathcal E_A(\rho)-TS(\rho)\geq F_\beta,
$
with equality exactly at $\rho=\rho_\beta$. The prepared Gibbs state also has
$
S(\rho_\beta)=k_B\bigl(\log Z_\beta+\beta\mathcal E_A(\rho_\beta)\bigr).
$
The trace-class and open-interval hypotheses are essential; a lower bound on $A$ alone does not imply finite $Z_\beta$.

items.title: Energy-band and grand quantum preparations
items.design_state: draft-research
items.physical_scope: Adopted finite-rank energy-band or commuting grand-canonical preparation for a nonzero model under the stated spectral, trace, and joint-moment conditions; infinite-rank band normalization and noncommuting energy-number ensembles are excluded.
items.statement:
Fix the positive Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in J/K and adopt two preparation rules within the normal-state model of [[post-qsm-normal-measurement-state]].

**Energy-band preparation.** Let $H=H^*$ have spectral PVM $E_H$, and let $P=E_H(B)$ be a nonzero finite-rank projection for a specified Borel energy band $B\subseteq\mathbb R$. When the model declares preparation in this band without additional constraints, adopt the density $\rho=P/\operatorname{Tr}P$. This is a uniform preparation over the finite-dimensional range of $P$; it is not asserted for infinite-rank projections.

**Grand preparation.** Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space with a specified nonempty finite or countably infinite orthonormal basis $(u_j)_{j\in J}$, so its finite linear span is dense in $\mathcal H$. For each $\psi=\sum_{j\in J}c_ju_j\in\mathcal H$, define the diagonal self-adjoint energy and particle-number operators by
$$D(H)=\left\{\psi:\sum_j|E_jc_j|^2<\infty\right\},\quad H\psi=\sum_jE_jc_ju_j;\qquad D(N)=\left\{\psi:\sum_j|n_jc_j|^2<\infty\right\},\quad N\psi=\sum_jn_jc_ju_j,$$
where $E_j\in\mathbb R$ and $n_j\in\mathbb N_0$. For chemical potential $\mu\in\mathbb R$, define the diagonal sum $K_\mu=H-\mu N$ by
$$D(K_\mu)=\left\{\psi:\sum_j|(E_j-\mu n_j)c_j|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad K_\mu\psi=\sum_j(E_j-\mu n_j)c_ju_j.$$
This specifies the self-adjoint operator sum used in this postulate; on $D(H)\cap D(N)$ it agrees with the algebraic difference. Require $\inf_j(E_j-\mu n_j)>-\infty$. Fix $\beta>0$ in J$^{-1}$ and assume
$
0<\Xi(\beta,\mu)=\sum_{j\in J} e^{-\beta(E_j-\mu n_j)}<\infty.
$
Adopt the normal density $\rho_{\beta,\mu}=\Xi^{-1}e^{-\beta K_\mu}$. For response claims, also require the uniform joint-moment envelopes in [[thm-tdmath-grand-response-covariance]]. Here $E_j,\mu$ are in J, $n_j$ is dimensionless, $\beta=1/(k_BT)$ is in J$^{-1}$, and $\Xi$ is dimensionless.

These are adopted preparation assumptions, not consequences that a physical system is actually prepared in these states. They do not assert dynamical thermalization, an infinite-rank microcanonical state, or a grand ensemble for noncommuting $H,N$. The mathematical variational results to which they refer do not prove the physical postulate.

The self-adjointness assertions above are mathematical properties of the specified maximal diagonal domains. For a real sequence $(a_j)_{j\in J}$, let $M_a\psi=\sum_j a_jc_ju_j$ on $D(M_a)=\{\psi:\sum_j|a_jc_j|^2<\infty\}$. This domain contains the dense finite linear span. By definition, $\phi\in D(M_a^*)$ exactly when some $\eta\in\mathcal H$ satisfies $\langle M_a\psi,\phi\rangle=\langle\psi,\eta\rangle$ for every $\psi\in D(M_a)$, and then $M_a^*\phi=\eta$. Testing $\psi=u_j$ gives $\eta_j=a_j\phi_j$; hence $\eta\in\mathcal H$ forces $\sum_j|a_j\phi_j|^2<\infty$, so $\phi\in D(M_a)$. Conversely, if $\phi\in D(M_a)$, then for every $\psi\in D(M_a)$ the two inner products converge by Cauchy–Schwarz and satisfy $\langle M_a\psi,\phi\rangle=\langle\psi,M_a\phi\rangle$, since every $a_j$ is real. Thus $D(M_a^*)=D(M_a)$ and $M_a^*=M_a$. This applies to $a_j=E_j$, $a_j=n_j$, and $a_j=E_j-\mu n_j$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.3, author-hosted manuscript
Mehran Kardar, Statistical Mechanics I, MIT OpenCourseWare, Lecture 23, Canonical and Grand Canonical Formulations

items.title: Canonical quantum thermal preparation
items.design_state: draft-research
items.physical_scope: Adopted nonzero finite-dimensional or trace-class canonical Gibbs preparation at positive temperature under the exact trace and moment hypotheses; no bath dynamics, thermalization, or experimental claim is asserted.
items.statement:
Adopt canonical preparation as follows. Fix the positive Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in J/K. Let $H=H^*$ act on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension $d\geq1$, or be self-adjoint on a nonzero separable Hilbert space, bounded below and satisfying $e^{-\beta H}\in\mathcal S_1$ for $\beta$ in an open interval about the chosen value. For temperature $T>0$, put $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ and adopt
$
\rho_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta H}}{Z_\beta},\qquad Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H}).
$
In the infinite-dimensional case all scalar energy moments used in a conclusion must also be finite on the actual spectral domain, as required by [[thm-qsm-trace-gibbs-variational]]. With $H$ in joules, $k_B$ in J/K, $T$ in K, and $\beta$ in J$^{-1}$, the exponent is dimensionless and $Z_\beta$ is a dimensionless trace.

This is an adopted preparation rule in the normal-state framework. It is not a theorem that unitary dynamics equilibrates, does not specify a bath or equilibration time, and makes no empirical claim. The finite and trace-Gibbs variational results describe the mathematical optimization associated with this state but do not establish that a physical system is prepared in it.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 5, §5.2, author-hosted manuscript
Mehran Kardar, Statistical Mechanics I, MIT OpenCourseWare, Lecture 21, Quantum Microstates and Quantum Macrostates

items.title: Commuting quantum grand responses
items.design_state: draft-research
items.physical_scope: Conditional grand-canonical model for self-adjoint energy and nonnegative-integer number operators on a nonzero model with a nonempty common eigenbasis and local joint-moment envelope; noncommuting energy-number ensembles and experimental claims are excluded.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$, and let $H$ and $N$ be the diagonal self-adjoint energy and dimensionless particle-number operators with the domains specified by [[post-qsm-band-and-grand-preparation]] and common nonempty finite or countably infinite orthonormal eigenbasis $(u_j)_{j\in J}$ satisfying $Hu_j=E_ju_j$, $Nu_j=n_ju_j$, and $n_j\in\mathbb N_0$. Let $\beta>0$ have units J$^{-1}$, let $\mu$ have units J, and let $(\beta,\mu)$ vary in an open parameter set $U$ where
$
0<\Xi(\beta,\mu)=\sum_{j\in J}e^{-\beta(E_j-\mu n_j)}<\infty.
$
On every compact subset of $U$, assume a summable envelope dominates
$
e^{-\beta(E_j-\mu n_j)}(1+|E_j|^2+|n_j|^2)
$
uniformly in $j,\beta,\mu$. Under the commuting grand preparation of [[post-qsm-band-and-grand-preparation]], set $p_j=e^{-\beta(E_j-\mu n_j)}/\Xi$ and write $\langle X\rangle=\sum_jp_jX_j$. Then, with the scalar-law variance defined by $\operatorname{Var}(N):=\sum_jp_j(n_j-\langle N\rangle)^2$,
$
\partial_\mu\log\Xi=\beta\langle N\rangle,\qquad
\partial_\mu\langle N\rangle=\beta\operatorname{Var}(N)\geq0,
\qquad
-\partial_\beta\log\Xi\big|_\mu=\langle H-\mu N\rangle.
$
In the natural parameters $(\theta_E,\theta_N)=(-\beta,\beta\mu)$, the Hessian of $\log\Xi$ is the covariance matrix of $(H,N)$, hence positive semidefinite. This result is conditional on the common eigenbasis and envelope; it does not cover noncommuting $H,N$, assert thermalization, or report measurements.

references.title: Mehran Kardar, Statistical Mechanics I, MIT OpenCourseWare, Lecture 23, Canonical and Grand Canonical Formulations
J. W. Gibbs, Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics, Chapter IV, The Canonical Distribution

items.title: Unitary entropy and Gibbs equilibrium identities
items.design_state: draft-research
items.physical_scope: Normal-state unitary model predictions and nonzero finite-dimensional canonical stationarity/KMS identity; real time is measured in seconds, and no irreversible relaxation, infinite-volume KMS theorem, or apparatus claim is made.
items.statement:
Assume the normal-state and canonical-preparation interpretations of [[post-qsm-normal-measurement-state]] and [[post-qsm-thermal-gibbs-preparation]], and fix the positive entropy scale $k_B>0$ in J/K. Model an isolated system on a separable complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ by the unitary evolution $U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ for real time $t$ measured in seconds, where the self-adjoint Hamiltonian $H=H^*$ has energy units J and $\hbar>0$ has action units J s. For every trace-class normal density $\rho$ on $\mathcal H$, the evolved state $U(t)\rho U(t)^*$ is a normal density and has the same von Neumann entropy, including when that entropy is $+\infty$. For the finite canonical/KMS clause, require $d=\dim\mathcal H\geq1$ and inverse-energy parameter $\beta>0$ in J$^{-1}$; then the canonical density $\sigma_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z_\beta$ is stationary under this evolution and obeys the finite Gibbs KMS strip identity
$
F_{A,B}(t+i\beta\hbar)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta\alpha_t(B)A),\qquad
F_{A,B}(z)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta A\alpha_z(B)),\quad
\alpha_z(B)=e^{izH/\hbar}Be^{-izH/\hbar},
$
for bounded matrices $A,B$, with complexified time $z$ measured in seconds. These are deductions inside the specified model; they do not imply equilibration, entropy increase, or infinite-volume KMS existence.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.3, author-hosted manuscript
Alain Connes and Matilde Marcolli, Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, §2.2, “The KMS condition”
references.locator: Complete author-hosted book; Chapter 3, §§2.1–2.2, printed pp. 404–408, especially Definition 3.6 and equation (3.11).

items.title: Gibbs energy, entropy and potential identities
items.design_state: draft-research
items.physical_scope: Canonical preparation identities for finite Hamiltonians or trace-class self-adjoint Gibbs operators with finite form energy; adopted thermodynamic identification only, with no empirical claim.
items.statement:
Under the adopted canonical preparation [[post-qsm-thermal-gibbs-preparation]], let $k_B>0$ and $\beta=1/(k_BT)>0$, with $\beta$ in J$^{-1}$, $H$ in J, $T$ in K, $k_B$ in J/K, entropy in J/K, and free energy in J. In a finite-dimensional model on a Hilbert space of dimension $d\geq1$, for $\sigma=e^{-\beta H}/Z_\beta$, $U=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma H)$, and $F_\beta=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_\beta$,
$
S(\sigma)=k_B(\log Z_\beta+\beta U),\qquad F_\beta=U-TS(\sigma).
$
The same identities hold for a self-adjoint Hamiltonian bounded below when its Gibbs exponential is trace class on an open positive-$\beta$ interval and the state has the finite form energy required by [[thm-qsm-trace-gibbs-variational]]. These are mathematical model identities under an adopted preparation rule; they do not establish that a physical system is equilibrated.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 5, §§5.1–5.2, author-hosted manuscript
Mehran Kardar, Statistical Mechanics I, MIT OpenCourseWare, Lecture 21, Quantum Microstates and Quantum Macrostates

items.title: Static finite quantum response and covariance
items.design_state: draft-research
items.physical_scope: Nonzero finite-dimensional static canonical model with a bounded Hermitian control observable; noncommuting response uses Kubo–Mori covariance, while ordinary variance is asserted only in the commuting case.
items.statement:
Adopt the finite canonical state rule of [[post-qsm-thermal-gibbs-preparation]]. Let $H(h)=H_0-hB$ on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension $d\geq1$, where $H_0,B$ are Hermitian, $h$ is a real static control, $hB$ has units J, and $\beta>0$ is fixed in J$^{-1}$. Put $\rho_h=e^{-\beta H(h)}/Z(h)$. With $\delta B=B-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_hB)I$, define
$
\operatorname{Cov}_{KM,\rho_h}(B,B)=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_h^{1-u}\delta B\rho_h^u\delta B)\,du.
$
Then the static susceptibility is
$
\frac{d}{dh}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_hB)=\beta\operatorname{Cov}_{KM,\rho_h}(B,B)\geq0.
$
Here $\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_h}(B)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_h(B-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_hB)I)^2)$ is the ordinary variance. The Kubo–Mori covariance equals this variance exactly when $[H(h),B]=0$; for noncommuting matrices the Kubo–Mori expression is the applicable covariance. This is a static model deduction, not a dynamical response or observation.

references.title: Zhang Jiang, Quantum Fisher information for states in exponential form, arXiv:1310.2687v3, §II, equations (2.1)–(2.14)
Mehran Kardar, Statistical Mechanics I, MIT OpenCourseWare, Lecture 21, Quantum Microstates and Quantum Macrostates

row.title: Normal density states and spectral moments — Examples

items.title: Pure entanglement and correlated mixtures
items.design_state: draft-research
items.physical_scope: Exact two-qubit state, marginal, entropy and sharp-observable probability calculations under the adopted normal-state Born interpretation; no apparatus or experimental outcome is asserted.
items.statement:
With $k_B>0$ as fixed by [[def-qsm-relative-entropy-domain]], for two qubits with basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, compare the Bell pure state $|\Phi\rangle=(|00\rangle+|11\rangle)/\sqrt2$, with density $\rho_\Phi=|\Phi\rangle\langle\Phi|$, and the classically correlated mixture
$
\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}=\tfrac12|00\rangle\langle00|+\tfrac12|11\rangle\langle11|.
$
Both states have marginals $I_2/2$ and hence marginal entropy $k_B\log2$. The global entropies differ:
$
S(\rho_\Phi)=0,\qquad S(\rho_{\mathrm{mix}})=k_B\log2.
$
The Bell pure state is entangled for the declared two-qubit splitting; the mixture is separable. The dimensionless Hermitian observable $W=|00\rangle\langle11|+|11\rangle\langle00|$ has outcome $+1$ with probability $1$ in $\rho_\Phi$, and probabilities $1/2,1/2$ for $+1,-1$ in $\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}$. These are exact predictions of the adopted measurement model, not reports of an apparatus.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.3, author-hosted manuscript
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 5, §5.2, author-hosted manuscript

items.title: Oscillator trace Gibbs and divergent normalization
items.design_state: draft-research
items.physical_scope: Exact canonical formulas for a one-mode diagonal oscillator model and a contrasting infinite-degeneracy model; no measured values or universal normalization claim.
items.statement:
On $\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)$, take $(e_n)_{n\geq0}$ to be the standard orthonormal basis and define the oscillator Hamiltonian
$
He_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)e_n,\qquad
D(H)=\left\{(c_n):\sum_{n\geq0}(n+\tfrac12)^2|c_n|^2<\infty\right\},
$
with $\omega>0$, $\hbar>0$. Its eigenvalues have units J. For $\beta>0$ in J$^{-1}$, put $x=\beta\hbar\omega$ and $r=e^{-x}$. The canonical trace and state are finite and
$
Z_\beta=\frac{e^{-x/2}}{1-e^{-x}},\qquad
U_\beta=\hbar\omega\left(\frac12+\frac{1}{e^x-1}\right),\qquad
S(\rho_\beta)=k_B\left[-\log(1-e^{-x})+\frac{x}{e^x-1}\right].
$
By contrast, on an infinite-dimensional $\ell^2$ space with $H=0$, $e^{-\beta H}=I$ is not trace class, so there is no normalized trace Gibbs density. The preparation in the first model is adopted by [[post-qsm-thermal-gibbs-preparation]]; no experiment is reported.

references.title: Mehran Kardar, Statistical Mechanics I, MIT OpenCourseWare, Lecture 21, Quantum Microstates and Quantum Macrostates
Mehran Kardar, Statistical Mechanics I, MIT OpenCourseWare, Lecture 23, Canonical and Grand Canonical Formulations

items.title: Two-level Gibbs and noncommuting susceptibility
items.design_state: draft-research
items.physical_scope: Exact finite two-level canonical model with a static transverse control; response is a model prediction and not an experimental measurement.
items.statement:
Take the two-dimensional Hilbert space with Hamiltonian $H(h)=\operatorname{diag}(-\epsilon/2,\epsilon/2)-h\sigma_x$, $\epsilon>0$, and $\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$. The control $h$ has units J so that $h\sigma_x$ is an energy. At fixed $\beta>0$, put $Z(h)=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H(h)})$, $\rho_h=e^{-\beta H(h)}/Z(h)$, and define $\langle A\rangle_h:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_hA)$. The finite canonical response is
$
\left.\frac{d}{dh}\langle\sigma_x\rangle_h\right|_{h=0}
=\chi=\beta\frac{\tanh x}{x},\qquad x=\frac{\beta\epsilon}{2}>0.
$
At $h=0$, the variance in the canonical state is $\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_0}(\sigma_x)=1$, so $0<\chi<\beta\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_0}(\sigma_x)=\beta$. The strict reduction from ordinary variance is a finite noncommuting quantum response; it makes no experimental claim.

references.title: Zhang Jiang, Quantum Fisher information for states in exponential form, arXiv:1310.2687v3, §II, equations (2.1)–(2.14)
Mehran Kardar, Statistical Mechanics I, MIT OpenCourseWare, Lecture 21, Quantum Microstates and Quantum Macrostates

row.title: Finite tensor density, observable and measurement language

items.title: Finite Hermitian diagonalization
items.design_state: Batch 37 draft; proof, source and readiness status are recorded in the batch evidence.
items.statement:
For every integer $d\ge1$ and Hermitian matrix $A\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, there is
an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb C^d$ consisting of eigenvectors of $A$, and
all eigenvalues are real. If in addition $x^*Ax\ge0$ for every $x\in\mathbb
C^d$, every eigenvalue is nonnegative and the matrix $A^{1/2}$ obtained by
replacing each eigenvalue by its nonnegative square root is well defined.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, §2.1.2
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2, §2.3

items.title: Finite tensor density, observable and measurement language
items.design_state: Batch 37 draft; proof, source and readiness status are recorded in the batch evidence.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $q\ge1$, let $V=\mathbb C^q$ with its standard ordered
orthonormal basis $(|j\rangle)_{j=1}^q$, and use the inner-product convention
that is linear in the first argument. For each integer $N\ge0$, write
$V_N=V^{\otimes N}$ with the displayed factor order; $V_0=\mathbb C$.
The lexicographically ordered product vectors form the chosen basis of
$V_N$, as in [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]].

A **finite tensor density** on $V_N$ is a density operator in the exact
root-library sense of [[def-qc-density-operator]]: a nonnegative endomorphism
$\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. In the standard column coordinates
this means $\rho=\rho^*$ and $x^*\rho x\ge0$ for every $x$.

A **bounded observable matrix** on $V_N$ is a Hermitian matrix $A=A^*$,
with operator norm $\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\|x\|=1}\|Ax\|$. Its
mathematical expectation functional in $\rho$ is
$\omega_\rho(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$. This is a finite matrix trace
pairing; its physical interpretation is supplied separately by a measurement
postulate.

A **finite POVM** with $r\ge1$ outcomes is a family
$M_1,\ldots,M_r$ of nonnegative matrices on $V_N$ with
$\sum_{a=1}^r M_a=I$. Each $M_a$ is an **effect**, meaning $0\le M_a\le I$;
the upper bound follows because $I-M_a=\sum_{b\ne a}M_b\ge0$. The numbers
$\operatorname{Tr}(\rho M_a)$ are its finite trace pairings. They are
nonnegative and normalized when read as outcome probabilities under the
adopted physical Born rule. Here $M\ge0$ means $M=M^*$ and
$x^*Mx\ge0$ for every column vector $x$. This definition alone does not
adopt the physical probability rule.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, §2.1.2
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2, §§2.3–2.3.1

items.title: Dimensionless entropy of a finite density matrix
items.design_state: Batch 37 draft; proof, source and readiness status are recorded in the batch evidence.
items.statement:
For a finite tensor density $\rho$ on $V_N$, list its eigenvalues with
multiplicity as $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{q^N}$. The finite Hermitian
diagonalization in [[lem-qsm-local-hermitian-diagonalization]] and positivity
of $\rho$ give $\lambda_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Define its
**dimensionless spectral entropy**, measured in nats, by
$$s_N(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\lambda_i>0}\lambda_i\log\lambda_i,$$
with $0\log0:=0$. This is independent of the ordering of the eigenvalues,
including when eigenvalues are repeated. It contains no physical entropy
unit; here $\log$ is the natural logarithm of [[def-natural-logarithm]],
and a later physical postulate may assign $S_N=k_Bs_N$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, §5.2.2
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §4.4.5

items.title: Additive spectral Hamiltonian and normalized ensembles
items.design_state: Batch 37 draft; proof, source and readiness status are recorded in the batch evidence.
items.statement:
Fix $q\ge1$ and real level parameters $e_1,\ldots,e_q$. Use the real
exponential of [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]] and natural logarithm
of [[def-natural-logarithm]]. For $N\ge1$, define
the one-site diagonal matrix $h|j\rangle=e_j|j\rangle$ and, for
$a=1,\ldots,N$,
$$h^{(a)}=I^{\otimes(a-1)}\otimes h\otimes I^{\otimes(N-a)},\qquad H_N=\sum_{a=1}^N h^{(a)}.$$
Thus the product basis vector $|j_1,\ldots,j_N\rangle$ has eigenvalue
$E(j_1,\ldots,j_N)=\sum_{a=1}^N e_{j_a}$; repeated level values remain
distinct basis labels and therefore count as degeneracy.

For finite $\beta\in\mathbb R$, put
$$Z_1=\sum_{j=1}^q e^{-\beta e_j},\qquad p_j=\frac{e^{-\beta e_j}}{Z_1},\qquad E=\sum_{j=1}^q p_je_j.$$
All terms in $Z_1$ are positive, so $Z_1>0$. Define the one-site canonical
density $\gamma=\operatorname{diag}(p_1,\ldots,p_q)$. For $N$ sites put
$$Z_N=\sum_{(j_1,\ldots,j_N)\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^N} e^{-\beta\sum_{a=1}^N e_{j_a}},\qquad \gamma_N=\operatorname{diag}\left( \frac{e^{-\beta\sum_{a=1}^N e_{j_a}}}{Z_N}\right)_ {(j_1,\ldots,j_N)\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^N}.$$
The mathematical definition permits $\beta=0$ and negative $\beta$ as well
as positive $\beta$; a physical positive-temperature interpretation is a
separate assumption.

For a width $\delta_N\ge0$, define the spectral band label set and its
projection by
$$\Gamma_N=\left\{(j_1,\ldots,j_N): \left|\sum_{a=1}^N e_{j_a}-NE\right|\le\delta_N\right\},\qquad \Pi_N=\sum_{\mathbf j\in\Gamma_N}|\mathbf j\rangle\langle\mathbf j|.$$
Its rank is $\Omega_N=\operatorname{Tr}\Pi_N=|\Gamma_N|$, which counts
all basis vectors in the band, including degeneracy. When $\Omega_N>0$,
define the normalized band density $\sigma_N=\Pi_N/\Omega_N$. If
$\Omega_N=0$, this normalized density is undefined.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, §§1.2–1.3
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.2–4.4

items.title: Subsystem expectations and reduced finite tensor densities
items.design_state: Batch 37 draft; proof, source and readiness status are recorded in the batch evidence.
items.statement:
Let $V_A,V_B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional tensor registers and let $\rho$
be a finite tensor density on $V_A\otimes V_B$. Then
$$\rho_A:=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho$$
is a finite tensor density on $V_A$. For every matrix $A$ on $V_A$,
$$\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_AA)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho(A\otimes I_B)).$$
For a finite POVM $(M_a)_{a=1}^r$ on $V_A$, the trace pairings of its
outcomes in $\rho_A$ equal the trace pairings of the lifted effects
$M_a\otimes I_B$ in $\rho$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, §§2.1.2–2.3
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2, §§2.3–2.3.1

items.title: Quasilocal completion of finite matrix registers
items.design_state: Batch 37 draft; proof, source and readiness status are recorded in the batch evidence.
items.statement:
Fix $q\ge1$ and the ordered registers $V_N=(\mathbb C^q)^{\otimes N}$,
with $V_0=\mathbb C$. Here $\operatorname{End}(V_N)$ is the space of linear
maps $V_N\to V_N$ as in [[def-linear-map]]. For such a map define its
operator norm by $\|A\|:=\sup_{\|x\|=1}\|Ax\|$, using the ordered tensor
inner product of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and let $A^*$ be
its adjoint. Embed $\mathcal A_N=\operatorname{End}(V_N)$ into
$\mathcal A_{N+1}$ by
$\iota_N(A)=A\otimes I_q$. Write a vector in $V_N\otimes\mathbb C^q$ as
$x=\sum_{j=1}^q x_j\otimes|j\rangle$. Then
$$\|(A\otimes I_q)x\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^q\|Ax_j\|^2 \le\|A\|^2\sum_{j=1}^q\|x_j\|^2=\|A\|^2\|x\|^2.$$
Testing on unit simple tensors $v\otimes|1\rangle$ and taking the supremum
over unit $v$ gives the reverse norm inequality, hence
$\|A\otimes I_q\|=\|A\|$. The embeddings are isometric unital
*-homomorphisms. For $m\ge N$, define
$\iota_{N,m}(A)=A\otimes I_q^{\otimes(m-N)}$ and identify
$A\in\mathcal A_N$ with its image at every larger register. For a two-step
inclusion the maps fit into this commutative diagram:

```tikzcd
\mathcal A_N \arrow[r,"\iota_N"] \arrow[rr,bend right=16,"\iota_{N,N+2}"'] & \mathcal A_{N+1} \arrow[r,"\iota_{N+1}"] & \mathcal A_{N+2}
```

The curved arrow tensors with two identities, and the upper path tensors with
one identity twice; both send $A$ to $A\otimes I_q\otimes I_q$. Let
$\mathcal A_{\rm loc}=\bigcup_{N\ge0}\mathcal A_N$ with the
induced norm, product and adjoint. Define $\mathcal A=\overline{\mathcal
A_{\rm loc}}$ in this norm. This is the
quasilocal matrix algebra for the one-dimensional ordered register chain; it
is a unital C*-algebra with unit the common image of $1\in\mathcal A_0$.

The sequence $(\mathcal A_N,\iota_N)$ is the specified inductive system.
This definition concerns one fixed local matrix size $q$ and makes no claim
about a physical lattice geometry or dynamics.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, §§2.1.2–2.3
Maria Shirbisheh, An Introduction to C*-Algebras, §3.1

items.physical_scope: Adopted preparation assignments for the explicitly finite, noninteracting q-level tensor model: canonical finite-temperature density and, when nonempty, a uniform exact energy-band density. These rules are conditional model inputs; they do not assert dynamical thermalization, experimental frequencies, data, or a continuum or interacting limit.
items.title: Adopted finite canonical and band preparation rules
items.design_state: Batch 37 draft; proof, source and readiness status are recorded in the batch evidence.
items.statement:
For the finite $q$-level tensor model of
[[def-qsm-local-additive-spectral-ensembles]], adopt the following
preparation rules in addition to the state and outcome assumptions P1 and P2
of [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] and
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]. The quantities in this
item are model assignments; they are not inferred from the cited texts or
from data.

1. For declared temperature $T>0$ kelvin and Boltzmann constant
   $k_B=1.380649\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, the fixed exact SI
   Boltzmann constant, use $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$ joules$^{-1}$. In this
   formulation $k_B$ is the primitive SI conversion constant between

   [[def-qsm-local-additive-spectral-ensembles]] are primitive model energy
   parameters in joules. The total label energy
   $E(j_1,\ldots,j_N)=\sum_{a=1}^Ne_{j_a}$ and the one-site canonical mean
   $E=\sum_{j=1}^qp_je_j$ defined there are derived scalar energies in

2. For declared band width $\delta_N\ge0$ in joules, if its label set
   $\Gamma_N$ is nonempty, the uniform band preparation is the density

3. For a stated finite POVM $(M_a)$ on the register, the outcome law is the
   adopted Born law $p_a=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho M_a)$ of P2. A prediction is
   the resulting model probability, not a reported detector frequency.

items.design_state: Batch 37 draft; proof, source and readiness status are recorded in the batch evidence.
items.statement:
Use the finite additive spectral data of
[[def-qsm-local-additive-spectral-ensembles]]. For every $N\ge1$,
$Z_N=Z_1^N$. For each product label $\mathbf j=(j_1,\ldots,j_N)$, the
diagonal entry of $\gamma_N$ is $\prod_{a=1}^N p_{j_a}$ and its off-diagonal
entries are zero. For each integer $k$ with $1\le k\le N$, write
$x,x'\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^k$ and $y\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^{N-k}$, and define the
first-$k$ reduced matrix $R_{N,k}$ by
$$ (R_{N,k})_{x,x'}:=\sum_{y\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^{N-k}}(\gamma_N)_{(x,y),(x',y)}. $$
When $k=N$, the tail-label set consists of the single empty tuple. Then
$R_{N,k}=\gamma_k$, where $\gamma_k$ is the diagonal matrix on
$V_k=(\mathbb C^q)^{\otimes k}$ with entries
$(\gamma_k)_{x,x}=\prod_{a=1}^k p_{x_a}$, and the canonical state has expected
additive energy $NE$.

items.title: Consistent finite classical laws define a quasilocal C-star state
items.design_state: Batch 37 draft; proof, source and readiness status are recorded in the batch evidence.
items.statement:
Let $q\ge1$ and, for every $N\ge1$, let
$\mu_N:\{1,\ldots,q\}^N\to[0,1]$ satisfy
$$\sum_{x\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^N}\mu_N(x)=1.$$
Assume consistency under deleting the last coordinate in the explicit sense
that, for every $N\ge1$ and $x\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^N$,
$$\mu_N(x)=\sum_{j=1}^q\mu_{N+1}(x,j).$$
For a local matrix $A\in\mathcal A_N$, $N\ge1$, define
$$\omega_N(A)=\sum_{x\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^N}\mu_N(x)A_{xx}.$$
For each $N\ge1$, if $f:\{1,\ldots,q\}^N\to\mathbb C$ and $D_f$ is the
diagonal matrix with entries $(D_f)_{xx}=f(x)$, then
$\omega_N(D_f)=\sum_x\mu_N(x)f(x)$. This rule extends uniquely from the
local algebra $\mathcal A_{\rm loc}$ to a state on its norm completion
$\mathcal A$ of [[def-qsm-local-matrix-net-completion]]. The theorem
constructs a classical diagonal state; it does not say that every state on
$\mathcal A$ is diagonal or classical.

items.title: Fixed-subsystem equivalence for independent finite energy shells
items.design_state: Batch 37 draft; proof, source and readiness status are recorded in the batch evidence.
items.statement:
Fix $q\ge1$, real one-site levels $e_j$, finite $\beta\in\mathbb R$, and
the ensembles of [[def-qsm-local-additive-spectral-ensembles]]. Suppose for
every $N$ the band width obeys
$$\delta_N\ge q\sum_{j=1}^q|e_j|,\qquad \delta_N/N\longrightarrow0.$$
Then every band is nonempty. For each fixed integer $k\ge1$ and $N\ge k$,
define $\sigma_{N,k}$ by its product-basis entries, for
$x,x'\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^k$,
$(\sigma_{N,k})_{x,x'}=\sum_{y\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^{N-k}}(\sigma_N)_{(x,y),(x',y)}$,
with a single empty tail label when $N=k$.
Define $\gamma_k$ to be the diagonal matrix on
$V_k=(\mathbb C^q)^{\otimes k}$ with entries
$(\gamma_k)_{x,x}=\prod_{a=1}^k p_{x_a}$ and zero off the diagonal. Then
$$\|\sigma_{N,k}-\gamma_k\|_1\to0,\qquad \frac1N s_N(\sigma_N)\to -\sum_{j=1}^q p_j\log p_j.$$
Here $\|D\|_1$ for a Hermitian finite matrix is the sum of absolute values
of its eigenvalues, and $s_N$ is dimensionless spectral entropy. This is an
independent finite-alphabet result; it asserts neither global trace-norm
convergence nor an interacting or continuous-model equivalence.

items.statement:
Fix a finite integer $r\ge1$, positive coefficients $a_j$, a real polynomial
$V$ on $\mathbb R^r$, and constants $c>0,C_0\ge0$ such that
$V(q)\ge c|q|^2-C_0$. Use the QFT supplier's form realization of
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]] and
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]] on
$L^2(\mathbb R^r,dq)$, and denote its self-adjoint operator by $h$. This
item's **regulated interacting model** is the tuple of these finite data,
the selected form realization, and an energy scale $E_*>0$ joules, with
$H=E_*h$. The coordinate $q$ and coefficients are dimensionless rescaled
model parameters unless another dimensional map is explicitly supplied.
The finite polynomial may couple coordinates; no limit in $r$ is included.

For each $b>0$, [[thm-qft-regulated-gibbs-trace]] proves
$\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-b h})<\infty$ and positivity. Thus for physical
$\beta>0$ in joules$^{-1}$, $b=\beta E_*>0$ and
$$\rho_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta H}}{Z_\beta},\qquad Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})\in(0,\infty)$$

quantum measurement state uses the current batch-36 draft carrier
[[post-qsm-normal-measurement-state]], which adopts a trace-class density on a
specified separable Hilbert space and the PVM Born law
$\mathbb P_\rho\{A\in C\}=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho E_A(C))$. This interface
matches the mathematical state constructed here. The mathematical probability and bounded trace-pairing inputs now have exact canonical suppliers through the trace-state calculus. The normal-state interpretation remains an adopted physical premise; source adoption is separate from native readiness and empirical validation. The QFT mathematical trace theorem remains the mathematical supplier.

self-adjointness of the bare compact-support differential expression, a

items.title: Local spin matrix algebras and their factor inclusions
items.design_state: reserved item; authored conditionally at inspected supplier interfaces
items.statement:
Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$, the countable site set $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}^d$ of [[lem-qsm-integer-lattice-countable]], and one finite spin dimension $q\ge1$. Equip $\Gamma$ with the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty(x,y)=\max_{1\le r\le d}|x_r-y_r|$; symmetry and separation hold coordinatewise, and the triangle inequality follows from $|x_r-z_r|\le|x_r-y_r|+|y_r-z_r|$ for every coordinate. A **finite region** is a finite subset $\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma$; its cardinality is $|\Lambda|$.

For a finite region $\Lambda$, let $S_\Lambda=\{1,\ldots,q\}^{\Lambda}$ be the set of spin configurations on $\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ be the vector space of functions $f:S_\Lambda\to\mathbb C$ with inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}f(s)\overline{g(s)}$. For each $s\in S_\Lambda$, let $e_s$ be the indicator function of $\{s\}$; these vectors form an orthonormal basis. For $\Lambda=\varnothing$, $S_\Lambda$ is a singleton and $\mathcal H_\Lambda\cong\mathbb C$. The **local spin matrix algebra** is

$$\mathcal A_\Lambda:=\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)\cong M_{q^{|\Lambda|}}(\mathbb C),$$

Here $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)$ denotes all complex-linear endomorphisms of the finite-dimensional Hilbert space; they are bounded. The algebra has composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity $I_\Lambda$, and induced operator norm

$$\|T\|:=\sup_{\|\xi\|=1}\|T\xi\|.$$

The **finite local trace** is $\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(T):=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}\langle T e_s,e_s\rangle$ in the displayed configuration basis $(e_s)$. This is the usual finite-matrix trace; basis independence and its cyclic/unitary identities are supplied by [[lem-qsm-matrix-state-calculus]].

If $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, restriction of configurations gives the canonical factorization $\mathcal H_{\Lambda'}\cong\mathcal H_\Lambda\otimes\mathcal H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$, with sites ordered lexicographically. The **factor inclusion** is the unital $*$-homomorphism $\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}:\mathcal A_\Lambda\to\mathcal A_{\Lambda'}$ given by $T\mapsto T\otimes I_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$. A **localization region** for $T$ is any finite $\Lambda$ for which $T\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ under these inclusions; a localization region need not be minimal.

The ordinary operator norm makes each local matrix algebra a nonzero unital complete C*-algebra, and every positive normalized complex-linear functional is uniquely a trace pairing with a density matrix, by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]]. This includes the empty region, whose Hilbert space is $\mathbb C$. This definition does not posit an infinite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert space.
items.strategy: Explicitly define the finite configuration Hilbert spaces, their matrix algebras, and the identity-tensor inclusions.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §§3.2.2–3.2.3, pp. 55–57
David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, Chapter 3 §1, pp. 25–26

items.title: Local spin factor inclusions preserve the operator norm
items.design_state: batch-local inventory expansion; proof and supplier status recorded in batch evidence
items.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$, $q\ge1$, and finite regions $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ as in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. Then the factor inclusion $\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(T)=T\otimes I$ is an isometric unital $*$-homomorphism:

$$\|\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(T)\|=\|T\|\qquad(T\in\mathcal A_\Lambda).$$

For nested finite regions $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'\subseteq\Lambda''$, the inclusions compose: $\iota_{\Lambda',\Lambda''}\circ\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}=\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda''}$.
items.strategy: Expand vectors in a finite orthonormal basis of the added tensor factor for the upper norm bound; use a near-norming vector and a unit configuration vector for the lower bound.

items.title: Norm-completed quasi-local quantum spin algebra
items.design_state: reserved item; authored conditionally at inspected supplier interfaces
items.statement:
Use the finite local matrix algebras and isometric factor inclusions of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]] and [[lem-qsm-local-spin-inclusions-isometric]]. Identify $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ with its image in every larger finite-region algebra. The directed union

$$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}:=\bigcup_{\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma,\ |\Lambda|<\infty}\mathcal A_\Lambda$$

is the algebra of **strictly local observables**. Its norm is $\|A\|=\|A\|_{\mathcal A_\Lambda}$ for any finite localization region $\Lambda$ of $A$; isometric inclusions make this independent of the chosen region. The **quasi-local spin algebra** is the norm completion

$$\mathcal A:=\overline{\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}}^{\,\|\cdot\|}.$$

The C*-algebra structure on this completion has product and adjoint extended continuously from the finite local matrix algebras. Countable Choice is assumed for the published existence theorem for metric completions; [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]] supplies the full extension argument using the finite C*-identity of [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]].

**No global Hilbert tensor product is selected.** “Quasi-local” means norm completion of the directed algebra of finite-region observables; it does not mean a chosen representation as operators on an infinite tensor-product Hilbert space. A local operator $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ may have more than one localization region. Disjoint finite local factors commute in their common finite tensor algebra.
items.strategy: Take the directed union of the finite local algebras with their isometric identifications and complete it in norm; no infinite Hilbert tensor product is selected.

items.title: Infinite algebraic state and finite-region restrictions
items.design_state: reserved item; authored conditionally at inspected supplier interfaces
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be the unital quasi-local spin C*-algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]], whose C*-structure uses Countable Choice as in [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]]. An **infinite algebraic state** is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ satisfying $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$.

For each finite region $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$, the restriction $\omega|_{\mathcal A_\Lambda}$ is a finite-matrix state. By [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]], every positive normalized functional on a finite matrix algebra is represented by a unique density matrix. Define its **local density matrix** $\rho_\Lambda$ by

$$\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(\rho_\Lambda A)\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda),$$

where $\rho_\Lambda=\rho_\Lambda^*\ge0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}\rho_\Lambda=1$. For $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, the local densities are **consistent** when $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$, with partial trace characterized by its pairing against every $A\otimes I_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$. No density operator on a globally chosen Hilbert space is part of this definition.

This agrees with the canonical state convention of [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]]: the finite restrictions have norm one by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]], giving $|\omega(A)|\le\|A\|$ on the dense local algebra and hence on its completion; evaluation at the norm-one identity gives $\|\omega\|=1$. Conversely a canonical state has local restrictions with density matrices of trace one, since the finite norm formula and continuity on the dense local algebra imply $\|\omega\|=\omega(I)$. No global density representation is asserted.
items.strategy: Define a bounded normalized positive functional and its finite-region density restrictions, conditional on the finite state/density correspondence.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §§2.4–2.5, pp. 34–40

Let $\{\rho_\Lambda\}$ be positive trace-one matrices, one on each finite-region algebra $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]], such that for every $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$ their partial traces agree: $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$. There is a unique infinite algebraic state $\omega$ on $\mathcal A$ whose restriction to each $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ is $A\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(\rho_\Lambda A)$.

items.title: Sequential compactness of the quasi-local spin state space
items.design_state: reserved item; authored conditionally at inspected supplier interfaces
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the countable union of finite regions and the finite-dimensional state/density interface explicitly stated in Facts [F3]. Let $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, and $q\ge1$ be as in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. Thus the state space is sequentially compact in the pointwise topology, meaning convergence on every fixed observable. The conclusion concerns functional values; it does not assert convergence of global density matrices or a global trace-class representation.

items.title: Cyclic representation of a quasi-local state
items.design_state: reserved item; authored conditionally at inspected supplier interfaces
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the C*-algebra completion interface of [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]], and the finite-matrix positive square-root interface of [[lem-qsm-matrix-state-calculus]]. Let $\{\rho_\Lambda\}$ be a consistent family of finite local density matrices as in [[lem-qsm-consistent-local-states]], and let $\omega$ be its extended algebraic state on the unital quasi-local algebra $\mathcal A$. Then there are a complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H_\omega$, a unital $*$-representation $\pi_\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\omega)$, and a unit vector $\Omega_\omega$ cyclic for $\pi_\omega$ such that

$$\omega(A)=\langle \pi_\omega(A)\Omega_\omega,\Omega_\omega\rangle\qquad(A\in\mathcal A),$$

using the linear-first inner-product convention. Here $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\omega)$ is the space of bounded linear operators with its operator norm, a $*$-representation is a complex-linear map preserving products, adjoints and the identity, and cyclic means that $\{\pi_\omega(A)\Omega_\omega:A\in\mathcal A\}$ is norm dense in $\mathcal H_\omega$. The theorem asserts existence of a cyclic representation, not uniqueness up to unitary equivalence.

items.title: Two-site Pauli observables commute at disjoint sites
items.design_state: batch-local inventory expansion; proof and supplier status recorded in batch evidence

Take $d=1$, spin dimension $q=2$, and distinct sites $x,y\in\mathbb Z$. On $\mathbb C^2$ define the Pauli matrices

$$X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Let $X_x$ and $Z_y$ be their one-site observables embedded in the two-site algebra $\mathcal A_{\{x,y\}}$ by the factor inclusions of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. Then $X_x$ and $Z_y$ are self-adjoint unitaries of norm one and commute. This is a finite example of the locality clause in [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]].

items.title: A norm-convergent observable with no finite localization region

items.statement:
Take $d=1$ and $q=2$. For $n\ge1$, let $Z_n$ be the one-site Pauli matrix $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ embedded at site $n\in\mathbb Z$. The sequence

$$H_N:=\sum_{n=1}^N2^{-n}Z_n$$

converges in norm in the quasi-local algebra to an element $H$. This element is self-adjoint but has no finite localization region. Thus norm completion adds observables that are not strictly local.

items.title: Consistent maximally mixed local densities
items.design_state: batch-local inventory expansion; proof and supplier status recorded in batch evidence
items.statement:
Fix finite spin dimension $q\ge1$ on $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$. For every finite region $\Lambda$, set

$$\rho_\Lambda:=q^{-|\Lambda|}I_\Lambda.$$

This is a consistent family of maximally mixed local density matrices. By the finite-dimensional density-state correspondence of [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]] and [[lem-qsm-consistent-local-states]], it determines a unique algebraic state $\omega$ on the quasi-local spin algebra. For local $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$, its expectation is $\omega(A)=q^{-|\Lambda|}\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(A)$.

items.title: Uniformly bounded finite-range quantum spin interaction
items.design_state: reserved A-page item; finite-range interaction and free-boundary finite-volume convention explicitly defined
items.statement:
Use the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, the finite spin dimension $q\ge1$, the local matrix algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$, and the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. For finite nonempty $Z\subset\Gamma$, write $\operatorname{diam}_\infty Z=\max_{x,y\in Z}d_\infty(x,y)$; for finite nonempty $X,Y\subset\Gamma$, write $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(X,Y)=\min_{x\in X,y\in Y}d_\infty(x,y)$.

A **uniformly bounded finite-range interaction** is a family $\Phi(Z)\in\mathcal A_Z$, indexed by finite nonempty $Z\subset\Gamma$, such that $\Phi(Z)^*=\Phi(Z)$ and there are an integer $M\ge1$, a finite $R\ge0$, and $\kappa<\infty$ satisfying

$$\Phi(Z)=0\quad\text{if }|Z|>M\text{ or }\operatorname{diam}_\infty Z>R,\qquad\kappa:=\sup_{x\in\Gamma}\sum_{Z\ni x}\|\Phi(Z)\|<\infty.$$

The norm in this sum is the operator norm in the local matrix algebra $\mathcal A_Z$. If a model lists several terms with the same support, first add them in that local algebra; the resulting single operator is $\Phi(Z)$, and $\kappa$ uses its norm. Thus no multiplicity is implicit.

For a finite region $\Lambda\subset\Gamma$, define the **free-boundary finite-volume Hamiltonian** by summing only terms whose complete support lies inside $\Lambda$; terms meeting $\Lambda$ but extending outside it are omitted:

$$H_\Lambda:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi(Z)\in\mathcal A_\Lambda.$$

It is a finite sum of self-adjoint matrices. For a fixed scale $\hbar>0$ and any finite $\Omega\supseteq\Lambda$, embed $H_\Lambda$ in $\mathcal A_\Omega$ by the canonical factor inclusion and define

$$\alpha_t^\Lambda(A):=e^{itH_\Lambda/\hbar}Ae^{-itH_\Lambda/\hbar}\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Omega,\ t\in\mathbb R).$$

These actions are compatible as $\Omega$ increases, because the extra tensor factors carry the identity. On $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ this is the ordinary finite matrix Heisenberg dynamics.

In physical SI bookkeeping, when $\Phi(Z)$ is interpreted as an energy, $\Phi(Z)$, $\kappa$, and $H_\Lambda$ have units J, $t$ has units s, and $\hbar$ is the adopted reduced Planck constant with units J s. The mathematics below uses only $\hbar>0$ and asserts no measured parameter value.
items.strategy: Define the local self-adjoint interaction family, finite range, per-site norm bound, finite-volume Hamiltonian, and time-scaled Heisenberg maps.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §3.3.7–3.3.8, pp. 66–68
Bruno Nachtergaele and Robert Sims, Lieb-Robinson Bounds in Quantum Many-Body Physics, §3.1, pp. 18–20

items.title: Volume-independent finite-range commutator path bound
items.design_state: reserved A-page item; complete finite-volume path argument with explicit nonsharp constants
items.statement:
Let $\Phi$ be an interaction of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]] with parameters $M,R,\kappa,\hbar$. Let $\mu>0$, let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ be finite, let $X\subseteq\Lambda$ be finite and nonempty, and let $Y\subset\mathbb Z^d$ be any finite nonempty set. Take $A\in\mathcal A_X$ and $B\in\mathcal A_Y$, with both embedded in the common finite algebra $\mathcal A_{\Lambda\cup Y}$. Then for every $t\in\mathbb R$,

$$\bigl\|[\alpha_t^\Lambda(A),B]\bigr\|\le 2\|A\|\,\|B\|\,|X|\exp\!\left(\frac{2\kappa M e^{\mu R}}{\hbar}|t|-\mu\operatorname{dist}_\infty(X,Y)\right).$$

Here the finite-volume dynamics is extended by the identity on sites outside $\Lambda$, as in [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]]. The parameter $\mu$ is measured per lattice step in the dimensionless max-coordinate metric. The bound is uniform over finite volumes containing $X$; it is an operator-norm estimate for the stipulated spin model, not a relativistic light cone.
items.strategy: Differentiate the interaction-picture commutator, solve the homogeneous equation by unitary conjugation, count finite-range support paths, and sum the factorial bound.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, Theorem 4.1.2 and proof, pp. 96–101

items.title: Boundary Duhamel estimate for thermodynamic spin dynamics
items.design_state: reserved A-page item; complete Duhamel boundary estimate and exterior-tail argument
items.statement:
Let $\Phi$ be an interaction of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]], fix $\mu>0$, and let $X\subseteq\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$ be finite regions with $X\ne\varnothing$. An **increasing finite exhaustion** of $\mathbb Z^d$ means a sequence of finite regions $(\Lambda_n)_{n\ge1}$ such that $\Lambda_n\subseteq\Lambda_{n+1}$ for every $n$ and $\bigcup_{n\ge1}\Lambda_n=\mathbb Z^d$. For every $A\in\mathcal A_X$ and $t\in\mathbb R$,

$$\|\alpha_t^{\Lambda'}(A)-\alpha_t^\Lambda(A)\|\le\frac{2\kappa |X|\|A\||t|}{\hbar}e^{(2\kappa M e^{\mu R}/\hbar)|t|+\mu R}\sum_{y\notin\Lambda}e^{-\mu\operatorname{dist}_\infty(X,\{y\})}.$$

The infinite sum is finite. Along every increasing finite exhaustion $(\Lambda_n)$ as defined above, $\sum_{y\notin\Lambda_n}e^{-\mu\operatorname{dist}_\infty(X,\{y\})}\to0$, so the estimate gives compact-time norm Cauchy convergence of free-boundary finite-volume dynamics on each local observable.
items.strategy: Compare nested finite volumes by Duhamel, control boundary-crossing terms with the commutator estimate, and sum the exterior exponential tail.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, Theorem 4.2.1 and proof, pp. 101–102

items.title: Strongly continuous thermodynamic spin automorphism group
items.design_state: reserved A-page item; complete conditional norm-limit proof using the owner-added exact C*-identity interface, now page-placed but awaiting current readiness
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C*-identity condition [A1] below. Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}=\bigcup_{\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d,\ |\Lambda|<\infty}\mathcal A_\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal A$ be its norm completion as in [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. These assumptions give the conditional unital C*-algebra structure supplied by [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]]. Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]].

For any increasing finite exhaustion $(\Lambda_n)_{n\ge1}$ in the convention of [[lem-qsm-boundary-dynamics-cauchy]]—that is, each $\Lambda_n$ is finite, $\Lambda_n\subseteq\Lambda_{n+1}$, and $\bigcup_{n\ge1}\Lambda_n=\mathbb Z^d$—the free-boundary finite-volume maps $\alpha_t^{\Lambda_n}$ converge in norm on every local observable, uniformly for $t$ in compact intervals. Their limit is independent of the exhaustion and extends uniquely to a strongly continuous one-parameter group $\alpha_t$ of maps $\alpha_t:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$. Here “one-parameter group” means $\alpha_0=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$ and $\alpha_{s+t}=\alpha_s\circ\alpha_t$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$. Each $\alpha_t$ is a bijective complex-linear unital $*$-homomorphism (a $*$-automorphism), with inverse $\alpha_{-t}$. Strong continuity means $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ is norm-continuous for every fixed $A\in\mathcal A$. This result does not assert that an infinite-volume Hamiltonian is an element of $\mathcal A$ or a bounded operator on a preselected infinite tensor-product Hilbert space.
items.strategy: Use the boundary-tail Cauchy estimate on the local algebra, extend the isometric limit, prove the group law, and establish strong continuity.

items.title: Local observables lie in the closed generator domain
items.design_state: reserved A-page item; complete local commutator and closed-graph arguments, conditional on the dynamics theorem and page-placed C*-identity supplier awaiting current readiness
items.statement:
Under the hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]], including its Countable Choice and finite-matrix C*-identity conditions, let $\alpha_t$ be the strongly continuous automorphism group. Define its generator by

$$D(\delta)=\left\{A\in\mathcal A:\lim_{t\to0}\frac{\alpha_t(A)-A}{t}\text{ exists in norm}\right\},\qquad\delta(A)=\lim_{t\to0}\frac{\alpha_t(A)-A}{t}.$$

Then $\delta$ is closed. For every local $A\in\mathcal A_X$,

$$A\in D(\delta),\qquad\delta(A)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\sum_{Z:\,Z\cap X\ne\varnothing}[\Phi(Z),A].$$

The sum is finite by the finite-range and finite-size hypotheses; its value is independent of the chosen localization region $X$.
items.strategy: Stabilize the finite local commutator, pass its integral identity to the norm limit, and prove graph closedness.
