items.title: Translation-invariant finite-range spin interaction
items.design_state: new A-page definition required to state the finite translation action and invariant shape convention
items.statement:
Use the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, the finite-site Hilbert spaces, local matrix algebras, factor inclusions, and norm-completed local algebra $\mathcal A$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]] and [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. Write $\tau_x$ for spatial translation by $x\in\Gamma$. For a finite region $\Lambda$ and its configuration basis $(e_s)_{s\in\{1,\ldots,q\}^{\Lambda}}$, the bijection $s\mapsto s_x$ defined by $s_x(y+x)=s(y)$ gives a unitary $U_{x,\Lambda}:\mathcal H_\Lambda\to\mathcal H_{\Lambda+x}$ by $U_{x,\Lambda}e_s=e_{s_x}$. On $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ put $\tau_x(A)=U_{x,\Lambda}AU_{x,\Lambda}^*$.

For $x,y\in\Gamma$, the basis relabellings satisfy $U_{x,\Lambda+y}U_{y,\Lambda}=U_{x+y,\Lambda}$, since both sides send each configuration vector $e_s$ to $e_{s_{x+y}}$. Consequently $\tau_0$ is the identity and $\tau_{x+y}=\tau_x\circ\tau_y$ on local observables; continuity extends the action law to $\mathcal A$.

This local map is independent of the chosen localization region: enlarging $\Lambda$ tensors both representatives with identities, and the same site relabelling gives the corresponding enlarged unitary. On each finite region it is a unitary conjugation, hence isometric and preserves products, adjoints, and identities. It therefore extends uniquely to an isometric *-automorphism of the norm completion $\mathcal A$: if $A_n$ is local and converges to $A$, define $\tau_x(A)=\lim_n\tau_x(A_n)$; isometry makes this limit independent of the approximating sequence, and $\tau_{-x}$ is its inverse. This construction uses the norm-completion property and the isometric local maps; it does not use the separate finite-matrix C*-identity condition.

Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction in the sense of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]], with parameters $M,R,\kappa$. It is translation invariant when $\tau_x(\Phi(Z))=\Phi(Z+x)$ for every finite nonempty support $Z$ and every $x\in\Gamma$. Let $\mathscr S_\Phi$ contain one representative of each nonzero translation orbit, anchored so that the lexicographically least site of each representative is $0$, using the standard coordinate lexicographic order on $\mathbb Z^d$. The least site exists because each support is finite and nonempty; every representative contains $0$. The list $\mathscr S_\Phi$ is finite: every such support has at most $M$ sites and lies in the finite cube $[-\lceil R\rceil,\lceil R\rceil]^d$. For finite $\Lambda$, the free-boundary Hamiltonian is $H_\Lambda=\sum_{\varnothing\ne Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi(Z)$, as in the interaction definition.

When $\Phi(Z)$ represents an energy, its norm, $H_\Lambda$, and the constant $J_\Phi:=\sum_{S\in\mathscr S_\Phi}\|\Phi(S)\|$ have units joules. The definition is mathematical and makes no empirical identification of an interaction with a material.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §§3.2.2–3.2.3 and §§3.3.7–3.3.8, pp. 56–57 and 66–68
Oscar E. Lanford III and Derek W. Robinson, Statistical Mechanics of Quantum Spin Systems III, pp. 332–333

items.title: Bounded quantum lattice pressure on cubes and van Hove sets
items.design_state: reserved A-page result; full block-boundary comparison proves cube and van Hove pressure limits
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $q\ge1$, and let $\Phi$ be a translation-invariant uniformly bounded finite-range interaction as in [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]]. For each finite nonempty $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, let $H_\Lambda$ be its free-boundary finite-volume Hamiltonian, $Z_\Lambda(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(e^{-\beta H_\Lambda})$, and $p_\Lambda(\beta)=|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta)$, where $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}$ is the ordinary finite-matrix trace of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. Fix $\beta>0$, measured in inverse joules when the interaction terms are assigned energy units.

Write $d_\infty(x,y):=\max_{1\le j\le d}|x_j-y_j|$ for the lattice metric of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. For a finite $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ and $x\in\Lambda$, define $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda):=\min_{y\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda}d_\infty(x,y)$. This minimum exists: $\Lambda$ is finite, so its complement is nonempty, and the distances from $x$ to that complement are positive integers. A sequence of finite nonempty regions $(\Lambda_n)$ is van Hove if $|\Lambda_n|\to\infty$ and, for every fixed integer $r\ge0$, the inner boundary $\partial_r\Lambda_n:=\{x\in\Lambda_n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda_n)\le r\}$ satisfies $|\partial_r\Lambda_n|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$. Then $p_{\Lambda_n}(\beta)$ converges to the same finite value $p_\Phi(\beta)$ for every van Hove sequence; in particular, for positive integers $L$, the cube limit for $Q_L=\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$ exists and equals this value. The normalization is dimensionless log-partition per lattice site; the finite-volume Helmholtz free energy per site is $-\beta^{-1}p_\Lambda(\beta)$.

For every van Hove sequence $(\Lambda_n)$ and every sequence of self-adjoint matrices $B_n\in\mathcal A_{\Lambda_n}$ satisfying $\|B_n\|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$, the perturbed normalized log-partition functions satisfy
$$|\Lambda_n|^{-1}\log\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}\!\left(e^{-\beta(H_{\Lambda_n}+B_n)}\right)\longrightarrow p_\Phi(\beta).$$
No spatial support condition on $B_n$ is needed. This theorem makes no claim for changes to the bulk interaction.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §§3.4.12–3.4.16, pp. 78–82
Oscar E. Lanford III and Derek W. Robinson, Statistical Mechanics of Quantum Spin Systems III, Theorem 3.1, pp. 332–334

items.title: Quantum spectral energy concentration at a differentiable pressure point
items.design_state: reserved A-page result; finite spectral Chernoff proof at differentiable pressure points
items.statement:
Use the translation-invariant finite-range spin model and pressure $p_\Phi$ of [[thm-qsm-quantum-lattice-pressure]]. Let $\beta>0$ and suppose $p_\Phi$ is differentiable at $\beta$. Put $e_\Phi(\beta):=-p_\Phi'(\beta)$, which has units joules per site when $\beta$ is measured in inverse joules. For each nonempty finite region $\Lambda$, let $\rho_{\Lambda,\beta}=e^{-\beta H_\Lambda}/Z_\Lambda(\beta)$ and define its energy spectral probability measure by $\mu_{\Lambda,\beta}(C)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda,\beta}E_{H_\Lambda}(C))$, where $E_{H_\Lambda}(C)$ is the sum of the orthogonal eigenspace projections of $H_\Lambda$ with eigenvalues in the Borel set $C\subseteq\mathbb R$. Its finite-volume mean energy density is $m_{\Lambda,\beta}:=|\Lambda|^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda,\beta}H_\Lambda)$.

For every van Hove sequence $(\Lambda_n)$ and every $\epsilon>0$, $m_{\Lambda_n,\beta}\to e_\Phi(\beta)$ and there are constants $c_\epsilon>0$ and $n_0$ such that
$$
\mu_{\Lambda_n,\beta}\!\left(\left\{E:\left|E/|\Lambda_n|-e_\Phi(\beta)\right|\ge\epsilon\right\}\right)\le e^{-c_\epsilon|\Lambda_n|}\qquad(n\ge n_0).
$$
This is a statement about the finite-volume Gibbs spectral distribution under the declared mathematical model; it supplies no empirical observation.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §§3.4.12–3.4.15, pp. 78–81
Oscar E. Lanford III and Derek W. Robinson, Statistical Mechanics of Quantum Spin Systems III, Theorem 3.1, pp. 332–334

items.title: Stationary quantum spin entropy and energy densities
items.design_state: reserved A-page result; conditional entropy-density, energy-density, compactness, and semicontinuity arguments
items.statement:
Use the finite-range model and translations of [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]]. An algebraic state means a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$, as in [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]]. It is translation invariant if $\omega(\tau_x(A))=\omega(A)$ for every $x\in\mathbb Z^d$ and $A\in\mathcal A$. Fix the positive entropy-normalization constant $k_B>0$ used by [[thm-qsm-finite-entropy-composition]]; only division by this positive constant is needed to pass from that supplier's physical entropy to the dimensionless entropy here. Assume Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice [A1]–[A2], and use the finite-entropy and state-compactness results [L1]–[L2] at their stated scopes.

For each positive integer $L$, let $Q_L=\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$, let $\rho_{Q_L}$ be the local density matrix of $\omega$, and set $S_{Q_L}(\omega)=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{Q_L}\log\rho_{Q_L})$, with $0\log0=0$. Then
$$
s(\omega):=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{S_{Q_L}(\omega)}{L^d}=\inf_{\ell\in\mathbb N_{>0}}\frac{S_{Q_\ell}(\omega)}{\ell^d}
$$
exists. The energy density $u_\Phi(\omega):=\sum_{S\in\mathscr S_\Phi}\omega(\Phi(S))$ is finite and satisfies $\omega(H_{Q_L})/L^d\to u_\Phi(\omega)$. The translation-invariant state space is sequentially compact for pointwise convergence, $s$ is upper semicontinuous there, and $u_\Phi$ is continuous there. Entropy and energy density are dimensionless per site and joules per site, respectively, when $\Phi$ is an energy interaction.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, Proposition 3.4.14–3.4.15 and surrounding text, pp. 78–81
Oscar E. Lanford III and Derek W. Robinson, Statistical Mechanics of Quantum Spin Systems III, pp. 332–334

items.title: Stationary quantum variational pressure maximum
items.design_state: reserved A-page result; complete conditional stationary block-Gibbs variational argument
items.statement:
Use the finite-range translation-invariant model of [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]] at fixed $\beta>0$ and $k_B>0$, where $k_B$ is a positive normalization constant (the Boltzmann constant in energy/temperature bookkeeping). Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{inv}}$ be its translation-invariant algebraic states, where an algebraic state has the exact boundedness, normalization, and positivity definition in [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]], and translation invariance means $\omega\circ\tau_x=\omega$ for every $x\in\mathbb Z^d$. Assume Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice [A1]–[A2], together with the finite Gibbs, entropy, and consistent-state interfaces [L1]–[L3] at their stated scopes. Then, with the pressure $p_\Phi(\beta)$, dimensionless entropy density $s(\omega)$, and energy density $u_\Phi(\omega)$ defined in [[thm-qsm-quantum-lattice-pressure]] and [[lem-qsm-stationary-spin-entropy-density]],
$$
p_\Phi(\beta)=\max_{\omega\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{inv}}}\bigl(s(\omega)-\beta u_\Phi(\omega)\bigr).
$$
At least one maximizing state exists. Both sides are dimensionless per lattice site when $\beta$ is inverse joules and $\Phi$ is in joules. This variational claim does not identify maximizers with KMS states.

items.title: Uniform onsite energy and exact pressure

items.statement: Fix $d\ge1$, a finite site dimension $q\ge1$, and $c\in\mathbb R$. On $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, the Hilbert space of a finite region $\Lambda$ is the tensor product $\mathcal H_\Lambda=\bigotimes_{x\in\Lambda}\mathbb C^q$, with sites ordered lexicographically, dimension $q^{|\Lambda|}$, and identity $I_\Lambda$. items.title: Physical-time KMS strip equilibrium condition
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier status and disposition are recorded in batch-41 evidence.
items.statement:
Here a complex C$^*$-algebra is a complex Banach algebra with associative bilinear multiplication, submultiplicative norm, and a conjugate-linear involution satisfying $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$; **unital** means that it has a nonzero identity $I$ ([[def-c-star-algebra]]). A $*$-automorphism is a bijective complex-linear map preserving multiplication and involution. Let $t\mapsto\alpha_t$ be a strongly continuous one-parameter group of such automorphisms, so $\alpha_0$ is the identity and $\alpha_s\alpha_t=\alpha_{s+t}$. It is **strongly continuous** when $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ is norm-continuous for each fixed $A\in\mathcal A$. A **state** is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$; this is the state convention of [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]].

Fix absolute temperature $T>0$ in kelvins and Boltzmann's constant $k_B>0$ in J K$^{-1}$; the inverse-temperature parameter is $\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$, measured in J$^{-1}$. Let the reduced Planck constant $\hbar>0$ have units J s. Write $b:=\beta\hbar$, measured in seconds, and

$$S_b:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le b\},\qquad S_b^\circ:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0<\operatorname{Im}z<b\}.$$

A state $\omega$ is a **$\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in physical time** when for every $A,B\in\mathcal A$ there is a bounded function $F_{A,B}:S_b\to\mathbb C$ (that is, $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F_{A,B}(z)|<\infty$) that is continuous on $S_b$, complex-differentiable at every point of $S_b^\circ$, and satisfies

$$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega\!\left(A\alpha_t(B)\right),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+ib)=\omega\!\left(\alpha_t(B)A\right)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$

For the assigned quantum spin model, $\mathcal A$ is the norm-completed quasi-local algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]] and $\alpha$ is the thermodynamic dynamics of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]], under that theorem's stated hypotheses. The strip width is $\beta\hbar$ in physical seconds; setting $\hbar=1$ is a separate natural-unit convention. This is a mathematical equilibrium criterion for the specified algebra and dynamics. It does not assert that a model describes a material, that a system has dynamically relaxed, or that all stationary states are KMS.

items.title: Bounded KMS strip norm and zero-edge uniqueness
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier status and disposition are recorded in batch-41 evidence.
items.statement:
Let $b>0$ and $S_b=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le b\}$, with interior $S_b^\circ=\{z:0<\operatorname{Im}z<b\}$. Let $F:S_b\to\mathbb C$ be bounded (so $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F(z)|<\infty$), continuous, and complex-differentiable at every point of $S_b^\circ$, and set

$$M_0:=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F(t)|,\qquad M_1:=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F(t+ib)|.$$

For $0<s<b$,

$$\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F(t+is)|\le M_0^{1-s/b}M_1^{s/b},$$

where each exponent is positive and $0^r=0$ for $r>0$. In particular, if $M_0,M_1\le C$ then $|F(z)|\le C$ on $S_b$. If two bounded continuous functions on $S_b$, holomorphic inside, have the same lower boundary values, then they agree on all of $S_b$.

items.title: Uniform local Gibbs strip limits
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier status and disposition are recorded in batch-41 evidence.
items.statement:
Let $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, with finite on-site spin dimension $q\ge1$, local matrix algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$, and quasi-local algebra $\mathcal A$ as in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]] and [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction as in [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]], with free-boundary Hamiltonians $H_{\Lambda_n}$ on any increasing finite exhaustion $\Lambda_n\uparrow\Gamma$. Fix $\hbar>0$ and $\beta>0$, and let $\alpha_t$ be the thermodynamic dynamics of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]].

For each $n$, let $\rho_n=e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}}/\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}(e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}})$ be the finite Gibbs density. For each finite $X\subseteq\Gamma$, define its extension density by adjoining the normalized trace density $q^{-1}I$ at every site of $X\setminus\Lambda_n$ and taking the partial trace from $X\cup\Lambda_n$ to $X$. Assume the finite-matrix C$^*$-identity and the finite-matrix state/density-norm interface recorded in Facts [A1]–[A2]. The resulting consistent local densities define algebraic states $\omega_n$ on $\mathcal A$.

At least one subsequence $\omega_{n_k}$ converges pointwise on $\mathcal A$ to an algebraic state $\omega$. For every pointwise-convergent subsequence and its limit $\omega$, and for every fixed pair of strictly local observables $A,B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}$, there is a bounded function $F_{A,B}$, continuous on $S_{\beta\hbar}$ and holomorphic inside, whose boundaries are

$$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega(A\alpha_t(B)),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+i\beta\hbar)=\omega(\alpha_t(B)A)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$

This is the local-pair boundary conclusion for a pointwise limit of finite Gibbs states.

David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, Chapter 1 §7, pp. 13–14; Chapter 2 §6, pp. 24–25

items.title: KMS states are invariant under their dynamics
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier status and disposition are recorded in batch-41 evidence.
items.statement:
Let $\omega$ be a $\beta$-KMS state for a strongly continuous group $\alpha_t$ as in [[def-qsm-kms-state]], with $b=\beta\hbar>0$. Then

$$\omega(\alpha_t(B))=\omega(B)\qquad(B\in\mathcal A,\ t\in\mathbb R).$$

Thus invariance is a consequence of the full bounded-strip KMS condition; it is not an extra clause in the definition.

items.title: Finite KMS condition exactly determines the Gibbs density
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier status and disposition are recorded in batch-41 evidence.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let $H=H^*$ on $\mathcal H$ with energy units J, let $\hbar>0$ have units J s, and let $\beta>0$ have units J$^{-1}$. Write $\operatorname{Tr}$ for the ordinary finite-dimensional trace. Assume the finite spectral-calculus and unital C$^*$-algebra clauses [A1]–[A2] below. Define the finite-matrix Heisenberg group

$$\alpha_t^H(X):=e^{itH/\hbar}Xe^{-itH/\hbar}\qquad(X\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H),\ t\in\mathbb R).$$

A state $\omega$ on the unital C$^*$-algebra $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ satisfies the $\beta$-KMS strip condition of [[def-qsm-kms-state]] for $\alpha^H$ if and only if

$$\omega(X)=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H}X)}{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})}\qquad(X\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)).$$

Here $\beta$ has units J$^{-1}$, $H$ has units J, and the physical-time strip has width $\beta\hbar$ seconds. The result is finite-dimensional and makes no infinite-volume or relaxation claim.

items.title: Finite-range interacting quantum spin KMS existence
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier status and disposition are recorded in batch-41 evidence.
items.statement:
Let $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, have finite on-site spin dimension $q\ge1$ and quasi-local spin algebra $\mathcal A$. Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction with free-boundary finite-volume Hamiltonians, and let $\alpha_t$ be the strongly continuous thermodynamic dynamics of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]]. Fix $\beta>0$ and $\hbar>0$. Assume Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C$^*$-identity, and the finite-matrix state/density-norm interface exactly as stated in Facts [A1]–[A2].

For any increasing finite exhaustion $\Lambda_n\uparrow\Gamma$, extend each finite Gibbs density on $\mathcal A_{\Lambda_n}$ by normalized trace densities on the outside sites, as in [[lem-qsm-gibbs-strip-limit]]. Every pointwise convergent subsequence of these algebraic states has a limit $\omega$ that is a $\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in physical time, with strip width $\beta\hbar$. At least one such subsequential limit exists under [A1]–[A2].

The conclusion is a conditional mathematical existence result for bounded finite-dimensional spin interactions. It does not assert uniqueness, clustering, phase classification, a global infinite-volume Gibbs density matrix, or dynamical relaxation to equilibrium.

items.title: Two-level Gibbs state has the physical-time KMS boundary factor
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier status and disposition are recorded in batch-41 evidence.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$ with orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, and let $H=\varepsilon|1\rangle\langle1|$ for an energy $\varepsilon>0$ in joules. For $\beta>0$ in J$^{-1}$, the finite Gibbs state has

$$Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon},\qquad p_0=Z^{-1},\qquad p_1=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}Z^{-1}.$$

Define $S_+=|1\rangle\langle0|$ and $S_-=|0\rangle\langle1|$. With $\alpha_t(X)=e^{itH/\hbar}Xe^{-itH/\hbar}$, the correlation for $A=S_-$ and $B=S_+$ is

$$F_{S_-,S_+}(z)=p_0e^{i\varepsilon z/\hbar}.$$

At the upper strip edge $z=t+i\beta\hbar$, the exponential contributes $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, so the boundary value is $p_1e^{i\varepsilon t/\hbar}$, exactly the reversed-order Gibbs expectation. The full two-level Gibbs state is KMS for every matrix pair by [[thm-qsm-finite-kms-gibbs-characterization]]; this example checks the physical-time sign and strip-width convention on a nontrivial pair. No measurement or material parameter is being reported.

items.title: Diagonal quantum Ising interaction and classical conditional energies
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; its exact design scope is retained under the owner direction and supplier interfaces are recorded in batch-42 evidence.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\geq1$, the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, and at each site the two-dimensional complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H_i=\mathbb C^2$ with an orthonormal basis $e_{+1},e_{-1}$. Define the dimensionless local spin matrix $Z_i$ by $Z_i e_s=s e_s$ for $s\in\{-1,+1\}$. It is self-adjoint, diagonal in this basis, and has operator norm one. The local matrix algebras and factor inclusions are those of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]], and the interaction/Hamiltonian convention is that of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]].

Let $J_{ij}=J_{ji}\in\mathbb R$ be specified for distinct sites, and let $h_i\in\mathbb R$. Assume there is a finite $R\geq0$ such that $J_{ij}=0$ when $\|i-j\|_\infty>R$, and
$$\sup_{i\in\Gamma}\left(|h_i|+\sum_{j\ne i}|J_{ij}|\right)<\infty.$$
The associated quantum interaction in the convention of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]] is
$$\Phi(\{i\})=-h_iZ_i,\qquad \Phi(\{i,j\})=-J_{ij}Z_iZ_j\quad(i\ne j),\qquad \Phi(S)=0\ \text{for all other finite nonempty }S.$$
Its per-site norm sum is finite by the displayed bound, and all its terms are diagonal and commute. For a finite $\Lambda\subset\Gamma$, its free-boundary Hamiltonian is
$$H_\Lambda=-\sum_{i\in\Lambda}h_iZ_i-\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq\Lambda}J_{ij}Z_iZ_j,$$
where every unordered pair is counted once.

For a classical configuration $\sigma\in X:=\{-1,+1\}^{\Gamma}$, a finite region $\Delta\subset\Gamma$, and an exterior assignment $\eta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\Delta^c}$, write $\widehat\sigma_i=\sigma_i$ for $i\in\Delta$ and $\widehat\sigma_i=\eta_i$ otherwise. The classical conditional energy is
$$E_\Delta(\sigma_\Delta\mid\eta)=-\sum_{i\in\Delta}h_i\sigma_i-\sum_{\{i,j\}:\{i,j\}\cap\Delta\ne\varnothing}J_{ij}\widehat\sigma_i\widehat\sigma_j.$$
This is the finite-range conditional-energy convention of [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]]: each interaction term meeting $\Delta$ is included once, including terms crossing its boundary. The sum is finite because $\Delta$ is finite and the interaction range is finite. Define the finite exterior boundary
$$C_\Delta:=\{j\notin\Delta:\text{there is }i\in\Delta\text{ with }J_{ij}\ne0\}.$$
It is finite, and $E_\Delta(\sigma_\Delta\mid\eta)$ depends on $\eta$ only through $\eta|_{C_\Delta}$.

For $\beta>0$ in inverse-energy units, set
$$Z_\Delta^\eta:=\sum_{\sigma_\Delta\in\{-1,+1\}^{\Delta}}e^{-\beta E_\Delta(\sigma_\Delta\mid\eta)},\qquad \gamma_\Delta(\sigma_\Delta\mid\eta):=\frac{e^{-\beta E_\Delta(\sigma_\Delta\mid\eta)}}{Z_\Delta^\eta}.$$
The kernel sends an exterior configuration to a probability distribution on the spins in $\Delta$. A DLR measure for this model means a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $X$ fixed by these kernels for every finite $\Delta$, in the specification terminology of [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. The finite kernel is defined without a choice principle; Countable Choice is stated separately when used to extend consistent cylinder probabilities to a measure.

The model is mathematical and supplies no measured coefficients. If interpreted with SI energy units, $J_{ij}$, $h_i$, $H_\Lambda$, and $E_\Delta$ are in joules, $\beta$ is in joules$^{-1}$, and $\beta E_\Delta$ is dimensionless.

The finite kernel requires no choice principle. Borel-measure extension from consistent cylinder probabilities uses [[def-countable-choice]].

items.title: Full-algebra quantum Ising KMS–DLR correspondence
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; its exact design scope is retained under the owner direction and supplier interfaces are recorded in batch-42 evidence.
items.statement:
Fix $d\geq1$, the inhomogeneous bounded finite-range diagonal spin-$\tfrac12$ Ising interaction of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]], $\beta>0$, $\hbar>0$, Countable Choice, and the finite-matrix C*-identity supplied by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]]. Let $\mathcal A$ be its norm-completed quasi-local matrix algebra and let $\alpha_t$ be its thermodynamic dynamics. Let $\mathcal D_\beta$ be the set of Borel probability measures on $\{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb Z^d}$ fixed by every finite conditional kernel $\gamma_\Delta$ of the model. Let $\mathcal K_\beta$ be the set of $\beta$-KMS states for $\alpha$ on the full algebra $\mathcal A$, using the physical-time strip width $\beta\hbar$ seconds.

For a local matrix $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$, define its diagonal cylinder function by
$$\operatorname{diag}(A)(\sigma):=\langle A e_{\sigma|_\Lambda},e_{\sigma|_\Lambda}\rangle.$$
Then the map
$$\mathcal D_\beta\longrightarrow\mathcal K_\beta,\qquad \mu\longmapsto\omega_\mu,\qquad \omega_\mu(A):=\int\operatorname{diag}(A)(\sigma)\,d\mu(\sigma)\quad(A\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}),$$
extends uniquely to an affine bijection from classical DLR measures to $\beta$-KMS states. The KMS conclusion holds on the full matrix algebra, including off-diagonal observables; no translation invariance is assumed for this correspondence.

items.design_state: Current assigned draft; its exact design scope is retained under the owner direction and supplier interfaces are recorded in batch-42 evidence.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, the finite-matrix C*-identity, $d=2$, uniform nearest-neighbor coupling $J>0$, zero field, $\beta J\geq2$, and $\hbar>0$, in the diagonal spin-$\tfrac12$ model of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]]. Let $\tau_k$ be the spatial translation automorphisms of [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]]; a state is **translation-invariant** when $\omega(\tau_k(A))=\omega(A)$ for every local $A$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^2$. Then there are two distinct translation-invariant full-algebra $\beta$-KMS states $\omega_+$ and $\omega_-$ with
$$\omega_+(Z_i)\geq m_*>0,\qquad \omega_-(Z_i)\leq-m_*<0\quad(i\in\mathbb Z^2),$$
where one may take $m_*=1-2\delta(\beta J)$, $\delta(K)=\frac43\,\frac{r^4(5-4r)}{(1-r)^2}$, and $r=3e^{-2K}$. This conservative bound does not assert extremality or that $\beta J=2$ is critical.

For the same uniform model with field parameter $h_i=h$, let
$$p_Q(h):=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{|\Lambda_n|}\log\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}\!\left(e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}(h)}\right),\qquad \Lambda_n=[-n,n]^2,$$
the dimensionless pressure per site along cubic boxes. This limit is the corresponding classical CSM pressure. It is not differentiable at $h=0$; for every $h>0$ its secant slope from zero is at least $\beta m_*$, and for every $h<0$ it is at most $-\beta m_*$. These are exact consequences of the stated diagonal model and the CSM suppliers, not empirical material claims.

row.title: Finite-excitation vacuum spin representation and normality

items.title: Finite-excitation vacuum spin representation and normality
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier interfaces, proof status, and dispositions are recorded in batch-43 evidence.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as in [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $d\ge1$, $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, and let the finite on-site spin dimension be $q\ge1$, with the local matrix algebras and factor inclusions of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]] and [[lem-qsm-local-spin-inclusions-isometric]]. Fix a reference basis label $0$ at each site. This is a relabeling of the local basis $\{1,\ldots,q\}$ used in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]; it changes no matrix algebra.

Define the **finite-excitation configuration set**
$$S_{\mathrm{fin}}:=\{s:\Gamma\to\{0,\ldots,q-1\}:\{x\in\Gamma:s_x\ne0\}\text{ is finite}\}.$$
This set is countable: every finite support is contained in a box $[-n,n]^d$, and each box has finitely many configurations that vanish outside it. The boxes form an explicit countable exhaustion, so the union of these finite configuration sets is countable. Thus its coordinate Hilbert space is separable.
For $s\in S_{\mathrm{fin}}$, let $e_s$ be the corresponding coordinate vector. The **vacuum spin Hilbert space** is
$$\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}}:=\ell^2(S_{\mathrm{fin}}),\qquad \langle\psi,\varphi\rangle:=\sum_{s\in S_{\mathrm{fin}}}\psi_s\overline{\varphi_s},$$
where the inner product is linear in its first variable. The vectors $(e_s)_{s\in S_{\mathrm{fin}}}$ form its specified orthonormal basis, and $\Omega:=e_{s^0}$, with $s^0_x=0$ for all $x$, is the reference vacuum vector.

For a finite region $\Lambda$, write
$$S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Gamma\setminus\Lambda):=\{u:\Gamma\setminus\Lambda\to\{0,\ldots,q-1\}:\{x:u_x\ne0\}\text{ is finite}\}.$$
Restriction to $\Lambda$ and its complement gives the configuration bijection
$$S_{\mathrm{fin}}\cong\{0,\ldots,q-1\}^{\Lambda}\times S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Gamma\setminus\Lambda)$$
induces a unitary
$$U_\Lambda:\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}}\to\mathcal H_\Lambda\otimes\ell^2(S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Gamma\setminus\Lambda)).$$
For $T\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$, define
$$\pi_\Lambda(T):=U_\Lambda^{-1}\bigl(T\otimes I\bigr)U_\Lambda.$$
Under the direct-sum decomposition over outside configurations, $\pi_\Lambda(T)$ is a copy of $T$ on each block. The outside configuration set contains the all-zero configuration, so it is nonempty; the norm of this direct sum is therefore the supremum of nonempty identical block norms, namely $\|\pi_\Lambda(T)\|=\|T\|$. If $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, associativity of the configuration factorization gives $\pi_{\Lambda'}(T\otimes I)=\pi_\Lambda(T)$ on every basis vector. Thus the local maps define a unital isometric $*$-representation $\pi_{\mathrm{loc}}$ on the strictly local algebra. For a Cauchy sequence $A_n$ in that algebra, $\pi_{\mathrm{loc}}(A_n)$ is Cauchy in operator norm; its limit is independent of the chosen representative because $\|\pi_{\mathrm{loc}}(A_n-A'_n)\|=\|A_n-A'_n\|$. Completeness of $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}})$ follows directly: an operator-norm Cauchy sequence is pointwise Cauchy on every vector, its pointwise limits define a bounded linear operator, and the same Cauchy estimates give operator-norm convergence. The limits therefore define a unique continuous extension $\pi$ to the norm completion $\mathcal A$. Continuity of product and adjoint and the norm identity show that the extension remains an isometric $*$-representation, hence is faithful. This construction selects a particular representation; it does not identify $\mathcal A$ with all of $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}})$.

For a set $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}})$, its **commutant** is
$$\mathcal S':=\{T\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}}):TS=ST\text{ for every }S\in\mathcal S\},$$
and its **bicommutant** is $\mathcal S'':=(\mathcal S')'$. A **normal state** on the represented von Neumann algebra $\pi(\mathcal A)''$ means a positive normalized functional $\varphi$ that preserves suprema of bounded increasing nets of positive operators: if $0\le X_i\uparrow X$ in $\pi(\mathcal A)''$, then $\varphi(X)=\sup_i\varphi(X_i)$. Here $\pi(\mathcal A)''$ is the bicommutant in $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}})$; $\pi(\mathcal A)$ is a unital $*$-algebra and its bicommutant is strongly closed. The term normal is representation-dependent.

David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, Chapter 1 §5, printed p. 10 (normal states); Chapter 2 §1, pp. 17–18 (quasi-local spin algebra); Chapter 2 §5, pp. 42–44 (commutant and irreducibility)

items.title: Faithful irreducible finite-excitation representation
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier interfaces, proof status, and dispositions are recorded in batch-43 evidence.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge1$, and finite on-site dimension $q\ge1$. Let $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}}$ and $\pi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}})$ be the finite-excitation representation of [[def-qsm-vacuum-spin-representation]]. Then $\pi$ is faithful and irreducible:
$$\pi(\mathcal A)'=\mathbb C I,\qquad \pi(\mathcal A)''=\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}}).$$

Here irreducible means precisely that the commutant consists only of scalar multiples of the identity. No classification of other representations is claimed.

items.title: Unique onsite product Gibbs KMS state
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier interfaces, proof status, and dispositions are recorded in batch-43 evidence.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the exact finite-matrix C*-identity and positive-functional/density interfaces in [A2] below. Let $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, and let $q\ge1$ be a finite on-site dimension as in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. Let $h=h^*$ be a $q\times q$ on-site Hamiltonian, with energy unit J, and set
$$Z:=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta h}),\qquad r:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta h},$$
where $h$ has unit J and $\beta>0$ has unit J$^{-1}$. Let $\hbar>0$ have unit J s. The consistent local densities $r^{\otimes\Lambda}$ have a unique state extension $\omega_r$ to the norm-completed quasi-local algebra $\mathcal A$ by [[lem-qsm-consistent-local-states]], with local restrictions
$$\omega_r(A)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(r^{\otimes\Lambda}A)\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda).$$
Define the onsite interaction by $\Phi(\{x\})=h_x$, the copy of $h$ at site $x$, and $\Phi(Z)=0$ for all other finite nonempty $Z$. Let $\alpha_t$ be its thermodynamic dynamics under [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]]. Then $\omega_r$ is the unique $\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in the physical-time strip convention of [[def-qsm-kms-state]], whose width is $\beta\hbar$ seconds. The conclusion is mathematical; it does not assert relaxation or select a physical preparation.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §3.4, Definition 3.4.4 and finite Gibbs/KMS characterization, printed pp. 74–77
David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, Chapter 1 §7, printed pp. 13–14; Chapter 2 §6, pp. 24–25

items.title: Thermal product state has no normal vacuum extension
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier interfaces, proof status, and dispositions are recorded in batch-43 evidence.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, let $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge1$, and let $q\ge2$. Let $h=h^*$ be a finite on-site Hamiltonian, $\beta>0$, and
$$r:=\frac{e^{-\beta h}}{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta h})}.$$
Let $\omega_r$ be the unique onsite product $\beta$-KMS state from [[thm-qsm-onsite-product-kms]], and let $\pi$ be the finite-excitation vacuum representation on $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}}$ from [[def-qsm-vacuum-spin-representation]]. Then $\omega_r$ has no normal extension to
$$\pi(\mathcal A)''=\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}}).$$
By an extension we mean a state $\widetilde\omega$ on $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}})$ satisfying $\widetilde\omega(\pi(A))=\omega_r(A)$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$. In particular, no positive trace-class density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{vac}}$ satisfies $\omega_r(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\,\pi(A))$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$. Normality is representation-dependent; the statement does not rule out a normal extension in another representation.

items.title: Unique tracial KMS state is not vacuum normal
items.design_state: Current assigned draft; exact supplier interfaces, proof status, and dispositions are recorded in batch-43 evidence.
items.statement:
Let $q\ge2$, $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge1$, and take the zero Hermitian onsite Hamiltonian $h=0\in M_q(\mathbb C)$ in joules. Fix any $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds and let $\beta>0$ have units inverse joules. The onsite dynamics is $\alpha_t(A)=A$ for $t\in\mathbb R$ in seconds, and the KMS strip has width $\beta\hbar$ seconds, with the convention of [[thm-qsm-onsite-product-kms]]. For every such $\beta$, the unique quasi-local KMS state has local densities
$$\rho_\Lambda=q^{-|\Lambda|}I_\Lambda.$$
It is tracial on the full quasi-local algebra, but has no normal extension to the finite-excitation vacuum representation.

row.title: Infinite quantum spin quantities and physical adoption

items.title: Infinite quantum spin physical quantities
items.statement:
Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$, the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, a finite on-site dimension $q\ge1$, a lattice spacing $a>0$ metres, and finite-region Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ and matrix algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ as in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. The observable algebra is the norm completion $\mathcal A$ of the directed union of the local algebras, as in [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. An **infinite spin state** is a bounded positive normalized functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with local density matrices $\rho_\Lambda$ specified by $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(\rho_\Lambda A)$ for $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$, as in [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]]. A bounded local observable is an element of some $\mathcal A_\Lambda$; a measurement observable is self-adjoint. Its model expectation is $\omega(A)$, real for self-adjoint $A$. For ordered bounded local observables $A_1,\ldots,A_n$, define the ordered correlation $C_\omega(A_1,\ldots,A_n):=\omega(A_1\cdots A_n)$. It may be complex when the product is not self-adjoint, depends on the order when observables do not commute, and has the product of their assigned units. The state functional is dimensionless on dimensionless operators; if $A$ has an assigned unit, $\omega(A)$ has that same unit.

Within this formulation, primitive model inputs are the dimensionless integers $d,q$, the lattice spacing $a$, the positive constants $\hbar,k_B$, the temperature $T$, and the interaction coefficients $\Phi$ (or $J_{ij},h_i$ in the diagonal Ising submodel). The inverse temperature, finite Hamiltonians, partition functions, pressure/free-energy/entropy/energy densities, and state correlations are derived constructions under their stated hypotheses. The Born probability interpretation and the identification of KMS states with physical equilibrium are adopted separately; neither follows from this mathematical definition.

In SI bookkeeping, $a$ is measured in metres, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, and $T>0$ in kelvins. The finite-range interaction coefficients are specified inputs; a term $\Phi(Z)$ has units joules when interpreted as energy. The dimensionless local spin matrices (including the Pauli matrices in the spin-$\tfrac12$ submodel) do not by themselves identify a magnetic moment or an applied field. In a term $-h_i Z_i$, $h_i$ is an energy coefficient in joules; any identification with a laboratory field or magnetic moment requires a separate coupling and calibration model. No numerical parameter value is specified here.

The inverse-temperature parameter is the derived quantity $\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$, in joules$^{-1}$. For finite $\Lambda$, the free-boundary Hamiltonian $H_\Lambda=\sum_{\varnothing\ne Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi(Z)$ and the finite partition function $Z_\Lambda(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(e^{-\beta H_\Lambda})$ are defined by [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]] and [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. When $\Phi$ is an energy interaction, $H_\Lambda$ is in joules, $\beta H_\Lambda$ is dimensionless, and $Z_\Lambda$ is positive and dimensionless. The finite-volume Gibbs density $\rho_{\Lambda,\beta}=e^{-\beta H_\Lambda}/Z_\Lambda$ is a finite-region density matrix; it is not an asserted density matrix on an infinite tensor-product Hilbert space.

For $t$ in seconds, the finite-volume Heisenberg evolution is $\alpha_t^\Lambda(A)=e^{itH_\Lambda/\hbar}Ae^{-itH_\Lambda/\hbar}$. The thermodynamic dynamics $\alpha_t$ exists under the exact hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]]. The $\beta$-KMS criterion for this dynamics uses a bounded continuous strip function with lower edge $\omega(A\alpha_t(B))$, upper edge $\omega(\alpha_t(B)A)$, and imaginary-time width $\beta\hbar$ seconds, exactly as in [[def-qsm-kms-state]]. This is a mathematical state criterion; no global infinite-volume Gibbs trace is part of the definition.

For $x,y\in\mathbb Z^d$, write $d_\infty(x,y):=\max_{1\le j\le d}|x_j-y_j|$. For a finite region $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ and $x\in\Lambda$, define $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda):=\min_{y\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda}d_\infty(x,y)$, using the convention of [[thm-qsm-quantum-lattice-pressure]]. The minimum exists because the complement is nonempty and its distances from $x$ are positive integers. For a translation-invariant interaction $\Phi$ of [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]] and finite nonempty $\Lambda$, define the finite-volume dimensionless log-partition per site by $p_\Lambda(\beta):=|\Lambda|^{-1}\log Z_\Lambda(\beta)$. A sequence $(\Lambda_n)$ is van Hove here when $|\Lambda_n|\to\infty$ and for each fixed integer $r\ge0$, the inner boundary $\partial_r\Lambda_n=\{x\in\Lambda_n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda_n)\le r\}$ satisfies $|\partial_r\Lambda_n|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$. Under the precise finite-range and translation-invariance assumptions of [[thm-qsm-quantum-lattice-pressure]], the common finite limit is $p_\Phi(\beta):=\lim_n p_{\Lambda_n}(\beta)$. It is dimensionless per lattice site, not a pressure in pascals. Define the finite-volume free energy per site $f_\Lambda(\beta):=-\beta^{-1}p_\Lambda(\beta)$ and the thermodynamic free energy per site $f_\Phi(\beta):=-\beta^{-1}p_\Phi(\beta)=-k_BT\,p_\Phi(\beta)$, in joules per site. Dividing by the model cell volume $a^d$ gives a free-energy density in joules per cubic metre when $d=3$; this fixed-lattice quantity does not by itself define a mechanical equation of state or pressure in pascals.

A state is **spatially translation invariant** when $\omega(\tau_x(A))=\omega(A)$ for every $x\in\mathbb Z^d$ and local $A$, with $\tau_x$ as defined in [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]]. For such a state, let $Q_L=\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$ and define the dimensionless cube entropy per site
$$s(\omega):=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{-\operatorname{Tr}_{Q_L}(\rho_{Q_L}\log\rho_{Q_L})}{L^d},\qquad 0\log0:=0.$$
Under Countable Choice and the full Axiom of Choice [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]], the exact entropy-density supplier [[lem-qsm-stationary-spin-entropy-density]] establishes that this limit exists for every such state and equals the infimum over positive integer cube sides. The corresponding physical entropy density is $k_Bs(\omega)/a^d$, in joules per kelvin per cubic metre for $d=3$. For the translation-invariant finite-range energy interaction, the same supplier defines the energy density per site $u_\Phi(\omega)=\sum_{S\in\mathscr S_\Phi}\omega(\Phi(S))$; it is in joules per site when $\Phi$ is an energy interaction, and $u_\Phi(\omega)/a^d$ is the energy density per physical volume in $d=3$. These thermodynamic limits are restricted to the supplier's stated assumptions and do not assert that a prepared physical material realizes a translation-invariant state.

items.title: KMS equilibrium and local Born quantum spin model
items.statement:
Adopt, for this bounded finite-dimensional quantum spin model, the following physical interpretation and equilibrium rule. A prepared state is a positive normalized functional $\omega$ on the quasi-local observable algebra of [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]]. The model assigns the Born probability $\omega(P)$ to a local projective-measurement outcome represented by a projection $P\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$; the probabilities of the mutually orthogonal spectral projections of a finite-region self-adjoint observable sum to one. For a physical equilibrium preparation at temperature $T>0$, adopt as the model's equilibrium criterion that $\omega$ is a $\beta$-KMS state for the thermodynamic dynamics $\alpha_t$, with $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ and the physical-time strip of width $\beta\hbar$ seconds as in [[def-qsm-kms-state]]. This is an adopted model postulate, not a deduction from the algebraic state definition or from the finite-volume Gibbs identity.

The postulate does not claim that an actual material has the specified interaction parameters, that a system dynamically relaxes to a KMS state, that equilibrium is unique, or that an apparatus realizes a specified projective measurement. It reports no experiment or measured value. Finite-volume approximations, when used, remain distinct from the infinite-volume state and its local restrictions.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §3.4, Definition 3.4.4 and thermal-equilibrium discussion, printed pp. 74–77
David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, Chapter 1 §7 and Chapter 2 §6, printed pp. 13–14 and 24–25

items.physical_scope: An adopted model for bounded finite-dimensional quantum spins on Gamma=Z^d with a specified finite-range interaction, local measurements, and T>0. Actual materials, calibration, thermalization, and empirical uncertainty are outside the postulate.

items.title: Conditional interacting spin dynamics and equilibrium predictions
items.statement:
Let $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, have finite on-site spin dimension $q\ge1$, local algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$, and quasi-local algebra $\mathcal A$ as in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]], [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. Adopt the physical spin-model interpretation and equilibrium criterion of [[post-qsm-infinite-spin-equilibrium]]. Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction as in [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]], with free-boundary $H_\Lambda$ and finite-volume dynamics $\alpha_t^\Lambda(A)=e^{itH_\Lambda/\hbar}Ae^{-itH_\Lambda/\hbar}$. Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C$^*$-identity and state/density-norm interface of [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]], exactly at the stated conditional scope.

Then the thermodynamic dynamics $\alpha_t$ exists as a strongly continuous one-parameter group of isometric $*$-automorphisms of $\mathcal A$. For every fixed $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$, at least one $\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha_t$ exists. This existence conclusion is a model deduction from the stated mathematical hypotheses; the physical postulate adopts KMS as an equilibrium criterion but the theorem does not imply dynamical relaxation, uniqueness, or a global infinite-volume Gibbs density matrix.

For $x,y\in\mathbb Z^d$, write $d_\infty(x,y):=\max_{1\le j\le d}|x_j-y_j|$. For finite $\Lambda$ and $x\in\Lambda$, use $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda):=\min_{y\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda}d_\infty(x,y)$, exactly as in [[thm-qsm-quantum-lattice-pressure]]; its minimum exists because the complement is nonempty and the distances are positive integers.

If, in addition, $\Phi$ is translation invariant in the sense of [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]], then for every sequence of finite nonempty regions $(\Lambda_n)$ satisfying $|\Lambda_n|\to\infty$ and, for each fixed integer $r\ge0$, $|\partial_r\Lambda_n|/|\Lambda_n|\to0$, where $\partial_r\Lambda_n:=\{x\in\Lambda_n:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,\mathbb Z^d\setminus\Lambda_n)\le r\}$, the dimensionless finite-volume log-partition per site
$$p_{\Lambda_n}(\beta):=|\Lambda_n|^{-1}\log\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}(e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}})$$
converges to the same finite $p_\Phi(\beta)$. This is the van Hove condition stated in [[thm-qsm-quantum-lattice-pressure]]. The corresponding model free energy per site $f_\Phi(\beta):=-\beta^{-1}p_\Phi(\beta)=-k_BT p_\Phi(\beta)$ is in joules per site when interaction terms are assigned energy units. The theorem makes no claim about a physical pressure in pascals or the accuracy of a material fit.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §§3.3–3.4, finite-range dynamics and equilibrium states, printed pp. 64–82
David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, Chapter 1 §7 and Chapter 2 §6, printed pp. 13–14 and 24–25
Oscar E. Lanford III and Derek W. Robinson, Statistical Mechanics of Quantum Spin Systems III, Theorem 3.1, printed pp. 332–334

items.physical_scope: Conditional predictions for finite-dimensional on-site spins on Z^d with a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction at positive temperature. Pressure is asserted only for translation-invariant interactions and van Hove sequences; no empirical material identification, thermalization, or uniqueness claim is made.

items.title: Conditional quantum Ising uniqueness and phase predictions
items.statement:
Adopt the model and units of [[def-qsm-infinite-spin-physical-quantities]] and the equilibrium criterion of [[post-qsm-infinite-spin-equilibrium]]. Let $T>0$, $k_B>0$, and $\hbar>0$. Let $Z_i$ be the dimensionless Pauli matrix with eigenvalues $\pm1$ at site $i$, and let the diagonal spin-$\tfrac12$ Ising interaction of [[def-qsm-diagonal-ising-interaction]] have symmetric energy coefficients $J_{ij}=J_{ji}$ and fields $h_i$ in joules, finite range, and a uniform per-site bound. Thus
$$H_\Lambda=-\sum_{i\in\Lambda}h_iZ_i-\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq\Lambda}J_{ij}Z_iZ_j,$$
with each unordered internal pair counted once. Here $|i-j|_1:=\sum_{k=1}^d|i_k-j_k|$ is the lattice $\ell^1$ distance, and $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$.

1. **Sufficient high-temperature uniqueness.** For translation-invariant symmetric pair couplings, a constant finite field $h_i=h$, and
$$\sup_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}\sum_{j\ne i}\tanh\!\left(\frac{|J_{ij}|}{k_BT}\right)<1,$$
the full quasi-local algebra has exactly one $\beta$-KMS state. In the homogeneous nearest-neighbor model this sufficient condition is $2d\tanh(|J|/(k_BT))<1$.

2. **One-dimensional uniqueness.** For $d=1$, uniform nearest-neighbor coupling $J\in\mathbb R$ and constant finite field $h$, every $T>0$ gives exactly one full-algebra $\beta$-KMS state.

3. **Two-dimensional sufficient coexistence.** For $d=2$, uniform nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic coupling $J>0$, zero field, and $T\le J/(2k_B)$, there are at least two distinct spatially translation-invariant full-algebra $\beta$-KMS states $\omega_+$ and $\omega_-$ with opposite nonzero dimensionless magnetizations $\omega_+(Z_i)\ge m_*>0$ and $\omega_-(Z_i)\le-m_*<0$. Here spatial translation invariance means $\omega(\tau_x(A))=\omega(A)$ for every local $A$ and $x\in\mathbb Z^2$, with $\tau_x$ from [[def-qsm-translation-invariant-spin-interaction]]. Put $K=\beta J$, $r=3e^{-2K}$, $\delta(K)=\frac43\frac{r^4(5-4r)}{(1-r)^2}$, and $m_*=1-2\delta(K)$. This is a sufficient coexistence bound; $T=J/(2k_B)$ is not asserted to be the critical temperature, the states are not asserted to be extremal, and no transverse-field result follows.

For the same two-dimensional model with uniform coupling $J$ and variable uniform longitudinal energy coefficient $h$, put
$$H_\Lambda(h)=-J\sum_{\substack{\{i,j\}\subseteq\Lambda\\|i-j|_1=1}}Z_iZ_j-h\sum_{i\in\Lambda}Z_i,$$
where each internal unordered nearest-neighbor pair is counted once. At fixed $\beta$, let $\Lambda_n=[-n,n]^2$ and define the dimensionless log-partition pressure per site
$$p_\beta(h):=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{|\Lambda_n|}\log\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}\!\left(e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}(h)}\right).$$
Under the stated coexistence condition this limit exists, is not differentiable at $h=0$, and satisfies $(p_\beta(h)-p_\beta(0))/h\ge\beta m_*$ for every $h>0$ and $(p_\beta(h)-p_\beta(0))/h\le-\beta m_*$ for every $h<0$. The $p_\beta$ here is dimensionless per site, not a mechanical pressure in pascals.

items.title: Controlled diagonal quantum Ising regimes
items.statement:
Use the homogeneous nearest-neighbor spin-$\tfrac12$ model $H_\Lambda=-J\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq\Lambda,\ |i-j|_1=1}Z_iZ_j-h\sum_{i\in\Lambda}Z_i$, with $J$ and $h$ in joules, $Z_i$ the dimensionless Pauli matrices, and $T>0$. Here $|i-j|_1:=\sum_{k=1}^d|i_k-j_k|$ is the lattice $\ell^1$ distance; each internal unordered nearest-neighbor pair occurs once. The relevant implications are conditional model predictions:

- In one dimension, finite $J,h$ give exactly one full-algebra $\beta$-KMS state for every $T>0$.
- In two dimensions with $h=0$, the strict condition $4\tanh(|J|/(k_BT))<1$ is sufficient for uniqueness.
- In two dimensions with $J>0$, $h=0$, and $T\le J/(2k_B)$, there are at least two translation-invariant $\beta$-KMS states with opposite nonzero magnetizations. For the dimensionless pressure function $p_\beta(h)$ defined by the supplier, the secant slope from zero is at least $\beta m_*$ for every $h>0$ and at most $-\beta m_*$ for every $h<0$, so it has a cusp at zero field.

The last inequality is a conservative sufficient coexistence range; it is not an identified critical temperature. The example does not classify parameters outside the displayed regimes or describe a transverse-field model.

items.title: Symmetric and antisymmetric identical-particle Fock spaces
items.design_state: Batch 45 authoring draft; current prerequisite availability and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $I$ be a specified finite or countably infinite
mode set with a fixed enumeration, and let $\mathfrak h=\ell^2(I)$ have its
coordinate orthonormal basis $(e_j)_{j\in I}$. Put
$\mathfrak h^{\otimes 0}=\mathbb C$, $\mathfrak h^{\otimes 1}=\mathfrak h$,
and define each completed tensor power recursively by
$\mathfrak h^{\otimes(n+1)}=\mathfrak h^{\otimes n}\widehat\otimes\mathfrak h$,
using the first-variable-linear product inner product of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. For $n\ge1$, let
$U_\pi$ permute the tensor factors for $\pi\in S_n$, and let
$$
P_\pm^{(n)}=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\chi_\pm(\pi)U_\pi, \qquad \chi_+(\pi)=1,\quad \chi_-(\pi)=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi),
$$
with $P_\pm^{(0)}=I_{\mathbb C}$. The permutation-sector theorem
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] makes these orthogonal
projections. Define the symmetric and antisymmetric sectors
$\mathcal H_\pm^{(n)}:=\operatorname{ran}P_\pm^{(n)}$. Define
$$
\mathcal F_\pm(\mathfrak h):=\left\{\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\ge0}:\psi_n\in\mathcal H_\pm^{(n)},\ \sum_{n\ge0}\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\}, \qquad \langle\psi,\varphi\rangle:=\sum_{n\ge0}\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle.
$$
The vector $\Omega=(1,0,0,\ldots)$ is the vacuum, and the finite-particle
subspace consists of vectors with only finitely many nonzero components.

This is a mathematical construction for a specified mode basis. Choosing its
symmetric or antisymmetric sector for a physical species is a separate model
postulate. No spin-statistics theorem or physical species assignment is part of
the definition.

references.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Lecture 22, Hilbert Space of Identical Particles
David Tong, Statistical Physics, §§3.5.1 and 3.6.1

items.strategy:
1.1 The tensor factors and product pairing in the Definition are supplied by [F1]. For every $n\ge1$, [F2] makes $P_\pm^{(n)}$ an orthogonal projection. The range of an orthogonal projection is closed: if $P x_k=x_k$ and $x_k\to x$, boundedness of $P$ gives $P x=\lim_k P x_k=\lim_k x_k=x$. Therefore each $\mathcal H_\pm^{(n)}$ is a closed subspace of the complete tensor Hilbert space and is itself complete. [given, A1, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 For $\psi,\varphi\in\mathcal F_\pm(\mathfrak h)$, Cauchy–Schwarz for the square-summable nonnegative sequences $(\|\psi_n\|)_n$ and $(\|\varphi_n\|)_n$ gives
$\sum_n|\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle|\le(\sum_n\|\psi_n\|^2)^{1/2}(\sum_n\|\varphi_n\|^2)^{1/2}<\infty$. Hence the displayed pairing converges absolutely, is sesquilinear, and is positive definite because $\langle\psi,\psi\rangle=\sum_n\|\psi_n\|^2=0$ forces every coordinate to vanish. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 Let $(\psi^{(k)})_k$ be Cauchy in this norm. For each fixed $n$, $(\psi_n^{(k)})_k$ is Cauchy in the complete sector $\mathcal H_\pm^{(n)}$, so it converges to some $\psi_n\in\mathcal H_\pm^{(n)}$. If $k\ge K$ and $\|\psi^{(k)}-\psi^{(m)}\|\le\varepsilon$ for all $m\ge K$, then for every finite $N$, passing $m\to\infty$ in the finite sum yields $\sum_{n\le N}\|\psi_n-\psi_n^{(k)}\|^2\le\varepsilon^2$. Also $\sum_{n\le N}\|\psi_n\|^2\le2\|\psi^{(k)}\|^2+2\varepsilon^2$. Taking suprema over finite $N$ proves $\sum_n\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty$, so $\psi\in\mathcal F_\pm(\mathfrak h)$, and then $\|\psi^{(k)}-\psi\|\le\varepsilon$ for all $k\ge K$. Thus the direct sum is complete. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 For $\psi\in\mathcal F_\pm(\mathfrak h)$, truncating after sector $N$ changes its squared norm by $\sum_{n>N}\|\psi_n\|^2\to0$. Therefore the finite-particle subspace is dense and $\Omega$ is a unit vector. [step 1.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Occupation bases and actual CCR/CAR domains
items.design_state: Batch 45 authoring draft; current prerequisite availability and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Let $I$ and $\mathcal F_\pm(\ell^2(I))$ be as in
[[def-qsm-identical-particle-fock-sectors]]. Define
$$
\Omega_B:=\{m:I\to\mathbb N_0:m\text{ has finite support}\},\qquad \Omega_F:=\{m:I\to\{0,1\}:m\text{ has finite support}\}.
$$
For either statistics choice, write $|m|=\sum_jm_j$. If $m\in\Omega_B$, choose the elementary tensor $x_m$ containing $m_j$ copies of each mode $j$ in the fixed order and set
$$
|m\rangle_B:=\sqrt{\frac{|m|!}{\prod_jm_j!}}\,P_+^{(|m|)}x_m.
$$
If $m\in\Omega_F$, list its occupied modes increasingly in the fixed enumeration, let $x_m$ be their elementary tensor and set
$$
|m\rangle_F:=\sqrt{|m|!}\,P_-^{(|m|)}x_m.
$$
For $|m|=0$, both vectors are the vacuum. These vectors form orthonormal bases and define unitary identifications $\mathcal F_+(\ell^2(I))\cong\ell^2(\Omega_B)$ and $\mathcal F_-(\ell^2(I))\cong\ell^2(\Omega_F)$.

On the finite-support span $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ of the bosonic basis, define
$$
a_j|m\rangle_B=\sqrt{m_j}|m-\mathbf1_j\rangle_B,\qquad a_j^\dagger|m\rangle_B=\sqrt{m_j+1}|m+\mathbf1_j\rangle_B,
$$
where the annihilation term is zero when $m_j=0$. Their maximal closed extensions have domains
$$
D(a_j)=\left\{c:\sum_{m\in\Omega_B}m_j|c_m|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad D(a_j^\dagger)=\left\{c:\sum_{m\in\Omega_B}(m_j+1)|c_m|^2<\infty\right\},
$$
and $a_j^\dagger=a_j^*$. On $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$, they satisfy
$[a_i,a_j^\dagger]=\delta_{ij}I$, $[a_i,a_j]=0$, and $[a_i^\dagger,a_j^\dagger]=0$.

On the fermionic basis define
$$
c_j|m\rangle_F=(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}m_i}m_j|m-\mathbf1_j\rangle_F,\qquad c_j^\dagger|m\rangle_F=(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}m_i}(1-m_j)|m+\mathbf1_j\rangle_F.
$$
These operators are bounded on the full fermionic Fock space and satisfy
$\{c_i,c_j^\dagger\}=\delta_{ij}I$ and $\{c_i,c_j\}=\{c_i^\dagger,c_j^\dagger\}=0$. These are mathematical sector relations; they do not select a physical species or imply a spin-statistics theorem.

references.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Lecture 22, Hilbert Space of Identical Particles
David Tong, Statistical Physics, §§3.5.1 and 3.6.1

items.strategy:
1.1 Let $n=|m|$. In the bosonic permutation average $P_+^{(n)}x_m$, each distinct product word with occupation profile $m$ occurs $\prod_jm_j!$ times out of $n!$ permutations. Therefore $$ P_+^{(n)}x_m=\frac{\prod_jm_j!}{n!}\sum_{w\in\mathcal W(m)}w, \qquad |\mathcal W(m)|=\frac{n!}{\prod_jm_j!}. $$ The product words are orthonormal by [F1], so the squared norm of this average is $\prod_jm_j!/n!$; the prefactor in $|m\rangle_B$ makes its norm one. Distinct occupation profiles have disjoint word supports, hence their vectors are orthogonal. [given, F1, algebra]

1.2 If a fermionic list repeats a mode, [F2] makes its antisymmetrization zero; $\Omega_F$ excludes these profiles. For distinct occupied modes, the $n!$ permuted product words are distinct orthonormal vectors with coefficients $\pm1/n!$, so $\|P_-^{(n)}x_m\|^2=1/n!$. The prefactor $\sqrt{n!}$ normalizes the vector. Distinct occupied subsets have disjoint product-word support and are orthogonal. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 The fixed enumeration identifies a finite-support configuration with a finite sequence of natural indices and finitely many nonnegative integer labels (or bits); the union over all finite sequence lengths is countable. Thus $\Omega_B$ and $\Omega_F$ are countable and their $\ell^2$ coordinate descriptions are well defined. [given, algebra]

1.4 On the bosonic basis, shifting the coordinate index gives $\|a_jc\|^2=\sum_m m_j|c_m|^2$ and $\|a_j^\dagger c\|^2=\sum_m(m_j+1)|c_m|^2$. Hence the stated weighted domains are exactly the domains on which the shifted coefficient sequences lie in $\ell^2$. If $c^{(r)}\to c$ and either shifted sequence converges in $\ell^2$, coordinate convergence shows the limiting output has the same weighted-shift coordinates; its square summability puts $c$ in the displayed domain. Thus both maximal shifts are closed. Testing the adjoint identity against each basis vector forces the reverse weighted shift [F3], while Cauchy--Schwarz gives the converse pairing bound [F4]. Truncating to finite initial sets of configurations makes the weighted tails tend to zero in graph norm, so $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is a core for both shifts under the graph definition in [F3]. [given, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 Product words span a dense subspace of each tensor power by [F1]. Applying the bounded projections $P_\pm^{(n)}$ to that dense span gives a dense subspace of each projected sector. Every projected product word is either zero or a scalar multiple of the corresponding occupation vector from steps 1.1–1.2. Thus the occupation vectors are complete in each sector and, after taking the direct sum over $n$, form orthonormal bases of the Fock spaces. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, algebra]

2.2 For $i=j$, direct action on $|m\rangle_B$ gives $a_ja_j^\dagger|m\rangle_B=(m_j+1)|m\rangle_B$ and $a_j^\dagger a_j|m\rangle_B=m_j|m\rangle_B$. For $i\ne j$, both orders of distinct coordinate shifts give the same coefficient and same occupation vector, so the shifts commute; the same direct coordinate calculation applies to two annihilators and two creators. This proves the CCR on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$, without asserting that unbounded commutators are defined on all Fock space. [step 1.4, algebra]

3.1 Each fermionic shift maps a subset of an orthonormal basis into another orthonormal subset with coefficients of modulus at most one, so it is a contraction on the finite span and extends boundedly. For distinct $i,j$, the two orders in any CAR anticommutator are either both zero or have equal magnitudes and opposite signs: toggling the earlier mode changes by one the number of occupied modes preceding the later index. For $i=j$, if $m_j=0$ then $c_jc_j^\dagger|m\rangle_F=|m\rangle_F$ and $c_j^\dagger c_j|m\rangle_F=0$; if $m_j=1$ the roles reverse. The other same-mode anticommutators vanish. Thus all CAR identities hold on the basis span and extend by boundedness to the whole Fock space. [given, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Explicit diagonal Fock domains and occupation trace
items.design_state: Batch 45 authoring draft; current prerequisite availability and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $I$ be finite or countably infinite with a specified enumeration, let $m\in\Omega_\pm$ be the occupation configurations of [[lem-qsm-fock-occupation-basis-and-car-relations]], and let $\epsilon_j\in\mathbb R$ be finite mode energies. For each finite-support configuration put
$$
E(m):=\sum_j\epsilon_jm_j,\qquad N(m):=|m|=\sum_jm_j.
$$
These are finite sums. On $\ell^2(\Omega_\pm)$, define the real diagonal multipliers
$$
D(H)=\left\{c:\sum_mE(m)^2|c_m|^2<\infty\right\},\quad (Hc)_m=E(m)c_m,
$$
$$
D(N)=\left\{c:\sum_m|m|^2|c_m|^2<\infty\right\},\quad (Nc)_m=|m|c_m,
$$
and, for $\mu\in\mathbb R$,
$$
D(K_\mu)=\left\{c:\sum_m|E(m)-\mu|m||^2|c_m|^2<\infty\right\},\quad (K_\mu c)_m=(E(m)-\mu|m|)c_m.
$$
Each is self-adjoint on its displayed domain. No equality between $D(K_\mu)$ and $D(H)\cap D(N)$ is asserted.

For $\beta>0$, set $q_j=e^{-\beta(\epsilon_j-\mu)}$. In the bosonic case assume
$$
0<q_j<1,\qquad q_*:=\sup_jq_j<1,\qquad \sum_jq_j<\infty;
$$
Here $q_*=0$ by convention when $I$ is empty; for nonempty $I$ the displayed supremum is unchanged. In the fermionic case assume $q_j>0$, $\sum_jq_j<\infty$, and only finitely many gaps $\epsilon_j-\mu$ are negative. Define the positive diagonal multiplier $G_{\beta,\mu}$ by $G_{\beta,\mu}|m\rangle=e^{-\beta(E(m)-\mu|m|)}|m\rangle$. Then $G_{\beta,\mu}$ is trace class, with
$$
\Xi_B=\operatorname{Tr}G_{\beta,\mu}=\prod_j(1-q_j)^{-1}<\infty,\qquad \Xi_F=\operatorname{Tr}G_{\beta,\mu}=\prod_j(1+q_j)<\infty.
$$
Thus $\rho_{\beta,\mu}=\Xi^{-1}G_{\beta,\mu}$ is a positive trace-class operator of trace one. Its finite-mode marginals are independent: bosonic occupation $n_j\in\mathbb N_0$ has law $(1-q_j)q_j^{n_j}$, and fermionic occupation $n_j\in\{0,1\}$ has probabilities $(1+q_j)^{-1}$ and $q_j(1+q_j)^{-1}$. In particular
$$
\mathbb E_BN_j=\frac{q_j}{1-q_j},\quad \operatorname{Var}_B(N_j)=\frac{q_j}{(1-q_j)^2},\qquad \mathbb E_FN_j=\frac{q_j}{1+q_j},\quad \operatorname{Var}_F(N_j)=\frac{q_j}{(1+q_j)^2}.
$$
The total number has finite mean and variance under the stated mode conditions. The trace hypotheses alone do not imply finite energy moments or differentiability in $\beta,\mu$.

For an additional compact-parameter envelope, the corresponding response identities hold. For fixed $\mu$, if for every compact $B\subset J\subset(0,\infty)$ a summable $(a_m)$ satisfies $(1+|E(m)-\mu|m||^2)e^{-\beta(E(m)-\mu|m|)}\le a_m$ for all $m$ and $\beta\in B$, then $-\partial_\beta\log\Xi=\mathbb E(K_\mu)$ and $\partial_\beta^2\log\Xi=\operatorname{Var}(K_\mu)$. If $(\beta,\mu)$ varies over an open set and a summable compact-parameter envelope dominates $e^{-\beta(E(m)-\mu|m|)}(1+|E(m)|^2+|m|^2)$, then at fixed $\beta$, $\partial_\mu\mathbb E(N)=\beta\operatorname{Var}(N)$ and $\partial_\mu\mathbb E(E)=\beta\operatorname{Cov}(E,N)$. These stronger moment envelopes are additional hypotheses, not consequences of trace-class normalization.

For a finite mode set $J$, the canonical fixed-number coefficients are defined by
$$
\prod_{j\in J}(1-ze^{-\beta\epsilon_j})^{-1}=\sum_{N\ge0}Z_{B,N}(J)z^N,\qquad \prod_{j\in J}(1+ze^{-\beta\epsilon_j})=\sum_{N=0}^{|J|}Z_{F,N}(J)z^N.
$$
Each coefficient is the sum of the Boltzmann weights over the corresponding number sector; for a countable mode set it is the increasing limit over finite mode sets and is finite under the stated grand-trace hypotheses. A fixed-number law is the grand law conditioned on total number, so its occupations are generally coupled. The oscillator specialization uses the actual one-particle Hermite basis and diagonal domain of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]], not a formal differential eigenfunction list.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, §§3.4–3.6.2
Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Lectures 22–25

items.strategy:
1.1 The configuration set $\Omega_\pm$ is countable by [F1]. Every $m$ has finite support, so the sums defining $E(m)$ and $|m|$ are finite real sums. The finite-support vectors form a dense subspace of $\ell^2(\Omega_\pm)$. [given, F1, A1]

1.2 If $I$ is empty, its only occupation configuration is the vacuum: $E=N=K_\mu=0$, $G=I$ on $\mathbb C$, $\Xi=1$ and $\rho=1$. The empty products are one, the total number has mean and variance zero, and every stated parameter derivative is zero; the convention $q_*=0$ makes the bosonic hypotheses valid. For a finite mode set $J$, summing the positive diagonal weights independently over each bosonic coordinate gives $\prod_{j\in J}\sum_{n\ge0}q_j^n=\prod_{j\in J}(1-q_j)^{-1}$. In the fermionic case each coordinate has only two values and contributes $1+q_j$. This proves the finite-mode trace products. [given, A1, algebra]

1.3 For a fixed $\mu$, the countable configuration model has weights $e^{-\beta(E(m)-\mu|m|)}$ and degeneracies one. Under the compact $\beta$-envelope in the Statement, [F2]–[F3] apply to this exact countable index set and energy $K_\mu(m)$, giving the displayed beta-derivative identities and finite moments. The envelope is stronger than trace finiteness and is stated separately. [F2, F3, A1]

1.4 For joint $(\beta,\mu)$ response, put $X_1(m)=E(m)$, $X_2(m)=|m|$, and natural parameter $\theta=(-\beta,\beta\mu)$. The map $(\beta,\mu)\mapsto\theta$ is a smooth bijection onto its open image for $\beta>0$, with nonzero Jacobian. The stated joint envelope is exactly the required second-moment envelope for [F5]; differentiating at fixed $\beta$ gives $\partial_\mu\mathbb E(N)=\beta\operatorname{Var}(N)$ and $\partial_\mu\mathbb E(E)=\beta\operatorname{Cov}(E,N)$. [F5, A1, algebra]

2.1 Let $D_\lambda$ multiply the coordinate $c_m$ by a real number $\lambda_m$, on the domain $\sum_m\lambda_m^2|c_m|^2<\infty$. Testing the adjoint identity on each coordinate vector forces the adjoint coordinates to be $\lambda_m c_m$, so $D(D_\lambda^*)$ is exactly this weighted $\ell^2$ domain by [F8]. Conversely, on that domain Cauchy–Schwarz makes the coordinate pairing bounded and identifies the adjoint action with the same multiplier. Apply this argument to $\lambda_m=E(m)$, $|m|$, and $E(m)-\mu|m|$; all three displayed operators are self-adjoint. [step 1.1, A1, F8, algebra]

2.2 Enumerate a countable mode set by increasing finite initial sets $J_M$. Their finite-support configuration sets increase to $\Omega_\pm$, so the full nonnegative trace sum is the increasing limit of the finite-mode sums. For bosons, $-\log(1-q_j)=\int_0^{q_j}(1-u)^{-1}du\le q_j/(1-q_*)$, hence $\sum_j-\log(1-q_j)<\infty$. For fermions, $\log(1+q_j)\le q_j$, hence $\sum_j\log(1+q_j)<\infty$. The products therefore have finite positive limits and equal the full diagonal trace sums; the negative fermionic gaps are finite by hypothesis, and each has finite weight. [step 1.2, A1, algebra]

3.1 If $\Omega_\pm$ is infinite, enumerate it as $m_1,m_2,\ldots$ and let $G_M$ retain the first $M$ diagonal entries of $G_{\beta,\mu}$; in the finite case take the full finite sum. Each $G_M$ has finite rank and hence is compact. Since the omitted entries are nonnegative and summable, their supremum is bounded by their sum, so $\|G_{\beta,\mu}-G_M\|\le\sum_{r>M}e^{-\beta(E(m_r)-\mu|m_r|)}\to0$. The norm-limit theorem therefore makes $G_{\beta,\mu}$ compact. It is positive diagonal and satisfies $G_{\beta,\mu}^*G_{\beta,\mu}=G_{\beta,\mu}^2$; uniqueness of its compact positive square root gives $|G_{\beta,\mu}|=G_{\beta,\mu}$. Its singular values are the nonnegative diagonal entries with multiplicity, whose sum is $\Xi<\infty$. Thus [F7] and the trace-class definition make it trace class and give $\operatorname{Tr}G_{\beta,\mu}=\Xi$. Dividing by $\Xi>0$ gives a positive trace-class operator of trace one. [step 2.2, F1, F7, A1, algebra]

3.2 Fix one mode $j$, and take increasing finite mode sets $J_M$ containing it. For bosons, the trace weight of configurations in $J_M$ with occupation $n$ at $j$ is $q_j^n\prod_{i\in J_M\setminus\{j\}}(1-q_i)^{-1}$; division by the total finite trace gives $(1-q_j)q_j^n$. For fermions the same calculation gives probability $q_j^n/(1+q_j)$, for $n\in\{0,1\}$. Taking increasing limits of the nonnegative configuration sums preserves these factorizations, because every finite-support configuration is eventually included and the finite products converge by step 2.2. Factoring over any fixed finite list of modes gives the product joint law, hence independence of finite collections in this diagonal grand state. [step 1.2, step 2.2, A1, algebra]

3.3 For finite $J$, multiplying the geometric series in each bosonic coordinate gives the coefficient identity for $Z_{B,N}(J)$; multiplying the two-term polynomials in each fermionic coordinate gives the identity for $Z_{F,N}(J)$. Each coefficient sums exactly the finite canonical Boltzmann weights with total occupation $N$. For countable $I$, increasing finite mode sets increase each coefficient to its sum over all finite-support configurations; for any admissible fugacity $z=e^{\beta\mu}>0$, nonnegativity gives $z^N Z_{\pm,N}\le\Xi$, hence $Z_{\pm,N}\le z^{-N}\Xi<\infty$, and a canonical density exists exactly when the coefficient is positive. Conditioning the grand law on $|m|=N$ multiplies by the indicator of that constraint and generally couples the mode occupations. [step 2.2, A1, algebra]

4.1 If $0<q_j<1$, [F4] gives the stated Bose and Fermi means and variances. For a fermionic mode with $q_j\ge1$, direct summation of its two probabilities gives $\mathbb E N_j=q_j/(1+q_j)$ and $\operatorname{Var}(N_j)=q_j/(1+q_j)^2$; no geometric-series claim is used there. The bosonic bounds $\mathbb E N_j\le q_j/(1-q_*)$ and $\operatorname{Var}(N_j)\le q_j/(1-q_*)^2$, and the fermionic bounds $\mathbb E N_j\le q_j$ and $\operatorname{Var}(N_j)\le q_j$, are summable. For finite initial mode sets, independence from step 3.2 gives $\mathbb E N_M=\sum_{j\in J_M}\mathbb E N_j$ and $\mathbb E N_M^2=\sum_{j\in J_M}\operatorname{Var}(N_j)+(\sum_{j\in J_M}\mathbb E N_j)^2$. Each configuration has finite support, so $N_M\uparrow N$; passing to the increasing limits of the defining nonnegative countable sums yields finite $\mathbb E N$ and $\mathbb E N^2$, with $\operatorname{Var}(N)=\sum_j\operatorname{Var}(N_j)<\infty$. [F4, step 3.2, A1, algebra]

5.1 In the one-dimensional oscillator specialization, [F6] supplies the Hermite eigenbasis, energy list and exact diagonal domain; substitution of those eigenvalues into the Fock multiplier gives the stated occupation construction. This uses the actual self-adjoint oscillator carrier rather than a formal differential eigenfunction list. [F6, A1] ∎

items.title: Lattice Gaussian Riemann limits and the singular Bose endpoint
items.design_state: Batch 45 authoring draft; current prerequisite availability and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]).
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $\alpha,\beta>0$, and $h>0$. Define
$F_B(p)=(e^{\beta\alpha|p|^2}-1)^{-1}$ for $p\ne0$ and
$F_F(p)=(e^{\beta(\alpha|p|^2-\mu)}+1)^{-1}$ for finite $\mu\in\mathbb R$.
For each $\mu<0$, both $F_B(\cdot;\mu)=(e^{\beta(\alpha|p|^2-\mu)}-1)^{-1}$ and $F_F$ are continuous, and for every fixed integer $s\ge0$ their polynomially weighted lattice sums converge with
$$h^d\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}|hk|^sF(hk)\longrightarrow\int_{\mathbb R^d}|p|^sF(p)\,dp\quad(h\downarrow0).$$
The convergence is uniform when $(\beta,\mu)$ ranges over a compact subset of $\{\beta>0,\mu<0\}$ for bosons or $\{\beta>0,\mu\in\mathbb R\}$ for fermions. At the Bose endpoint $\mu=0$, define $F_B(p;0)=(e^{\beta\alpha|p|^2}-1)^{-1}$ for $p\ne0$. For every fixed $\beta,\alpha>0$ and $d\ge1$, monotone convergence gives $\int F_B(p;\mu)\,dp\uparrow\int F_B(p;0)\,dp$ as $\mu\uparrow0$, where the extended endpoint value is
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}F_B(p;0)\,dp=(\pi/(\beta\alpha))^{d/2}\sum_{\ell=1}^\infty\ell^{-d/2}\in(0,+\infty].$$
It is finite exactly when $d>2$. In that case the missing-origin lattice sums satisfy
$$h^d\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}}F_B(hk;0)\longrightarrow\int_{\mathbb R^d}F_B(p;0)\,dp\qquad(h\downarrow0).$$
No value is assigned to $F_B(0;0)$.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, §§3.5–3.6, thermodynamic momentum integrals and Bose/Fermi occupations
Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Lectures 23–25, quantum gases and Bose condensation

items.strategy:
1.1 For $\mu<0$, the Bose denominator is bounded below by $e^{\beta(-\mu)}-1>0$ on compact sets; for finite $\mu$, the Fermi denominator is at least $1$. At large $|p|$, each occupation is bounded by $C e^{-c|p|^2}$ for positive constants $C,c$ depending on a compact parameter neighborhood. A polynomial factor $|p|^s$ is absorbed by a slower Gaussian because $r^s e^{-c r^2/2}$ is bounded on $[0,\infty)$. Thus the continuum integrands and their polynomially weighted tails are integrable by comparison with products of one dimensional Gaussians and Tonelli [F3,F1]. For each fixed $h>0$, the max-norm shell $|k|_\infty=n$ has at most $C_dn^{d-1}$ points, and its summand is bounded by a fixed polynomial in $n$ times $e^{-c h^2n^2}$; the ratio of successive polynomial-Gaussian terms is eventually below a constant less than one, proving every lattice sum is finite. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

1.2 At $\mu=0$ and $p\ne0$, $e^x-1\ge x$ gives $F_B(p)\le(\beta\alpha|p|^2)^{-1}$. If $|k|_\infty=n$, the number of integer lattice points in that shell is $(2n+1)^d-(2n-1)^d\le C_dn^{d-1}$, while $|k|\ge n$. Hence for $0<h\le\delta$, $h^d\sum_{0<|hk|\le\delta}F_B(hk)\le C h^{d-2}\sum_{n\le\delta/h}n^{d-3}\le C'\delta^{d-2}$ when $d>2$; the last estimate follows by comparison on each unit interval with the integral of $x^{d-3}$ (and for $d=3$ the sum is bounded by a constant times $\delta/h$). The continuum small-ball integral has the same bound by decomposing into dyadic annuli, each with volume at most a constant times its radius to power $d$. [given, F2, F5, algebra]

2.1 On a fixed compact cube, uniform continuity of $|p|^sF(p)$ implies that replacing its value on each mesh cube by its value at the lattice corner changes the integral by at most the cube volume times the common modulus of continuity; summing finitely many cubes makes this error tend to zero. The measure of each mesh cube is $h^d$ by [F5]. This proves convergence on compact cubes. [step 1.1, F5, algebra]

3.1 To control tails uniformly for $0<h\le1$, let $Q_{k,h}=hk+[-h/2,h/2]^d$. For $p\in Q_{k,h}$, $|hk|^2\ge |p|^2/2-dh^2/4$. The Gaussian bound from step 1.1 therefore bounds each weighted lattice summand times $h^d$ by a fixed constant times the integral of a slower Gaussian over $Q_{k,h}$; the polynomial weight is absorbed by reducing its exponent once more. Cubes whose centers satisfy $|hk|>R$ lie outside the ball of radius $R-\sqrt d/2$. The integral of the slower Gaussian on that exterior tends to zero as $R\to\infty$, by [F1,F3]. Compact convergence from step 2.1 and this uniform tail bound prove the stated full-space limit and finiteness of every lattice sum. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, F3, algebra]

4.1 Outside any fixed ball around zero, $F_B$ is continuous and has Gaussian tails, so the compact-annulus and tail argument in steps 2.1 and 3.1 applies.
