Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the inherited Bose occupation-space construction.

For the Fermi atom of [[pthm-qsm-onsite-interacting-atoms]], set $h=0$, $\mu=\epsilon$, and $U>0$. Then $\Xi_F=3+e^{-\beta U}$ and $\operatorname{Cov}(n_\uparrow,n_\downarrow)=(e^{-\beta U}-1)/(3+e^{-\beta U})^2<0$. For the Bose site, set $\mu=\epsilon+U$ with $U>0$; the two zero-temperature minimizing occupations are $1$ and $2$, each with limiting Gibbs probability $1/2$, and the entropy tends to $k_B\log2$.

references.title: Immanuel Bloch, Jean Dalibard, and Wilhelm Zwerger, Many-body physics with ultracold gases, §§IV.A and IV.E

items.physical_scope: A symmetric-parameter instance of the finite Fermi atom and a single Bose zero-temperature boundary in the isolated onsite models. No lattice or material-specific conclusion is drawn.
items.strategy:
1.1 Substituting $h=0$ and $\mu=\epsilon$ into the Fermi weights gives $w_\uparrow=w_\downarrow=1$, $w_2=e^{-\beta U}$, and $\Xi_F=3+e^{-\beta U}$. Since $U,\beta>0$, $e^{-\beta U}<1$, so [F1] gives the strictly negative covariance stated in the Example. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 In the Bose result of [F1], set $r=1$ and $\mu=\epsilon+U$. The adjacent minimizing occupations are $1,2$, their limiting probabilities are $1/2,1/2$, and the binary entropy is $-k_B(2)(1/2)\log(1/2)=k_B\log2$. [given, F1, algebra] ∎

row.title: Trace-class bounded-observable response

items.title: Banach-space Volterra and Dyson series with a norm remainder
items.design_state: A-page mathematical helper: the shared Banach/trace-norm/Dyson existence and remainder result used by the normal, finite-matrix, and algebraic response consumers.
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a complex Banach space, let $T>0$, and let $\mathcal B(X)$ be the bounded complex-linear operators on $X$ with the operator norm. Let $K:[0,T]\to\mathcal B(X)$ be strongly continuous, meaning $t\mapsto K(t)x$ is norm-continuous for every fixed $x\in X$. Suppose a continuous function $a:[0,T]\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $\|K(t)\|\le a(t)$. Set $c_T=\int_0^T a(s)\,ds$, where the scalar integral is the Riemann integral. Define $\Delta_0(t)=x_0$ and recursively $\Delta_n(t)=\int_0^t K(s)\Delta_{n-1}(s)\,ds$ for $n\ge1$, using the norm-Riemann integral in $X$.

For each $\epsilon\in\mathbb C$, the series $x_\epsilon(t)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\epsilon^n\Delta_n(t)$ converges uniformly on $[0,T]$. It is the unique continuously differentiable solution of $x_\epsilon'(t)=\epsilon K(t)x_\epsilon(t)$ and $x_\epsilon(0)=x_0$, and

$$\left\|x_\epsilon(t)-x_0-\epsilon\int_0^tK(s)x_0\,ds\right\|\le \|x_0\|\frac{(|\epsilon|c_T)^2e^{|\epsilon|c_T}}{2}.$$

If $X$ is a unital complex $C^*$-algebra and $K(t)x=b(t)x$ for a norm-continuous curve $b:[0,T]\to X$ of skew-adjoint elements, then for real $\epsilon$ the solution with $x_0=1$ is unitary. If $X=\mathcal H$ is a complex Hilbert space and each $K(t)$ is a bounded skew-adjoint operator, then for real $\epsilon$ the solution operators $W_\epsilon(t):x_0\mapsto x_\epsilon(t)$ are unitary even when $K(t)$ is only strongly continuous.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, complete lecture notes, §3.3.11–3.3.12
MIT OpenCourseWare 8.512, Theory of Solids II, Lecture 1: Linear Response Theory, §§1.1–1.2

items.title: Finite matrix trace-norm ideal inequalities
items.design_state: A-page mathematical helper: finite trace-norm ideal and trace bounds used by the exact finite-time matrix response.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$. For a matrix $X$ define $|X|=(X^*X)^{1/2}$ by finite Hermitian functional calculus and define its trace norm by $\|X\|_1=\operatorname{Tr}|X|$. This is a complete norm on the finite-dimensional matrix space. For all matrices $X,Y$,
$$
\|YX\|_1\le\|Y\|\|X\|_1,\qquad \|XY\|_1\le\|Y\|\|X\|_1,\qquad |\operatorname{Tr}X|\le\|X\|_1.
$$
For unitary $U$, $\|UXU^*\|_1=\|X\|_1$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, author-hosted manuscript, Chapter 2, §§2.1–2.3
Mehran Kardar, Statistical Mechanics I, MIT OpenCourseWare, Lecture 21: Quantum Microstates and Quantum Macrostates

items.title: Lorentzian kernels converge to delta and principal-value distributions
items.design_state: New A-page intermediate result: the test-function proof of the Lorentzian delta and principal-value limits required by the spectral fluctuation–response theorem.
items.statement:
Let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be continuously differentiable with compact support. For $\eta>0$, define $P_\eta(x)=\eta/(x^2+\eta^2)$ and $Q_\eta(x)=x/(x^2+\eta^2)$. Define
$$\operatorname{PV}\!\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\psi(x)}x\,dx:=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\int_{|x|>\delta}\frac{\psi(x)}x\,dx$$
when this symmetric limit exists. Then
$$\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\int_{\mathbb R}P_\eta(x)\psi(x)\,dx=\pi\psi(0),\qquad\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\int_{\mathbb R}Q_\eta(x)\psi(x)\,dx=\operatorname{PV}\!\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\psi(x)}x\,dx.$$
Thus $P_\eta$ converges distributionally to $\pi\delta_0$, and $Q_\eta$ converges distributionally to the Cauchy principal-value distribution $\operatorname{PV}(1/x)$, with the stated test-function convention.

references.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 8.512, Theory of Solids II, Lecture 1: Linear Response Theory, §1.3
Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), §2, printed pp. 574–575

items.title: Stationary-state covariance identity for time-integrated observables
items.design_state: New A-page intermediate result: the stationary C*-state double-integral identity and positive covariance matrix required by the Green–Kubo limit.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital complex C$^*$-algebra, and let $(\alpha_t)_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a group of $*$-automorphisms of $\mathcal A$, so $\alpha_0=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$ and $\alpha_{s+t}=\alpha_s\circ\alpha_t$. Assume point-norm continuity: for each $X\in\mathcal A$, the orbit map $t\mapsto\alpha_t(X)$ is norm-continuous. Let $\phi:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ be a bounded linear functional with $\phi(I)=1$, $\phi(X^*X)\ge0$ for every $X\in\mathcal A$, and $\phi\circ\alpha_t=\phi$ for every $t$. For $m\ge1$, take self-adjoint $V_1,\ldots,V_m\in\mathcal A$ with $\phi(V_a)=0$. For $T>0$, define the norm-Riemann integrals
$$X_{a,T}=\int_0^T\alpha_t(V_a)\,dt,$$
and for $s\ge0$ define
$$G_{ab}(s)=\frac12\left(\operatorname{Re}\phi(V_a\alpha_s(V_b))+\operatorname{Re}\phi(V_b\alpha_s(V_a))\right).$$
Then each $X_{a,T}$ is self-adjoint and
$$\frac{1}{2T}\operatorname{Re}\phi(X_{a,T}X_{b,T})=\int_0^T\left(1-\frac{s}{T}\right)G_{ab}(s)\,ds.$$
The real symmetric matrix with entries on the left is positive semidefinite.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §3.3.12, printed pp. 69–71
Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), §3, printed p. 575

items.title: Trace-class bounded-observable response
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T4 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, let $H=H^*$ be a densely defined operator with domain $D(H)$, and let $\hbar>0$. Put $U_0(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$. Let $\rho$ be a density operator, meaning a positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$ as in [[def-qsm-density-trace-state]], and assume $\rho U_0(t)=U_0(t)\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. Let $A,B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ be bounded self-adjoint operators, let $T>0$ be a finite time in s, let $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and let $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless. Interpret $H$ in J, $\hbar$ in J s, and $h(t)B$ in J; if $A,B$ carry units $[A],[B]$, then $R_{AB}$ has units $[A][B]/(\mathrm J\,\mathrm s)$.

Define $B_s=U_0(s)^*BU_0(s)$, $\alpha_t(A)=U_0(t)^*AU_0(t)$, and
$$
R_{AB}(u)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\rho[\alpha_u(A),B]\right),\qquad C_T=\frac2{\hbar}\int_0^T|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds.
$$
The trace-class interaction-picture solution of $\rho_I'(t)=\frac{i\epsilon h(t)}{\hbar}[B_t,\rho_I(t)]$, $\rho_I(0)=\rho$, satisfies
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_I(t)\alpha_t(A))=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\alpha_t(A))+\epsilon\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds+r_\epsilon(t),
$$
where $|r_\epsilon(t)|\le\|A\|(|\epsilon|C_T)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_T}/2$ for $0\le t\le T$. Thus the bounded-observable first variation is exact, with an explicit finite-time remainder. No energy or entropy moment of $\rho$ is assumed, and no trace of an unbounded product such as $\rho H A$ is used.

references.title: Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), §2
MIT OpenCourseWare 8.512, Theory of Solids II, Lecture 1: Linear Response Theory, §§1.1–1.2
Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, complete lecture notes, §3.3.11–3.3.12

items.title: Finite unitary dynamics and stationary Gibbs states
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T0 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$, let $H=H^*$ be a Hamiltonian with energy unit J, and let $\hbar>0$ have unit J s. A **finite density matrix** is a positive semidefinite matrix $\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. For time $t\in\mathbb R$ measured in s, set $U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ and $\alpha_t(A)=U(t)^*AU(t)$. Then $U(t)$ is a unitary group, $\alpha_t$ is a group of matrix $*$-automorphisms, and for every finite density matrix $\rho$ and matrix $A$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}(U(t)\rho U(t)^*A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\alpha_t(A)).$$

The von Neumann entropy $S(\rho)=-k_B\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)$ is finite and unchanged by $U(t)\rho U(t)^*$. For $\beta>0$ with unit J$^{-1}$, let $Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})$ and $\sigma_\beta=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H}$. Then $Z_\beta>0$, $\sigma_\beta$ is stationary, and the finite Gibbs correlation has the KMS strip identity

$$F_{A,B}(t+i\beta\hbar)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta\alpha_t(B)A),\qquad F_{A,B}(z)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta A\alpha_z(B)),$$

where $\alpha_z(B)=e^{izH/\hbar}Be^{-izH/\hbar}$. The function $F_{A,B}$ is entire and bounded on $0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le\beta\hbar$. This finite-dimensional result asserts no approach to equilibrium.

references.title: Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), §§2–3
MIT OpenCourseWare 8.512, Theory of Solids II, Lecture 1: Linear Response Theory, §1.1

items.title: Finite Cesaro dephasing with degenerate energy blocks
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T0 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Under the finite-dimensional unitary dynamics of [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-unitary]], let $P_E$ be the orthogonal spectral projection of $H$ for its distinct energy $E$. For every density matrix $\rho$,

$$\frac1T\int_0^T U(t)\rho U(t)^*\,dt\longrightarrow\sum_E P_E\rho P_E$$

in trace norm as $T\to\infty$. The diagonal energy blocks, including all blocks within degenerate eigenspaces, remain. This is Cesaro convergence of the averaged state; pointwise convergence of $U(t)\rho U(t)^*$ is not asserted.

references.title: Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), §§2–3
MIT OpenCourseWare 8.512, Theory of Solids II, Lecture 1: Linear Response Theory, §1.1

items.title: Finite-time Kubo formula with norm remainder
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T1 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$, $H=H^*$ with energy unit J, $\hbar>0$ with unit J s, $\beta>0$ with unit J$^{-1}$, and let $\sigma=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H}$ be the stationary Gibbs density from [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-unitary]]. Let $A=A^*$ and $B=B^*$ be matrices, let $T>0$ be finite in s, let $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and let $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless; $h(t)B$ has unit J. Put $U_0(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ for time $t$ in s, $\alpha_t(A)=U_0(t)^*AU_0(t)$, and $B_t=\alpha_t(B)$. Let $W_\epsilon$ solve
$$W_\epsilon'(t)=\frac{i\epsilon h(t)}{\hbar}B_tW_\epsilon(t),\qquad W_\epsilon(0)=I,$$
and set $U_\epsilon(t)=U_0(t)W_\epsilon(t)$ and $\rho_I(t)=W_\epsilon(t)\sigma W_\epsilon(t)^*$. Then $U_\epsilon$ solves $i\hbar U_\epsilon'(t)=(H-\epsilon h(t)B)U_\epsilon(t)$, $U_\epsilon(0)=I$, and $\rho_\epsilon(t):=U_\epsilon(t)\sigma U_\epsilon(t)^*$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\epsilon(t)A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_I(t)\alpha_t(A))$. Define
$$R_{AB}(u)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma[\alpha_u(A),B]\right),\qquad C_T=\frac{2}{\hbar}\int_0^T|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds.$$
Then $W_\epsilon(t)$ is unitary and, for $0\le t\le T$,
$$\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_I(t)\alpha_t(A))=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha_t(A))+\epsilon\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds+r_\epsilon(t),\qquad |r_\epsilon(t)|\le\|A\|\frac{(|\epsilon|C_T)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_T}}2.$$
The initial Gibbs matrix is fixed as $\epsilon$ varies. The result is an exact finite-time first variation with a controlled remainder, not a static derivative of a re-prepared Gibbs family. $C_T$ and $\epsilon$ are dimensionless, and $R_{AB}$ has units $[A][B]/(\mathrm J\,\mathrm s)$.

items.title: Arbitrarily late finite phase recurrences
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T0 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement: Let $H=H^*$ with energy unit J act on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let $\hbar>0$ have unit J s, and let $U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ for time $t$ measured in s. For every time unit $t_0>0$ measured in s, there is a sequence $t_n\to+\infty$ and phases $\lambda_n\in\mathbb C$, $|\lambda_n|=1$, such that $\|U(t_n)-\lambda_n I\|\to0$. Consequently, for every density matrix $\rho$ and bounded observable $A$, the expectation $\operatorname{Tr}(U(t_n)\rho U(t_n)^*A)$ tends to $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$. If $H$ has only one distinct energy, exact recurrences occur at every time.

items.title: Bounded-commutator graph-domain Schrödinger response
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T4 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, $H=H^*$ a densely defined Hamiltonian on $D(H)$ with unit J, $\hbar>0$ with unit J s, $\rho$ a positive trace-class density with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$ and $\rho U_0(t)=U_0(t)\rho$, and $A=A^*\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$. Fix a reference energy $E_0>0$ in joules and equip $D(H)$ with the graph norm $\|\psi\|_G:=\|\psi\|+\|H\psi\|/E_0$. Let $B=B^*\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ with unit $[B]$. Assume $B(D(H))\subseteq D(H)$ and that $[H,B]\psi=HB\psi-BH\psi$ on $D(H)$ extends to a bounded operator $C$ on $\mathcal H$. Let $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous for finite $T>0$ with $h(t)B$ in J, and let $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless. Then the bounded-observable response and remainder from [[thm-qsm-dt-normal-state-kubo]] hold. In addition, with $U_0(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$, $B_t=U_0(t)^*BU_0(t)$, and $W_\epsilon'(t)=i\epsilon h(t)B_tW_\epsilon(t)/\hbar$, $W_\epsilon(0)=I$, the interaction-picture propagator maps $D(H)$ onto itself, and
$$\Psi(t)=U_0(t)W_\epsilon(t)\psi$$
is a strong solution on $[0,T]$ for each $\psi\in D(H)$, meaning that $\Psi:[0,T]\to\mathcal H$ belongs to $C([0,T];D(H))$ for the graph norm and to $C^1([0,T];\mathcal H)$, satisfies $\Psi(0)=\psi$, and satisfies $i\hbar\Psi'(t)=(H-\epsilon h(t)B)\Psi(t)$ for every $t\in[0,T]$ (with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints). No domain-preservation claim is made for a general bounded $B$ without the stated commutator hypothesis.

items.title: Adopted isolated prepared unitary model
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T0 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
For a specified finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, $H=H^*$ in J, and adopted $\hbar>0$ in J s, take a prepared finite density matrix $\rho_0$ (positive semidefinite with trace one). For time $t$ measured in s, adopt isolated evolution
$$U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar},\qquad \rho_t=U(t)\rho_0U(t)^*,$$
and the Born expectation $\mathbb E_t[A]=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA)$ for each bounded self-adjoint matrix observable $A$. This adopts the finite subsystem's preparation and unitary time evolution as a model assumption. It inherits the full Axiom of Choice convention, stated in [[def-axiom-of-choice]], of [[post-qsm-normal-measurement-state]] for the wider Hilbert-space spectral-measure framework, although this finite bounded-observable clause uses no unbounded spectral measurement. No actual apparatus, measured value, thermalization, or infinite-volume Hamiltonian is asserted.

The finite unitary and Gibbs conventions are stated in [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-unitary]] as formulation context; they do not prove that this postulate describes nature.

items.title: Prepared control and expectation convention
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T1 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
On a finite-dimensional subsystem with unperturbed $H=H^*$ in J, bounded self-adjoint control observable $B$, $\hbar>0$ in J s, and finite interval $[0,T]$ with $T>0$ in s, adopt the idealized controlled Hamiltonian
$$H_\epsilon(t)=H-\epsilon h(t)B,$$
where $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous, $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$ is dimensionless, and $h(t)B$ has unit J. The initial prepared state is held fixed at $t=0$ as the Gibbs matrix $\sigma=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H}$, $\beta>0$ in J$^{-1}$; the model does not re-prepare a Gibbs state for $H_\epsilon(t)$. Expectations use the adopted normal-state Born convention of [[post-qsm-normal-measurement-state]]. The full Axiom of Choice convention, stated in [[def-axiom-of-choice]], of that wider measurement framework is retained. This is an adopted control model; it makes no claim about a particular device or data.

For the controlled propagator $U_\epsilon$ satisfying $i\hbar U_\epsilon'(t)=H_\epsilon(t)U_\epsilon(t)$ and $U_\epsilon(0)=I$, define $\rho_\epsilon(t)=U_\epsilon(t)\sigma U_\epsilon(t)^*$ and $\mathbb E_{\epsilon,t}[A]=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\epsilon(t)A)$ for bounded self-adjoint matrices $A$. Existence and uniqueness of this finite-dimensional propagator are supplied by [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-kubo]].

The finite-time response theorem [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-kubo]] supplies the exact mathematical response interface used to formulate this postulate. It does not establish the physical applicability of the control model.

items.title: Finite spectral balance and distributional fluctuation response
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T2 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be finite-dimensional, $H=H^*$ with unit J, $\hbar>0$ with unit J s, $\beta>0$ with unit J$^{-1}$, and $\sigma=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H}$ as in [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-unitary]]. Let $A=A^*$ be a matrix observable, write $Hu_i=E_i u_i$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis, $r_i=e^{-\beta E_i}/Z_\beta$, $A_{ij}=\langle Au_j,u_i\rangle$, and $\omega_{ji}=(E_j-E_i)/\hbar$. Define the finite positive spectral measure
$$S_{AA}=2\pi\sum_{i,j}r_i|A_{ij}|^2\,\delta_{\omega_{ji}},$$
where $\delta_\nu$ is unit point mass at frequency $\nu$ and $S_{AA}(-\cdot)$ denotes pushforward under $\omega\mapsto-\omega$; $\omega_{ji}$ has unit s$^{-1}$. With observable unit $[A]$, the atomic masses of the finite measure $S_{AA}$ have units $[A]^2$. For every smooth compactly supported complex-valued function $\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$, the distribution represented by the measure $S_{AA}$ acts as $\langle S_{AA},\varphi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R}\varphi(\omega)\,dS_{AA}(\omega)$. In the Fourier convention below, the generalized density $S_{AA}(\omega)$ relative to $d\omega$ has units $[A]^2$ multiplied by seconds; it is a finite sum of Dirac distributions, not an ordinary function density. The equilibrium correlation is $C_{AA}(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha_t(A)A)$, and its Fourier convention is $S_{AA}(\omega)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{i\omega t}C_{AA}(t)\,dt$ in the distributional sense.

For $t\ge0$, set $R_{AA}(t)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma[\alpha_t(A),A])$ and, for $\eta>0$, define the retarded transform $\chi_\eta(\omega)=\int_0^\infty e^{(i\omega-\eta)t}R_{AA}(t)\,dt$. Then
$$\chi_\eta(\omega)=\sum_{i,j}\frac{(r_i-r_j)|A_{ij}|^2}{\hbar(\omega_{ji}-\omega-i\eta)}.$$
As $\eta\downarrow0$, its boundary value is the corresponding sum of principal-value real parts and Lorentzian imaginary terms weighted by $r_i-r_j$, and distributionally
$$\operatorname{Im}\chi=\frac{1}{2\hbar}(1-e^{-\beta\hbar\omega})S_{AA}(\omega).$$
Detailed balance is $S_{AA}(-d\omega)=e^{-\beta\hbar\omega}S_{AA}(d\omega)$. Thus, on $\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$,
$$S_{\mathrm{sym}}(d\omega)=\hbar\coth\!\left(\frac{\beta\hbar\omega}{2}\right)\operatorname{Im}\chi(d\omega),\qquad S_{\mathrm{sym}}=\tfrac12(S_{AA}+S_{AA}(-\cdot)).$$
Any zero-frequency mass of $S_{AA}$ is retained separately: the commutator factor vanishes there, so the formula does not determine that atom or define a value for the singular product with $\coth$ at $\omega=0$.

items.title: Absolute convergence of trace-Gibbs bounded correlation series
items.design_state: New A-page intermediate result: the absolute double-series estimate and finite spectral measure needed for trace-Gibbs detailed balance.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be separable, $K=K^*$ a densely defined Hamiltonian bounded below with energy unit J, and $\beta$ lie in an open interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$ measured in J$^{-1}$ on which $e^{-sK}$ is trace class for every $s\in I$. Set $Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta K})$, $\sigma_\beta=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta K}$, and $U(t)=e^{-itK/\hbar}$ with $\hbar>0$ in J s and $t$ in s. By [[thm-qsm-trace-gibbs-variational]], $K$ has a complete orthonormal energy basis $(u_i)$, $Ku_i=E_i u_i$, with Gibbs weights $r_i=e^{-\beta E_i}/Z_\beta>0$ and $\sum_i r_i=1$. For bounded $A,B$, put $A_{ij}=\langle Au_j,u_i\rangle$, $B_{ij}=\langle Bu_j,u_i\rangle$, and $\omega_{ji}=(E_j-E_i)/\hbar$. Then
$$C_{AB}(t):=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta U(t)^*AU(t)B)=\sum_{i,j}r_iA_{ij}B_{ji}e^{-i\omega_{ji}t}$$
converges absolutely and uniformly on $\mathbb R$, with $\sum_{i,j}r_i|A_{ij}||B_{ji}|\le\|A\|\|B\|$. Consequently
$$S_{AB}:=2\pi\sum_{i,j}r_iA_{ij}B_{ji}\,\delta_{\omega_{ji}}$$
is a finite complex Borel measure with total variation at most $2\pi\|A\|\|B\|$, and $C_{AB}(t)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int e^{-i\omega t}\,dS_{AB}(\omega)$. A Dirac measure $\delta_\nu$ assigns mass one to the point $\nu$. When $A,B$ carry units $[A],[B]$, the atomic masses of the finite measure $S_{AB}$ have units $[A][B]$. For every smooth compactly supported complex-valued function $\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$, the distribution represented by $S_{AB}$ acts as $\langle S_{AB},\varphi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R}\varphi(\omega)\,dS_{AB}(\omega)$. In the Fourier convention, the generalized density $S_{AB}(\omega)$ relative to $d\omega$ has units $[A][B]$ multiplied by seconds; it is a sum of Dirac distributions, not an ordinary function density.

items.title: Trace-Gibbs bounded correlation measure and balance
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T2 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be separable, $K=K^*$ densely defined and bounded below with energy unit J, and let $e^{-sK}$ be trace class for every $s$ in an open interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$ measured in J$^{-1}$. Fix $\beta\in I$, $Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta K})$, $\sigma_\beta=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta K}$, and $U(t)=e^{-itK/\hbar}$ for $\hbar>0$ in J s and $t$ in s. For bounded $A,B$, let $C_{AB}$ and $S_{AB}$ be the correlation function and finite spectral measure defined in [[lem-qsm-dt-trace-gibbs-correlation-series]]. Write $S_{BA}(-\cdot)$ for the pushforward under $\omega\mapsto-\omega$. Then for every bounded Borel test function $f$ with compact support,
$$\int f(\omega)\,S_{BA}(-d\omega)=\int f(\omega)e^{-\beta\hbar\omega}\,S_{AB}(d\omega).$$
The weighted measure on the right extends to a finite complex measure: the reindexed coefficient family is absolutely summable and has the same total-variation bound as $S_{BA}$. For Hermitian $A=B$, $S_{AA}$ is a positive finite measure. This is a discrete-spectrum equilibrium correlation identity; it asserts no temporal decay, continuum limit, or ordinary zero-frequency transport coefficient.

items.title: Conditional prepared finite quantum control response
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T1 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Assume the adopted finite isolated model and fixed-preparation control convention of [[post-qsm-dt-isolated-model]] and [[post-qsm-dt-physical-control]]. Let $T>0$ be finite in s, let $A=A^*$ be a bounded matrix observable, and set $\alpha_t(A)=e^{itH/\hbar}Ae^{-itH/\hbar}$ for time $t$ measured in s. Define
$$R_{AB}(u)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma[\alpha_u(A),B]\right),\qquad C_T=\frac2\hbar\int_0^T|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds.$$
Then for $0\le t\le T$ the model expectation obeys
$$\mathbb E_{\epsilon,t}[A]=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha_t(A))+\epsilon\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds+r_\epsilon(t),\qquad |r_\epsilon(t)|\le\|A\|\frac{(|\epsilon|C_T)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_T}}2.$$
Here $H$ and $hB$ have unit J, $\hbar$ has unit J s, $t$ has unit s, $\beta$ has unit J$^{-1}$, and $\epsilon,C_T$ are dimensionless. This is a conditional model prediction for the adopted preparation and dynamics, not a claim that an observed finite dataset must equal the prediction.

items.title: Bounded C-star Dyson response for finite-range spin dynamics
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T3 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Use $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, finite on-site dimension $q\ge1$, and a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction $\Phi$ with parameters $M\ge1$, $R<\infty$, $\kappa<\infty$, and $\hbar>0$ as in [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]]. Assume Countable Choice and the exact finite-matrix C$^*$-identity condition supplied in [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]]. Let $\mathcal A$ be the norm-completed quasi-local spin algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]], and let $\alpha_t$ be the strongly continuous automorphism group of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]]. Let $\{\rho_\Lambda\}$ be consistent positive trace-one local density matrices; write $\phi$ for their unique state extension supplied by [[lem-qsm-consistent-local-states]], and additionally assume $\phi\circ\alpha_t=\phi$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. This is an algebraic state on $\mathcal A$, not a trace-class density on an infinite tensor-product Hilbert space.

For $A\in\mathcal A$, $B=B^*\in\mathcal A$, continuous real $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$, finite $T>0$, and dimensionless $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$, put $B_t=\alpha_t(B)$ and let $W_\epsilon$ solve
$$W_\epsilon'(t)=\frac{i\epsilon h(t)}{\hbar}B_tW_\epsilon(t),\qquad W_\epsilon(0)=I.$$
The C$^*$-algebra Dyson solution is unitary. Define $\alpha_t^\epsilon(A)=W_\epsilon(t)^*\alpha_t(A)W_\epsilon(t)$,
$$R_{AB}(u)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\phi([\alpha_u(A),B]),\qquad C_T=\frac2\hbar\int_0^T|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds.$$
Then
$$\phi(\alpha_t^\epsilon(A))=\phi(\alpha_t(A))+\epsilon\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds+r_\epsilon(t),\qquad |r_\epsilon(t)|\le\|A\|\frac{(|\epsilon|C_T)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_T}}2.$$
When energy is the interpretation of $H_\Lambda$ and $hB$, their units are J, $t$ is s, $\hbar$ is J s, and $C_T$ is dimensionless. No global trace Hamiltonian, spatial-to-temporal decay implication, or dc coefficient follows.

items.title: Nonzero pure-point equilibrium covariance is not integrable
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T5 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the trace-class Gibbs hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-dt-trace-gibbs-correlation-measure]] for a self-adjoint Hamiltonian $K$ in J with a complete discrete energy basis and faithful Gibbs density $\sigma_\beta$ at $\beta>0$ in J$^{-1}$. Let $\hbar>0$ be in J s, $t$ in s, and let $A=A^*$ be a nonzero bounded observable with $\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta A)=0$. Define
$$C_{AA}(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta U(t)^*AU(t)A),\qquad G_{AA}(t)=\operatorname{Re}C_{AA}(t),\qquad U(t)=e^{-itK/\hbar}.$$
Then neither $C_{AA}$ nor $G_{AA}$ belongs to $L^1([0,\infty))$. In particular, the ordinary absolutely convergent isolated-system correlation integral used in a dc Green–Kubo formula does not exist under these hypotheses. This claim concerns discrete-spectrum trace-Gibbs dynamics only; it asserts no failure of temporal decay or transport limits in an infinite-volume or open-system model.

items.title: Integrability-qualified quantum variance Green–Kubo limit
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T5 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C$^*$-identity hypothesis used by [[thm-qsm-dt-algebraic-kubo]]. Use its finite-range spin algebra $\mathcal A$, strongly continuous automorphism group $\alpha_t$, and invariant state $\phi$ obtained from consistent local densities. Let $V=V^*\in\mathcal A$ satisfy $\phi(V)=0$, and define
$$X_T=\int_0^T\alpha_t(V)\,dt,\qquad G(t)=\operatorname{Re}\phi(V\alpha_t(V)).$$
If $G\in L^1([0,\infty))$, then
$$\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\phi(X_T^2)}{2T}=D:=\int_0^\infty G(t)\,dt\ge0.$$
For a finite list of centered self-adjoint observables $V_1,\ldots,V_m$, if each symmetrized covariance $G_{ab}(t)=\tfrac12(\operatorname{Re}\phi(V_a\alpha_t(V_b))+\operatorname{Re}\phi(V_b\alpha_t(V_a)))$ is absolutely integrable on $[0,\infty)$, then $D_{ab}=\int_0^\infty G_{ab}(t)dt$ is a real positive semidefinite matrix. For a velocity observable measured in m s$^{-1}$, $D$ has units m$^2$ s$^{-1}$; for general $V$, its units are $[V]^2$ s. The result is a variance of a time-integrated observable, not a joint classical trajectory or a universal transport law.

Let $\mathcal H=\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)$ with standard orthonormal basis $(e_n)_{n\ge0}$. Fix $\omega>0$ in s$^{-1}$ and $\hbar>0$ in J s. Define the diagonal Hamiltonian
$$He_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)e_n,\qquad D(H)=\{c\in\ell^2:\sum_{n\ge0}(n+\tfrac12)^2|c_n|^2<\infty\}.$$

items.title: Finite matrix trace cyclicity and nondegeneracy
items.design_state: New A-page intermediate result required by the Choi/Kraus, duality, and GKSL trace calculations; it proves finite trace cyclicity and matrix-unit pairing nondegeneracy directly.
items.statement:
Let $d,e\geq1$. For $A\in M_{e\times d}(\mathbb C)$ and $B\in M_{d\times e}(\mathbb C)$,
$$ \operatorname{Tr}_e(AB)=\operatorname{Tr}_d(BA), $$
where $\operatorname{Tr}_r$ is the diagonal-sum trace on $M_r(\mathbb C)$. This includes cyclicity for square matrices. For $C\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, the bilinear trace pairing is nondegenerate: if $\operatorname{Tr}_d(XC)=0$ for every $X\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, then $C=0$. No adjoint is inserted in this pairing.

items.title: Finite completely positive trace-preserving maps
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C0; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C0.
items.statement:
Let $d,e\geq1$ be integers, let $H_{\mathrm{in}}=\mathbb C^d$ and $H_{\mathrm{out}}=\mathbb C^e$ with their standard inner products, and write $M_d(\mathbb C)$ and $M_e(\mathbb C)$ for the complex linear maps on these spaces. A matrix $X$ is **positive semidefinite**, written $X\geq0$, when it is Hermitian and $\langle Xv,v\rangle\geq0$ for every vector $v$. The finite spectral convention in [[lem-qsm-matrix-state-calculus]] gives positive matrices their orthonormal eigenbases and positive square roots.

A **positive map** is a complex-linear map $\Phi:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_e(\mathbb C)$ such that $\Phi(X)\geq0$ whenever $X\geq0$. For each integer $r\geq1$, identify $M_r(\mathbb C)\otimes M_d(\mathbb C)$ with matrices on $\mathbb C^r\otimes\mathbb C^d$ in the ordered product basis. The map $\Phi$ is **completely positive** when $\operatorname{id}_r\otimes\Phi$ is positive for every such $r$, where $\operatorname{id}_r$ is the identity map on $M_r(\mathbb C)$.

The map $\Phi$ is **trace-preserving** when $\operatorname{Tr}(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{Tr}(X)$ for every $X\in M_d(\mathbb C)$. A **finite quantum channel** is a complex-linear map that is both completely positive and trace-preserving, abbreviated CPTP. Unitality, $\Phi(I_d)=I_e$, is a separate condition and is not part of this definition.

This is a mathematical definition. A physical preparation, measurement, or open-system model must separately identify when one of these maps represents a physical transformation.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.2.1–2.2.3
Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 3, §3.2

items.title: Finite GKSL generators and units
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C3; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C3.
items.statement:
Fix a finite dimension $d\geq1$, a positive constant $\hbar$ in joule-seconds, a Hermitian matrix $H\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ in joules, and a finite family $L_1,\ldots,L_m\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ with units ${\rm s}^{-1/2}$, where $m\geq0$. On dimensionless matrices $X\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, define the **finite Gorini–Kossakowski–Sudarshan–Lindblad (GKSL) generator**

$$\mathcal L(X)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}[H,X]+\sum_{a=1}^{m}\left(L_aXL_a^*-\frac12\{L_a^*L_a,X\}\right),$$

where $[A,B]=AB-BA$, $\{A,B\}=AB+BA$, and $A^*$ is the conjugate transpose. Each summand has units ${\rm s}^{-1}$ times the units of $X$. An empty sum when $m=0$ is zero. The resulting $\mathcal L$ is a linear map on the matrix space used in the finite-channel definition [[def-qsm-dt-channel-definition]].

For a compact time interval $I\subset\mathbb R$ whose coordinate is time in seconds, continuous functions $H:I\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ and $L_a:I\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ with $H(t)=H(t)^*$ define the corresponding **continuous finite GKSL family** $\mathcal L_t$ by the same formula at each $t$. A propagator for this family means a family of linear maps $\Lambda(t,s)$, $s\leq t$ in $I$, satisfying $\partial_t\Lambda(t,s)=\mathcal L_t\circ\Lambda(t,s)$ and $\Lambda(s,s)=\operatorname{id}$. This definition alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness.

These are finite-dimensional mathematical definitions. They do not assert that a physical system follows this generator or that a microscopic bath has a Markovian limit.

references.title: Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 21, §21.1
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.2.1–2.2.3

items.title: Complete finite Choi-Kraus equivalence
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C0; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C0.
items.statement:
Let $d,e\geq1$ and let $\Phi:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_e(\mathbb C)$ be complex-linear. Choose the standard input basis $(|i\rangle)_{i=1}^d$, let $E_{ij}=|i\rangle\langle j|$, and use the ordered tensor convention input-reference $\otimes$ output. Define the (unnormalized) Choi matrix

$$J(\Phi):=\sum_{i,j=1}^{d}E_{ij}\otimes\Phi(E_{ij})\in M_d(\mathbb C)\otimes M_e(\mathbb C).$$ Then $\Phi$ is completely positive if and only if $J(\Phi)\geq0$, and this holds if and only if there are $q\leq de$ matrices $K_1,\ldots,K_q:\mathbb C^d\to\mathbb C^e$ such that $$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a=1}^{q}K_aXK_a^*\qquad(X\in M_d(\mathbb C)).$$

The empty sum is allowed when $\Phi=0$. For any such Kraus representation, $\Phi$ is trace-preserving if and only if $\sum_{a=1}^{q}K_a^*K_a=I_d$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §2.2.2, Theorem 2.22
Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 3, §3.2

items.title: Channel duals and norm closure
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C0; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C0.
items.statement:
Let $\Phi:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_e(\mathbb C)$ be a finite channel as defined in [[def-qsm-dt-channel-definition]]. There is a unique linear map $\Phi^\dagger:M_e(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ satisfying the trace-pairing identity

$$\operatorname{Tr}(\Phi(X)A)=\operatorname{Tr}(X\Phi^\dagger(A))\qquad(X\in M_d(\mathbb C),\ A\in M_e(\mathbb C)).$$

If $\Phi(X)=\sum_aK_aXK_a^*$, then $\Phi^\dagger(A)=\sum_aK_a^*AK_a$; in particular, $\Phi^\dagger$ is completely positive and unital. Composition and finite convex combinations of channels are channels. A limit in the induced operator norm $\|\Psi\|_{\infty\to\infty}:=\sup_{\|X\|_\infty\leq1}\|\Psi(X)\|_\infty$, where $\|X\|_\infty:=\sup_{\|v\|=1}\|Xv\|$, of channels $M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_e(\mathbb C)$ is also a channel. Moreover, a norm limit of completely positive maps of these fixed finite dimensions is completely positive.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.2.1–2.2.2
Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 3, §3.2

items.title: Finite GKSL generates CPTP semigroups
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C3; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C3.
items.statement: Let $\mathcal L$ be a finite GKSL generator on $M_d(\mathbb C)$, $d\geq1$, with the units and conventions of [[def-qsm-dt-gksl-definition]]. For a bounded operator $A$ on a complex Banach space, write $e^{tA}:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}t^nA^n/n!$ for the operator-norm convergent series of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]]. Then $T_t=e^{t\mathcal L}$ is a finite channel for every $t\geq0$. The family satisfies $T_0=\operatorname{id}$, $T_{t+s}=T_t\circ T_s$, and is norm-continuous. Time is measured in seconds; no negative-time channel or physical bath limit is asserted.

references.title: Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 21, §21.1
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.2.1–2.2.2

items.title: Independent-preparation reduced unitary channel
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C2; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C2.
items.statement:
Let $H_S=\mathbb C^d$ and $H_E=\mathbb C^m$, with $d,m\geq1$, in fixed ordered orthonormal bases. For a bounded operator $A$ on a complex Banach space, define $e^A:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}A^n/n!$ by its operator-norm convergent series ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]]). Let $H_{\mathrm{tot}}=H_{\mathrm{tot}}^*$ be a matrix on $H_S\otimes H_E$ with energy units joules, let $\hbar>0$ have units joule-seconds, and set $U_t=e^{-itH_{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$ for $t\in\mathbb R$ measured in seconds. Let $\sigma_E\geq0$ with $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma_E=1$, and define

$$\Phi_t(\rho):=\operatorname{Tr}_E\!\left(U_t(\rho\otimes\sigma_E)U_t^*\right)\qquad(\rho\in M_d(\mathbb C)).$$

For each $t$, $\Phi_t:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ is a finite quantum channel. The theorem concerns the product preparation $\rho\otimes\sigma_E$; it makes no claim that a correlated initial joint state defines a map of the system marginal alone.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.1.3 and 2.2.2
Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapters 3 and 21

items.title: Schwarz and trace-norm channel contraction
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C1; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C1.
items.statement:
Let $\Phi:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_e(\mathbb C)$ be a finite channel, and define $\|X\|_\infty=\sup_{\|v\|=1}\|Xv\|$ and $\|X\|_1=\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt{X^*X}$. Its trace dual $\Phi^\dagger:M_e(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ from [[thm-qsm-dt-channel-duality]] satisfies

$$\|\Phi^\dagger(A)\|_\infty\leq\|A\|_\infty\qquad(A\in M_e(\mathbb C)).$$ For every $X\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, the Schrödinger map contracts the trace norm: $$\|\Phi(X)\|_1\leq\|X\|_1.$$

The second inequality applies to arbitrary complex matrices, not only density matrices.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 3, §3.3, Theorem 3.39 and Corollary 3.40
Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 3, §§3.5–3.6

items.title: Norm-continuous finite channel semigroups are GKSL
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C4; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C4.
items.statement: Let $d\geq1$ and let $T_t:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$, $t\geq0$ measured in seconds, be a semigroup of finite channels, so $T_0=\operatorname{id}$ and $T_{t+s}=T_t\circ T_s$. Assume $t\mapsto T_t$ is continuous in the induced operator norm on the finite-dimensional space of linear maps $M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$. For a bounded operator $A$ on a complex Banach space, write $e^{tA}:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}t^nA^n/n!$ for the operator-norm convergent exponential series of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]]. Then there is a unique linear generator $\mathcal L$, in ${\rm s}^{-1}$, with $T_t=e^{t\mathcal L}$, and $\mathcal L$ has the finite GKSL form in [[def-qsm-dt-gksl-definition]] with at most $d^2-1$ jump matrices. Conversely, every such finite GKSL generator produces a norm-continuous channel semigroup, as in [[thm-qsm-dt-gksl-sufficient]].

references.title: Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 21, §21.1
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.2.1–2.2.2

items.title: Pinching raises finite entropy
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C5; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C5.
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\geq1$, and let $P_0,\ldots,P_{r-1}$ be pairwise orthogonal projections, meaning $P_j=P_j^*=P_j^2$ and $P_jP_k=0$ for $j\ne k$, with $r\geq1$ and $\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}P_j=I$. Define the pinching map $\Delta:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ by $\Delta(X)=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}P_jXP_j$. For every positive semidefinite trace-one matrix $\rho$, $\Delta$ is a finite channel and

$$S(\Delta(\rho))\geq S(\rho),$$

where $S(\rho)=-k_B\sum_\lambda\lambda\log\lambda$, the sum is over eigenvalues with multiplicity, $0\log0=0$, the logarithm is natural, and $k_B>0$ has units joule per kelvin. The theorem concerns only this finite pinching operation; it does not say that every channel increases entropy.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 4, §4.1.1, Proposition 4.6
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 5, §5.2.2, Theorem 5.23

items.title: Continuous finite GKSL channel propagators
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C3; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C3.
items.statement:
Let $I=[s_0,s_1]\subset\mathbb R$ be a compact time interval in seconds, $d\geq1$, $H:I\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ continuous with $H(t)=H(t)^*$ in joules, and $L_a:I\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ continuous with finite $a=1,\ldots,m$ in ${\rm s}^{-1/2}$. At each $t\in I$, form $\mathcal L_t$ by [[def-qsm-dt-gksl-definition]]. For every $s\leq t$ in $I$, the propagator $\Lambda(t,s)$ solving

$$\partial_t\Lambda(t,s)=\mathcal L_t\circ\Lambda(t,s),\qquad \Lambda(s,s)=\operatorname{id},$$

exists uniquely and is a finite channel. No semigroup law is asserted when $t\mapsto\mathcal L_t$ varies.

references.title: Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 21, §21.1
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.2.1–2.2.2

row.title: Finite completely positive trace-preserving maps — Examples

items.title: Amplitude damping can decrease system entropy
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C5; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C5.
items.statement: Every finite quantum channel $\Phi$ and every positive semidefinite trace-one matrix $\rho$ satisfy $S(\Phi(\rho))\geq S(\rho)$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 4, §4.1.1 and Chapter 5, §5.2.2
Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 3, §3.2, Example 3.17

items.title: Transpose positivity fails ancillary positivity
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C1; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C1.
items.statement: Every complex-linear positive trace-preserving map between finite matrix algebras is completely positive.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §2.2.2, Theorem 2.22
Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 3, §3.2, Example 3.11 and Theorem 3.18

items.title: Correlated preparations with identical marginals diverge
items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C2; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C2.
items.statement: For fixed finite system and environment spaces and a fixed joint unitary $U$, the final system matrix $\operatorname{Tr}_E(U\omega U^*)$ is determined by the initial system marginal $\operatorname{Tr}_E\omega$ for every positive semidefinite trace-one matrix $\omega$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §2.1.3

items.design_state: Exact hypotheses and units in C2; no stronger continuum/bath-limit claim.; original research argument workers/dynamics-transport/channels-and-generators.md#C2.
items.statement: Every reduced-unitary family from a fixed finite system–environment Hamiltonian and a fixed product environment state is a semigroup: $\Phi_{t+s}=\Phi_t\circ\Phi_s$ for all $t,s\geq0$.

row.title: Specified finite GNS detailed balance

items.title: Specified finite GNS detailed balance

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §§1.2.4 and 1.3.4
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §2

items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$ be finite, let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^d$ with its standard inner product, and write $M_d(\mathbb C)$ for its matrices. Let $H_{\rm s}=H_{\rm s}^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ be a Hamiltonian in joules, let $\hbar>0$ have units joule-seconds, and let $m\geq0$ be an integer with $L_1,\ldots,L_m\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ a finite family of jump matrices in seconds$^{-1/2}$. Matrices on which the generators act are dimensionless. The Schrödinger generator $\mathcal L$ is the finite GKSL generator of [[def-qsm-dt-gksl-definition]].

Its trace-dual observable generator is

$$G(A)=\frac{i}{\hbar}[H_{\rm s},A]+D(A),\qquad D(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\left(L_j^*AL_j-\frac12\{L_j^*L_j,A\}\right).$$

Here $[U,V]=UV-VU$, $\{U,V\}=UV+VU$, and $A^*$ is the conjugate transpose. The units of $G$, $D$, and $\mathcal L$ are seconds$^{-1}$. The generator preserves the identity, $D(I)=0$, so $e^{tD}(I)=I$.

Let $\sigma=\sigma^*>0$ be a dimensionless density matrix on $\mathcal H$, so $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma=1$. Define

$$\langle A,B\rangle_\sigma:=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma B^*A),\qquad \|A\|_\sigma:=\langle A,A\rangle_\sigma^{1/2}.$$

This inner product is linear in its first variable. It is positive definite because $\sigma>0$. The data satisfy **the specified finite GNS detailed-balance convention** when $[H_{\rm s},\sigma]=0$ and $D$ is self-adjoint for this inner product, meaning $\langle D(A),B\rangle_\sigma=\langle A,D(B)\rangle_\sigma$ for all $A,B\in M_d(\mathbb C)$. The Hamiltonian part of $G$ is kept separate and is anti-self-adjoint. Quantum detailed-balance conventions vary; in particular, this definition does not identify GNS symmetry with KMS or Kubo–Mori symmetry.

items.title: Faithful scalar-kernel detailed balance gives a relaxation gap

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §1.3.4
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §§2 and 7

items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$, and let $G=K+D$ and the faithful density matrix $\sigma$ satisfy [[def-qsm-dt-gns-detailed-balance]], with $\ker D=\mathbb C I$. Write $\mathcal M_0=\{A\in M_d(\mathbb C):\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma A)=0\}$. If $d>1$, the restriction $D|_{\mathcal M_0}$ has only strictly negative eigenvalues. Define

$$\gamma:=\min\{-\lambda:\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(D|_{\mathcal M_0})\}>0.$$

Then for every $A\in\mathcal M_0$ and $t\geq0$,

$$\|e^{tG}A\|_\sigma\leq e^{-\gamma t}\|A\|_\sigma.$$

For every density matrix $\rho$, let $\rho_t=e^{t\mathcal L}\rho$, where $\mathcal L$ is the Schrödinger trace-dual generator. Then

$$\|\rho_t-\sigma\|_1\leq\|\sigma^{-1/2}(\rho-\sigma)\|_2e^{-\gamma t}.$$

Here $\|X\|_1=\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt{X^*X}$ and $\|X\|_2=(\operatorname{Tr}X^*X)^{1/2}$. For centered $A,B\in\mathcal M_0$, the correlation $t\mapsto\langle e^{tG}A,B\rangle_\sigma$ is absolutely integrable. Also

$$\Gamma(A):=\operatorname{Re}\int_0^\infty\langle e^{tG}A,A\rangle_\sigma\,dt=\operatorname{Re}\langle(-G|_{\mathcal M_0})^{-1}A,A\rangle_\sigma\geq0.$$

For $d=1$, $\mathcal M_0=\{0\}$, $\rho=\sigma$, and all centered and relaxation claims are trivial; no $\gamma$ is defined. The units of $\gamma$ are seconds$^{-1}$. These are finite-dimensional conditional model results; they assert no infinite-dimensional bath limit.

items.title: Connected Gibbs jump generators satisfy detailed balance

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §1.3.4
David Aldous and James Allen Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, Chapters 2–3
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §2

items.statement:
Let $d\geq2$, let $E=\{1,\ldots,d\}$, let $E_a\in\mathbb R$ be finite energies in joules, and let $\beta>0$ have units joule$^{-1}$. Define

$$Z_\beta:=\sum_{a\in E}e^{-\beta E_a},\qquad \pi_a:=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta E_a}.$$

For each $a\ne b$, let $w_{ab}\geq0$ be a rate in seconds$^{-1}$ satisfying Gibbs detailed balance $\pi_aw_{ab}=\pi_bw_{ba}$, and assume the undirected graph with edge $\{a,b\}$ whenever $w_{ab}>0$ is connected. On $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^d$, fix an orthonormal energy basis $(|a\rangle)$, set $H_{\rm s}=\sum_aE_a|a\rangle\langle a|$, and define $L_{ab}=\sqrt{w_{ab}}|b\rangle\langle a|$ for $a\ne b$. Fix $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. For real functions $f,g:E\to\mathbb R$, define $\langle f,g\rangle_\pi:=\sum_a\pi_af_ag_a$, and define the row-generator action on column observables by $(Wf)_a:=\sum_{b\ne a}w_{ab}(f_b-f_a)$. Let

$$\sigma:=\sum_a\pi_a|a\rangle\langle a|,\qquad r_a:=\sum_{b\ne a}w_{ab}.$$

Use the finite GKSL generator with Hamiltonian $H_{\rm s}$ and the jump matrices $L_{ab}$. Its observable dissipator $D$ is self-adjoint for the $\sigma$-GNS inner product of [[def-qsm-dt-gns-detailed-balance]], $H_{\rm s}$ commutes with $\sigma$, and $\ker D=\mathbb C I$. On diagonal observables, $W$ is self-adjoint on $L^2(E,\pi)$ with constants as its kernel; for $d\geq2$ its restriction to $\pi^\perp:=\{f:E\to\mathbb R:\sum_a\pi_af_a=0\}$ has a positive spectral gap $\gamma_{\rm cl}$. Thus the generator satisfies the specified finite GNS detailed-balance convention and the generic gap conclusion of [[thm-qsm-dt-detailed-balance-gap]] applies. This claim does not assert a microscopic bath limit.

items.title: Specified energy-jump instrument realizes a finite chain

references.title: M. B. Plenio and P. L. Knight, The quantum-jump approach to dissipative dynamics in quantum optics, §IV.1 “Quantum jumps” and §IV.3 “Simulation of single trajectories”, equations 120–133
David Aldous and James Allen Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, Chapter 2 §2.1.2

items.statement:
Use the finite energy basis, energies $E_a$, rates $w_{ab}$, Hamiltonian $H_{\rm s}$, and jump matrices $L_{ab}=\sqrt{w_{ab}}|b\rangle\langle a|$ of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]]. Define $R:=\sum_{a\ne b}L_{ab}^*L_{ab}=\sum_a r_a|a\rangle\langle a|$ and the no-click matrix $K:=-iH_{\rm s}/\hbar-R/2$. The **specified energy-resolved instrument** has the following outcomes:

1. If the current state is the energy eigenstate $|a\rangle$, then during a no-click interval of length $t$ the unnormalized state is $e^{tK}|a\rangle$.
2. In an infinitesimal interval $dt$, the outcome labelled $a\to b$ has jump operation $\sqrt{dt}\,L_{ab}$ and probability $dt\,\langle a|L_{ab}^*L_{ab}|a\rangle+o(dt)$. Its normalized post-click state is $L_{ab}|a\rangle/\|L_{ab}|a\rangle\|=|b\rangle$.
3. The no-click operation over $dt$ is $M_0(dt)=I+Kdt+o(dt)$. Since $K^*+K=-R$ and $\sum_{a\ne b}L_{ab}^*L_{ab}=R$, the no-click and jump effects sum to $I+o(dt)$.
4. After each recorded jump, repeat the same rule from the new energy label.

The output path records the current label $a(t)\in E$. This is one selected instrument model; the one-time GKSL semigroup alone does not specify a unique record process.

items.title: Gibbs jump commuting relative entropy production

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §1.3.4
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §2

items.statement:
Use the finite connected Gibbs jump model of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]]. For a diagonal density $\rho_t=\sum_a p_a(t)|a\rangle\langle a|$, the populations satisfy $p'_a=\sum_{b\ne a}(p_bw_{ba}-p_aw_{ab})$. Define the dimensionless classical relative entropy

$$K(p\mid\pi):=\sum_{a\in E}p_a\log\frac{p_a}{\pi_a},\qquad 0\log(0/\pi_a):=0,$$

where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. For every $t>0$, $p_a(t)>0$ for all $a$, and

$$\frac{d}{dt}K(p_t\mid\pi)=-\frac12\sum_{\substack{a,b\in E\\a\ne b}}\pi_aw_{ab}(u_a-u_b)(\log u_a-\log u_b)\leq0,\qquad u_a:=p_a/\pi_a.$$

Equality in this derivative holds exactly when $p_t=\pi$. For any initial probability vector, including one with zero entries, $t\mapsto K(p_t\mid\pi)$ is continuous at $t=0$ and nonincreasing on $[0,\infty)$. This is a finite commuting-state statement; it asserts no entropy-production theorem for noncommuting densities.

items.title: Gap-controlled correlation resolvent and positive coefficients

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §1.3.4
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §§2 and 7

items.statement:
Assume the finite GNS detailed-balance hypotheses, $d>1$, and the positive gap $\gamma$ of [[thm-qsm-dt-detailed-balance-gap]]. For centered $A,B\in\mathcal M_0$, define $C_{A,B}(t):=\langle e^{tG}A,B\rangle_\sigma$. Then

$$|C_{A,B}(t)|\leq e^{-\gamma t}\|A\|_\sigma\|B\|_\sigma,\qquad t\geq0,$$

so the correlation is absolutely integrable and

$$\int_0^\infty C_{A,B}(t)\,dt=\left\langle(-G|_{\mathcal M_0})^{-1}A,B\right\rangle_\sigma.$$

For centered $A$, the real coefficient

$$\Gamma(A):=\operatorname{Re}\int_0^\infty\langle e^{tG}A,A\rangle_\sigma\,dt$$

is nonnegative. Its real polarization on any finite list of Hermitian centered observables is a positive-semidefinite real symmetric correlation-integral matrix. No mixing, central-limit theorem, or infinite-volume transport claim follows.

items.title: Fixed-dissipator finite response and integrable kernel

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §§1.3.4 and 1.4.2
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §2

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal L_0$ be the finite Schrödinger generator trace-dual to $G$ in [[def-qsm-dt-gns-detailed-balance]], and assume the gap hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-dt-detailed-balance-gap]] with $d>1$. Let $A\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, $B=B^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ be dimensionless observables, and let $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous with units joules. For dimensionless $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$, perturb only the Hamiltonian by $H_\epsilon(t)=H_{\rm s}-\epsilon h(t)B$; hold the dissipator fixed. Let $\rho^\epsilon_t$ be the unique state solution with $\rho^\epsilon_0=\sigma$, supplied by [[thm-qsm-dt-time-dependent-gksl]].

Define $A_0:=A-\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma A)I$ and, for $\tau\geq0$,

$$R_{AB}(\tau):=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma[e^{\tau G}A_0,B]\right).$$

Then, on every finite interval $[0,T]$, the derivative at $\epsilon=0$ exists and

$$\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^\epsilon_tA)\right|_{\epsilon=0}=\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds.$$

The kernel is absolutely integrable on $[0,\infty)$. If $\mu$ is the smallest eigenvalue of $\sigma$, then

$$|R_{AB}(\tau)|\leq\frac{2\|B\|_\infty}{\hbar\sqrt{\mu}}\,e^{-\gamma\tau}\|A_0\|_\sigma.$$

This is an open-system model response with a fixed dissipator. It does not assert that the driven stationary state is the Gibbs state of $H_{\rm s}-\epsilon hB$.

items.title: Specified effective GKSL bath and instrument assumption
items.physical_scope: For a finite-dimensional subsystem represented by H=C^d (d>=1), the chosen thermal GKSL state law and energy-resolved instrument apply physically only on the declared finite interval [0,t_res], where t_res>0 is in seconds. All-time limits are mathematical continuations of the same fixed generator and instrument, with no physical-applicability claim beyond t_res. No microscopic bath limit, calibrated rate, or reported measurement is asserted.

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §§1.3.4 and 1.5.3
M. B. Plenio and P. L. Knight, The quantum-jump approach to dissipative dynamics in quantum optics, §IV.1 “Quantum jumps” and §IV.3 “Simulation of single trajectories”

items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$ be finite and let the modeled subsystem Hilbert space be $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^d$. A state is a dimensionless matrix $\rho=\rho^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ such that $x^*\rho x\geq0$ for every $x\in\mathbb C^d$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. An initial preparation is a chosen state $\rho_0$. Let $H_{\rm s}=H_{\rm s}^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ have units joules, let $\hbar>0$ have units joule-seconds, and let $L_1,\ldots,L_m\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, $m\geq0$ finite, have units seconds$^{-1/2}$. We adopt the time-independent finite GKSL generator of [[def-qsm-dt-gksl-definition]],

$$\mathcal L(X)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}[H_{\rm s},X]+\sum_{j=1}^{m}\left(L_jXL_j^*-\frac12\{L_j^*L_j,X\}\right),$$

where $[U,V]=UV-VU$ and $\{U,V\}=UV+VU$. The exact state law is

$$\frac{d}{dt}\rho_t=\mathcal L(\rho_t),\qquad \rho_{t=0}=\rho_0,\qquad \rho_t=e^{t\mathcal L}\rho_0,\qquad 0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}.$$

Here $t_{\rm res}\in(0,\infty)$ is the finite resolved duration, in seconds, adopted for this model. For mathematical long-time calculations, the same constant generator defines the continuation $e^{t\mathcal L}\rho_0$ for every $t\geq0$; this continuation makes no physical-applicability claim for $t>t_{\rm res}$. By [[thm-qsm-dt-gksl-sufficient]] it is a density-state evolution on that mathematical continuation as well.

Let $k_{\rm B}>0$ denote Boltzmann's constant, with SI units joules per kelvin; it converts absolute temperature to an inverse-energy parameter. Let $T_{\rm bath}>0$ be the adopted absolute temperature parameter in kelvins and set $\beta:=(k_{\rm B}T_{\rm bath})^{-1}$, with units joules$^{-1}$. The temperature and rates are model inputs here; no measured calibration is asserted. The temperature parameter alone imposes no detailed-balance condition on an arbitrary choice of $L_j$. When the generator is specialized to the connected Gibbs-jump model, its energies, $\beta$, and rates must satisfy the hypotheses in [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]].

Within this effective formulation, the dimension $d$, preparation $\rho_0$, general coefficient matrices $H_{\rm s}$ and $L_j$, positive constants $\hbar$ and $k_{\rm B}$, temperature $T_{\rm bath}$, and resolved duration $t_{\rm res}$ are primitive, adopted model inputs with the types and units stated above; none is derived here from a microscopic reservoir or inferred from a measurement. This status is local to this formulation, not a claim that each is fundamental in every physical theory. The space $\mathbb C^d$, inverse-energy parameter $\beta$, generator $\mathcal L$, and state family $\rho_t$ are derived by their displayed constructions once those inputs and the physical state-law postulate are fixed. The selected Hermitian observable $A$ and its unit assignment are additional adopted observable data; its expectation is derived by the trace formula below.

In the connected Gibbs-jump parameterization, the orthonormal energy basis, real level energies $E_a$ in joules, and rates $w_{ab}\geq0$ in seconds$^{-1}$ are instead the adopted primitive spectral and rate data, subject to the Gibbs-balance and connectivity hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]]. In that parameterization the operator coefficients are derived as $H_{\rm s}=\sum_a E_a|a\rangle\langle a|$ and $L_{ab}=\sqrt{w_{ab}}|b\rangle\langle a|$; they replace, rather than supplement, the independent general matrix choices above. The Gibbs weights $\pi_a=e^{-\beta E_a}/\sum_b e^{-\beta E_b}$ are derived, while the energy-resolved instrument remains a separate adopted assumption. In particular, neither the temperature nor the Gibbs-balance relation derives the numerical rates.

For that Gibbs-jump specialization, record predictions additionally adopt the particular ideal energy-resolved instrument defined in [[def-qsm-dt-monitored-chain]], and only on $0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}$ as a physical model. Its law for all $t\geq0$ is used only as a mathematical continuation when deriving a long-time coefficient. A one-time channel family alone does not select this record law. Full [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is retained as the formal set-theoretic premise in the monitored-chain supplier's construction of the joint path law; it is not a physical postulate about nature. A selected observable is represented by a Hermitian matrix $A\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ with its assigned physical units, and its model expectation $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA)$ has those same units; no measurement outcome is reported.

items.title: Stationary monitored-chain transport variance coefficient

references.title: David Aldous and James Allen Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, Chapters 2–3
M. B. Plenio and P. L. Knight, The quantum-jump approach to dissipative dynamics in quantum optics, §IV.1 “Quantum jumps” and §IV.3 “Simulation of single trajectories”

items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice and the connected finite Gibbs jump data of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]]. Use the energy-resolved record path supplied by [[def-qsm-dt-monitored-chain]], initialized with law $\pi$. Let $v:E\to\mathbb R$ be a real velocity observable with units metres per second and $\pi(v):=\sum_a\pi_av_a=0$. Define the record displacement

$$Y_T:=\int_0^T v_{a(s)}\,ds,\qquad C_v(s):=\langle v,e^{sW}v\rangle_\pi,$$

where $Wf(a)=\sum_{b\ne a}w_{ab}(f_b-f_a)$, $\langle f,g\rangle_\pi=\sum_a\pi_a f_ag_a$, and $\pi^\perp:=\{f:E\to\mathbb R:\sum_a\pi_af_a=0\}$. Then for every $T\geq0$,

$$\mathbb E_\pi[Y_T]=0,\qquad \operatorname{Var}_\pi(Y_T)=2\int_0^T(T-s)C_v(s)\,ds.$$

If $\gamma_{\rm cl}>0$ is the reversible spectral gap of $W$ on $\pi$-centered functions, then $|C_v(s)|\leq e^{-\gamma_{\rm cl}s}\sum_a\pi_av_a^2$, and

$$D_{\rm rec}:=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{Var}_\pi(Y_T)}{2T}=\int_0^\infty C_v(s)\,ds=\langle(-W|_{\pi^\perp})^{-1}v,v\rangle_\pi\geq0.$$

The units of $D_{\rm rec}$ are square metres per second. This proves a variance coefficient for the selected finite record model; it does not prove a central-limit theorem or a generic quantum transport law.

items.title: Conditional specified thermal bath relaxation
items.physical_scope: Conditional predictions for the specified finite connected Gibbs-jump GKSL model, physically applicable only on the postulate's finite interval [0,t_res]. The all-time exponential estimate and qubit formulas are proved for the mathematical continuation of the fixed generator; no physical applicability for t>t_res, measured rates, microscopic bath limit, or universal thermalization law is claimed.

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §§1.3.4 and 1.5.3
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §2

items.statement:
Assume full AC, the adopted finite effective-bath model [[post-qsm-dt-effective-bath]] on its physical interval $0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}$, and the connected finite Gibbs-jump hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]]. For an initial density $\rho$, let $\rho_t=e^{t\mathcal L}\rho$ denote the mathematical all-time continuation of the fixed finite Schrödinger generator, and let $\sigma=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H_{\rm s}}$. If $d>1$, the finite detailed-balance gap $\gamma>0$ gives the conditional model prediction for every $t\geq0$ in that continuation

$$\|\rho_t-\sigma\|_1\leq\|\sigma^{-1/2}(\rho-\sigma)\|_2e^{-\gamma t}.$$

Under the adopted physical model this bound is applicable only for $0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}$; its all-time form is a mathematical consequence of continuing the same fixed generator, not a claim about physical evolution for $t>t_{\rm res}$.

For the two-level specialization, let $H_{\rm s}=\Delta Z/2$, $\Delta>0$ joules, $Z=|0\rangle\langle0|-|1\rangle\langle1|$, and $X=|0\rangle\langle1|+|1\rangle\langle0|$, $Y=-i|0\rangle\langle1|+i|1\rangle\langle0|$. Adopt downward jump $\sqrt a\,|1\rangle\langle0|$ with $a>0$ seconds$^{-1}$, upward jump $\sqrt b\,|0\rangle\langle1|$ with $b/a=e^{-\beta\Delta}$, and optionally a dephasing jump $\sqrt{\gamma_\phi/2}\,Z$ with $\gamma_\phi\geq0$ seconds$^{-1}$. Put

$$\omega:=\Delta/\hbar,\quad \gamma_1:=a+b,\quad \gamma_2:=\frac{a+b}{2}+\gamma_\phi,\quad z_{\rm eq}:=\frac{b-a}{a+b}=-\tanh(\beta\Delta/2).$$

For every $t\geq0$ in the mathematical continuation, the exact model expectations and coherence satisfy

$$\langle Z\rangle_t=z_{\rm eq}+e^{-\gamma_1t}(\langle Z\rangle_0-z_{\rm eq}),\qquad \rho_{01}(t)=e^{-(\gamma_2+i\omega)t}\rho_{01}(0).$$

Equivalently, $e^{tG}X=e^{-\gamma_2t}(X\cos\omega t-Y\sin\omega t)$ and $e^{tG}Z=z_{\rm eq}I+e^{-\gamma_1t}(Z-z_{\rm eq}I)$. For $d=1$, $\rho=\sigma$ and relaxation is trivial. These are conditional model deductions, not experimental findings or claims that a physical bath realizes the postulate.

The qubit formulas above are stated for the mathematical continuation; their physical model applicability is limited to $0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}$.

items.statement:
Assume full AC, [[post-qsm-dt-effective-bath]], and the finite connected Gibbs-jump model with its selected energy-resolved instrument. Prepare the system with diagonal Gibbs law $\pi$. Assign a real pointer velocity $v_a$ in metres per second to each recorded energy label, with $\sum_a\pi_av_a=0$, and define the model record displacement $Y_T=\int_0^T v_{a(s)}\,ds$. The postulate's physical applicability is limited to $0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}$. For formulas at arbitrary $T\geq0$ and their limit, continue the same finite-rate chain as an idealized mathematical model; this gives no physical-applicability claim for $T>t_{\rm res}$. Thus the displayed formula is a conditional physical-model prediction for $0\leq T\leq t_{\rm res}$ and a mathematical model identity for all $T\geq0$ in the continuation:

$$\mathbb E_\pi[Y_T]=0,\qquad \operatorname{Var}_\pi(Y_T)=2\int_0^T(T-s)C_v(s)\,ds,$$

where $C_v(s)=\sum_a\pi_av_a(e^{sW}v)_a$. The limit

$$D_{\rm rec}:=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{Var}_\pi(Y_T)}{2T}=\int_0^\infty C_v(s)\,ds=\langle(-W|_{\pi^\perp})^{-1}v,v\rangle_\pi\geq0$$

exists and has units square metres per second. This long-time limit is a derived coefficient of the idealized mathematical continuation. It is not a measurement of a system's position, a calibrated material coefficient, or evidence that the microscopic bath obeys the effective model.

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §§1.5.3 and 1.3.4
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §2

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$, $H_{\rm s}=\Delta Z/2$ with $\Delta>0$ joules, $Z=|0\rangle\langle0|-|1\rangle\langle1|$, $X=|0\rangle\langle1|+|1\rangle\langle0|$, and $Y=-i|0\rangle\langle1|+i|1\rangle\langle0|$. Take downward rate $a>0$, upward rate $b>0$, $b/a=e^{-\beta\Delta}$, and optional dephasing rate $\gamma_\phi\geq0$. Here $\beta>0$ is in joules$^{-1}$, $\hbar$ is in joule-seconds, and $a,b,\gamma_\phi$ are in seconds$^{-1}$. Use the finite GKSL generator of [[def-qsm-dt-gns-detailed-balance]] with Hamiltonian $H_{\rm s}$ and exactly the jumps $L_\downarrow=\sqrt a\,|1\rangle\langle0|$, $L_\uparrow=\sqrt b\,|0\rangle\langle1|$, and $L_\phi=\sqrt{\gamma_\phi/2}\,Z$. Thus the additional dephasing dissipator, on either states or observables, is $D_\phi(A)=(\gamma_\phi/2)(ZAZ-A)$; when $\gamma_\phi=0$ this jump is zero. Let $\gamma_1=a+b$, $\gamma_2=(a+b)/2+\gamma_\phi$, $\omega=\Delta/\hbar$, and $z_{\rm eq}=-\tanh(\beta\Delta/2)$. Set $\sigma=(I+z_{\rm eq}Z)/2$. Define the centered correlations

$$C_{XX}(t):=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma e^{tG}(X)X),\qquad C_{ZZ}(t):=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma e^{tG}(Z-z_{\rm eq}I)(Z-z_{\rm eq}I)).$$

Then

$$C_{XX}(t)=e^{-\gamma_2t}\left(\cos(\omega t)-i\tanh(\beta\Delta/2)\sin(\omega t)\right),\qquad C_{ZZ}(t)=(1-z_{\rm eq}^2)e^{-\gamma_1t}.$$

The real correlation-integral coefficients are

$$\Gamma_X=\frac{\gamma_2}{\gamma_2^2+\omega^2},\qquad \Gamma_Z=\frac{1-z_{\rm eq}^2}{\gamma_1}.$$

Under the fixed-dissipator perturbation $H_\epsilon(t)=H_{\rm s}-\epsilon h(t)X$, define $\chi_{\rm open}(0):=\int_0^\infty R_{XX}(t)\,dt$. The open response kernel and its zero-frequency integral are

$$R_{XX}(t)=\frac{2}{\hbar}\tanh(\beta\Delta/2)e^{-\gamma_2t}\sin(\omega t),\qquad \chi_{\rm open}(0)=\frac{2\tanh(\beta\Delta/2)\,\omega}{\hbar(\gamma_2^2+\omega^2)}.$$

For $q\in\mathbb R$ measured in joules, define $H(q):=H_{\rm s}-qX$ and $\sigma_q:=e^{-\beta H(q)}/\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H(q)})$. The static Gibbs susceptibility for this family is

$$\chi_{\rm Gibbs}(0):=\left.\frac{d}{dq}\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_qX)\right|_{q=0}=\frac{2}{\hbar\omega}\tanh(\beta\Delta/2).$$

Thus $\chi_{\rm open}(0)$ and $\chi_{\rm Gibbs}(0)$ differ for positive $\gamma_2$; the model has a fixed dissipator, so its zero-frequency response is not the derivative of the instantaneous Gibbs preparation.

items.title: Exact centered qubit-record displacement variance

references.title: David Aldous and James Allen Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, Chapters 2–3
M. B. Plenio and P. L. Knight, The quantum-jump approach to dissipative dynamics in quantum optics, §IV.1 “Quantum jumps” and §IV.3 “Simulation of single trajectories”

items.statement:
Assume full AC and initialize the selected energy-resolved record with the Gibbs law $\pi$. Use the two energy states $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$ of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]] with energies $E_0=\Delta/2$ and $E_1=-\Delta/2$, where $\Delta>0$ is in joules and $\beta>0$ is in joules$^{-1}$. Let $a>0$ be the rate from $0\to1$ and $b>0$ the rate from $1\to0$, both in seconds$^{-1}$, with $b/a=e^{-\beta\Delta}$. The stationary mean is $z_{\rm eq}:=(b-a)/(a+b)$. Write $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ and let $v_0$ be a speed scale in metres per second; assign centered pointer velocities $v_a=v_0(Z_{aa}-z_{\rm eq})$. The monitored record displacement $Y_T=\int_0^T v_{a(s)}ds$ has

$$C_v(s)=v_0^2(1-z_{\rm eq}^2)e^{-(a+b)s},$$

and exact variance

$$\operatorname{Var}(Y_T)=2v_0^2(1-z_{\rm eq}^2)\left[\frac{T}{a+b}-\frac{1-e^{-(a+b)T}}{(a+b)^2}\right].$$

Consequently

$$\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{Var}(Y_T)}{2T}=\frac{v_0^2(1-z_{\rm eq}^2)}{a+b}.$$

This is a variance of the selected classical record with units of squared metres. The record is not asserted to be a continuous quantum position or an experimental velocity.
